records.title: Director, Quality
records.description:
At Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company (EBAD), we believe that our strengths are built on our most important resource - our people. Join EBAD and you'll be a part of a team who creates cutting edge technology that will blast us into the future. No other company can match the innovative energetic solutions that we provide. At EBAD you will actively contribute to successful missions putting men, women and satellites into space, and protecting our armed service men and women around the world. If this is the culture and work environment you are seeking, then EBAD is the place for you!
 
 
**Job Description**
**Location:**
Simsbury, CT
 
 
**Reports to:**
VP of Operations
 
 
**Industry:**
Aerospace & Defense
 
 
**Experience Level:**
Director (15+ years)
 
 
**Shape the Future. Deliver Excellence. Achieve Zero Failure.**
At
**Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense (EBAD),**
we’ve been innovating for nearly
**200 years,**
delivering mission-critical technologies that protect lives and advance exploration. As we prepare to double in size over the next 3–5 years, we’re investing in our people and culture to support this transformation.
 
 
We’re seeking a dynamic
**Director of Quality**
to lead a complex, multi-site quality organization and drive performance at scale. Based at our headquarters in Simsbury, Connecticut, this role is critical to ensure the highest levels of product integrity, compliance, and customer trust across a rapidly growing business. This is not just about maintaining standards but about building a future-state vision for quality that enables growth, safeguards mission success, and strengthens EBAD’s reputation as a trusted partner.
 
 
**The Opportunity:**
EBAD’s customers depend on us to deliver our products with zero failure in mission-critical environments. The Director of Quality will be responsible for developing and executing a strategic Quality Management System (QMS) while leading quality operations across multiple sites. This leader will be tasked with driving measurable quality improvement, while also championing a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
 
 
This is an exciting opportunity for a leader to make an immediate impact by providing direction, driving the strategy for the business, and developing a problem-solving culture.
 
 
**Core Competencies for Success:**

* Quality & Compliance Leadership: Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability industries, with expertise in zero-failure mission environments.
* Continuous Improvement & Performance: Skilled in EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices with the ability to drive metrics-based improvement and systemic problem-solving.
* Team Development & Leadership: Demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and build strong teams while fostering engagement and accountability.
* Collaboration & Influence: Strong cross-functional partnership with credibility to influence senior leadership, customers, and suppliers.
* Resilience & Adaptability: Able to manage ambiguity, drive change, and motivate teams in a fast-scaling environment.

**The Candidate We Are Looking For:**

* BS in an engineering discipline (MS preferred)
* Minimum 10 years of experience in high-mix, low-volume operations and manufacturing environment
* Proven success leading complex, multi-site quality organizations in aerospace, defense, or other mission-critical industries
* Demonstrated expertise in leading audits and managing compliance across regulatory bodies, customers, and suppliers, with deep knowledge of standards such as AS9100, ISO9001, and DoD requirements
* Proven ability to enhance customer quality by partnering closely with engineering, operations, and supply chain teams to consistently meet customer demand
* Strong record of measurable quality improvements
* Skilled in continuous improvement, performance metrics, and problem-solving through EBOS, Lean, and Kaizen practices
* Track record of building and developing strong teams, fostering high engagement, and driving accountability

**A Defining Leadership Opportunity:**

* Legacy: Join a privately held, 188-year-old business that takes a long-term approach, free from the short-term pressures of quarterly-driven reporting.
* Impact: Lead a mission-critical function where zero failure is the standard and success is business-defining.
* Partnership: Work directly with the BU President, senior leadership, and enterprise HR leaders in a highly influential role at the intersection of people and business strategy.
* Culture of Excellence: Help shape a culture that values people, integrity, and mission-driven excellence, driven by a Kaizen mindset and a commitment to quality and continuous improvement.

**Ready to Make a Difference?**
If you’re a proven quality engineering leader with the vision, discipline, and drive to achieve zero failure in a complex and growing business, this is your opportunity.
 
 
**Compensation and Rewards:**
We recognize that world-class leaders deliver world-class impact, and we reward accordingly. This role offers a competitive executive package that includes:
 
 
**Base Salary:**
$175k – $225k plus annual bonus
 
 
**Executive Relocation:**
Comprehensive support for a seamless transition
 
 
**Additional Enhancements:**
Potential sign-on incentives and tailored rewards based on experience
 
 
*We offer a competitive compensation package aligned with skills & experience, with flexibility to reward top talent and extraordinary qualifications.*
*Ensign-Bickford Aerospace & Defense Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, age, disability, sexual orientation, genetic information, national origin, or veteran status.*

records.title: Director of Quality Assurance
records.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies’ core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.
 
 
The Director of Quality, Defense is responsible for overseeing all quality activities, personnel, systems, and performance associated with Defense programs across multiple Karman Space & Defense operating sites. This role provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure all Defense hardware, assemblies, and services meet or exceed contractual, regulatory, and customer requirements.
 
 
This position will manage the Defense Quality Engineering organization, supports execution of Defense programs, and ensures consistent application of quality standards and tools across the sector. This leader works in close partnership with the Enterprise Director of Quality to align each site’s AS9100 compliant QMS with the emerging enterprise quality architecture and to transition multiple Defense sites toward a unified enterprise certification.
 
 
This role is critical in driving disciplined execution, continuous improvement, product integrity, and customer satisfaction within the Defense market segment.
 
 
Reports to Vice President, Defense. Functional Partnership with Enterprise Director of Quality (Karman Space & Defense).
 
 
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Lead, develop, and manage the Quality Engineering team supporting all Defense programs and projects.
* Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, proactive risk management, and continuous improvement across Defense Quality functions.
* Serve as the primary Defense quality leader to the VP of Defense and the Defense leadership team.
* Ensure the quality of all Defense hardware, assemblies, engineered systems, and services produced across multiple sites.
* Oversee program quality planning, including inspection strategies, qualification/verification plans, critical characteristics control, product safety considerations, and risk mitigation.
* Review and approve quality requirements for Defense proposals, contracts, and manufacturing plans.
* Drive effective root cause analysis, corrective action, and failure review processes for Defense programs.
* Ensure each Defense site maintains compliance to AS9100, customer requirements, and regulatory obligations.
* Provide direct guidance to site Quality Managers/Quality Engineers on QMS implementation, audit readiness, and procedural improvement.
* Support site internal audits, customer audits, DCMA oversight, and third‑party certification audits.
* Partner with the Enterprise Director of Quality to align Defense site QMS structures, documentation, and practices with the enterprise quality framework.
* Support the long-term strategy to transition multiple Defense AS9100 certificates into a unified enterprise certificate.
* Collaborate closely on enterprise initiatives such as configuration management improvements, risk management systems, document control harmonization, supplier quality strategies, and enterprise metrics.

**Education And Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or related technical field preferred
* 10 years of experience in aerospace/defense quality roles preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100, ISO 9001, and Defense customer quality standards.
* Quality Engineering experience with complex programs including design.

**Itar Requirements**
To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, certain positions may require applicants to be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C.
 
 

* 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C.
* 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

**Travel Requirements**
Occasional travel 0-10% of the time.
 
 
Salary Range
 
 
$140,000 - $180,000 USD
 
 
Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
 
 
View our Privacy Policy

records.title: Plant Director
records.description:
**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!**
Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you'll lead great people, drive meaningful impact, and help shape the future of our business while supporting the bakery and restaurant teams behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests enjoy every day. That's the kind of culture that has earned us a place on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For® list every year since 2014.

**The Plant Director**
provides strategic and operational leadership for a three-shift, seven-day manufacturing facility encompassing approximately 160 full-time, non-union employees. Leading all aspects of production and packaging operations, you will drive performance, efficiency, quality, and continuous improvement across scheduling, logistics, pre-scaling, mixing, depositing, baking, decorating, and packaging to support the Bakery's operational and business objectives.

They utilize excellent leadership, analytical, management, and technical skills, abilities, and behaviors to drive performance in key areas such as people, safety, quality, service, and cost, aligned with measurable objectives and the Company’s Mission, Vision, and Values. The Director also assists with business continuity in the absence of the VP of Operations.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **Service oriented:**
 you are a people person who is systematic and trustworthy and interacts constructively with peers or teams of various levels demonstrating strong, positive communication skills.
* **Driven by results:**
 you are conscientious and persistent about delivering timely, high-quality deliverables, and performing all job functions safely while following instructions.
* **Improvement focused:**
 you never turn off the thought “how can I do this better/faster”.
* **Pressure resistant:**
 you have ice in your veins while under pressure. Maintaining a positive outlook at work while the heat is on is never an issue for you.

**Here’s more of what you’ll get to do:**

* Maintain positive employee relations through respectful, open, and effective two-way communication at the individual and team levels.
* Partner with human resources and training departments to develop, implement, and maintain effective training and development programs that support performance goals and provide a satisfying work environment.
* Maintain a fair and professional work environment that balances business objectives with quality-of-work-life factors for employees.
* Work with Human Resources to ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and company policies, while driving improvements in employee performance as measured by turnover rate, attendance, and feedback mechanisms.
* Oversee production planning and scheduling to optimize service and efficiency, balancing resources such as crewing, materials, and equipment with other department managers.
* Supervise the development of synchronized crewing, equipment setup, and materials preparation plans to ensure schedule attainment and optimize capacity utilization.
* Manage timekeeping, labor efficiency, and plant productivity in compliance with legal and company policies, aiming to minimize overtime and control non-productive line time.
* Collaborate with the Plant Engineer to ensure preventive and emergency maintenance efforts are effective, minimizing downtime and optimizing machine performance.
* Manage material usage to ensure minimal waste and maximum yield, while maintaining strict adherence to product quality standards and inventory management.
* Monitor spending and manage operations within approved budget levels, while driving improvements in cost performance through labor productivity, waste reduction, and yield maximization.
* Ensure disciplined compliance with product and process quality standards, food safety, and regulatory requirements, striving for “EXCELLENT” or “SUPERIOR” scores in third-party audits.
* Lead plant safety efforts, including co-chairing the Safety Steering Committee, safety inspections, and training, while driving improvements in safety performance as measured by injury frequency and workers' compensation data.
* Participate in business plan development, budgeting processes, and plant-level meetings to ensure effective communication and alignment with operational goals.
* Ability to transform the facility into a CI culture driven by people, process and equipment/technology.
* Ensure the utilization of 4-step process to drive result in sustainability which are Huddles, Daily meeting, utilization of Red Zone and Sic meetings.

**What we require:**

* Minimum of 15 years of experience in food manufacturing management, preferably in the bakery/dessert industry, with demonstrated success at the Plant Manager or Director of Manufacturing/Operations level.
* Bachelor’s degree (MBA a Plus)
* Strong experience with food safety, food process equipment, and regulations.
* Strong experience with emergency preparedness and emergency response plans and procedures.
* Familiar with regulatory and safety codes, including USDA, FDA, and OSHA regulations.
* Knowledge and demonstrated skill in lean manufacturing, Kaizen, kitting, and Six Sigma techniques.
* Prior experience with direct responsibility for a large-scale P&L.
* Strong and effective strategic management skills, including long-range planning, organizing, communicating, influencing, gathering and using information, and motivating a team to achieve results. Ability to use, and teach others to use, various analytical tools and techniques.
* Demonstrated mentoring skills.

**What we offer:**

* Eligible for annual bonus
* Eligible for annual equity grants
* Medical, Dental & Vision
* Eligible for benefits first day of the month following date of hire
* 401K with company match
* 3 weeks of vacation which increases to 4 weeks starting in your 5th year
* 5 days of sick time per year (first year prorated)
* Tuition Reimbursement of $2,500 for qualified programs
* Adoption Assistance Benefit of $2,500
* 25%-35% discount when dining as a guest
* Reusable gift card loaded annually for your dining enjoyment

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery creates over 35,000 delicious cheesecakes per day across our two facilities in Calabasas, CA and Rocky Mount, NC plus other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees, and third-party bakery customers.

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery is a subsidiary of The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated. Recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® since 2014, The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a global $3.8 billion public company with more than 370 casual dining restaurants and over 48,000 staff members.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming workplace for all. records.title: Director Internal Fill Finish Manufacturing
records.description:
**Build Our Future Together**
At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. Regeneron is currently looking for a Director of Internal Fill Finish Manufacturing to join our Industrial Operations and Product Supply (IOPS) team. This leadership role is accountable for the aseptic filling operation for clinical and commercial drug products, including vials and syringes in both liquid and lyophilized formats. The Director owns the full filling value stream: materials management; preparation of equipment, format parts, and components; formulation of drug product and placebo; aseptic filling; and lyophilization. The Director also ensures a seamless handoff to downstream finishing operations (Visual Inspection, syringe safety systems and autoinjector assembly, packaging, labeling, and serialization) and oversees facility cleaning and contamination control for the filling suites.
 
 
This role focuses on the start-up and execution of compliant GMP aseptic operations, ensuring the facility is properly staffed and trained, and supporting a dynamic, flexible production planning process that meets the needs of Regeneron’s patients. The Director will work directly with Drug Substance and Finish manufacturing management to ensure production timelines are met and will be a key member of various management teams within IOPS.
 
 
This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.
 
 
**When & Where**

* Location: Rensselaer, NY
* Work model: Monday- Friday, 8am-4:30pm

**Discover Your Role**

* Provides leadership, vision, and management to the Filling team and its supporting functions, and leads all aspects of Filling operations at the facility to manufacture commercial and clinical parenteral medicines according to approved protocols, regulations, and schedules
* Directly oversees aseptic filling of drug product and placebo into vials and syringes, in liquid and lyophilized formats, including stoppering, capping, and crimping
* Directly oversees formulation of bulk drug product and placebo, including solution preparation and sterile filtration
* Directly oversees preparation of equipment, format parts, and components to support aseptic filling, including washing, depyrogenation, sterilization, and setup of filling lines
* Directly oversees lyophilization operations, including loading, cycle execution, and unloading, as well as the management of materials and components required to support filling operations
* Directly oversees cleaning and sanitization of filling suites, including Graded space (Grade A–D) and Controlled Non-Classified rooms (iCNC), and supports the site contamination control strategy, environmental monitoring, and aseptic process simulations (media fills)
* Ensures a smooth, timely handoff of filled product to downstream finishing operations (Visual Inspection, assembly, packaging, and labeling) in partnership with the leaders of those areas
* Troubleshoots and resolves issues impeding filling deliverables, including equipment performance, line interventions, and yield; provides technical input to resolve filling and aseptic process challenges
* Partners with department Directors and Project Management to implement new filling processes, including new formats, PFS and vial filling lines, formulation, aseptic filling, and lyophilization
* Manages department metrics and goals, monitors performance to objectives, and drives continuous improvement initiatives essential to meeting patient and business needs
* Leads the annual merit performance review process, builds departmental structure, and develops long-term staffing plans, including aseptic gowning qualification and training programs
* Collaborates with department Directors to support development of the annual budget, and rapidly and accurately communicates issues to department Directors
* Writes, reviews, and/or approves Standard Operating Procedures, specifications, regulatory filings, or other controlled documents as needed
* Executes Quality Management System assignments (CAPA, Deviation, Investigation, Change Control, etc.)
* Participates in the development and maintenance of a safe manufacturing environment and ensures that IOPS safety standards are maintained
* Oversees, supports, and participates in cGMP audits of all filling areas within the facility; maintains site inspection readiness and represents the filling operation during regulatory and client audits

**This Role Requires**

* BS in any of the physical or biological sciences or chemical engineering, with biopharmaceutical/biotech experience in a GMP drug product production facility, including aseptic filling experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience

+ Director: 12+ years of experience
+ Senior Director: 15+ years of experience
+ Level will be determined based on experience

* Experience overseeing aseptic filling operations in a biologics manufacturing environment, including vial and prefilled syringe filling
* Working knowledge of lyophilization, formulation, and aseptic technique, including barrier and isolator/RABS technologies
* Working knowledge of contamination control, environmental monitoring, and aseptic process simulation requirements
* Experience with multiproduct biologics facility start-up is preferred
* Experience interacting with multiple health authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA)

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.
 
 
Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.
 
 
Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.
 
 
As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.
 
 
For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.
 
 
**Salary Range (annually)**
$175,700.00 - $292,700.00

records.description:
Job Type
 
 
Full-time
 
 
**Description**
**Spartronics, LLC**
**Career Opportunity: Site Director of Operations**
**Location:**
North Logan, Utah
 
 
**Employment Type:**
Full-Time | Salaried | Exempt
 
 
**Work Arrangement:**
On-Site
 
 
**Schedule:**
Full-Time, Monday–Friday
 
 
**Reports To:**
Vice President of Operations – West / Logan Site Leader
 
 
**Who We Are**
At
**Spartronics**
, we build more than electronics. We build the technology that powers critical applications across aerospace and defense, medical devices, life sciences, and industrial markets.
 
 
As a leading provider of electronic manufacturing services (EMS), Spartronics specializes in complex, high-reliability products, including printed circuit board assemblies (PCBA), electromechanical assemblies, integrated systems, and complete product manufacturing solutions.
 
 
**Career Opportunity: Director of Operations**
Spartronics is seeking an experienced
**Director of Operations**
to lead manufacturing operations and drive operational excellence at our North Logan, Utah facility.
 
 
This senior leadership position is responsible for the overall performance, execution, and continuous improvement of the site's operational functions, including
**Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Materials Planning**
, while providing indirect operational oversight and cross-functional partnership with Program Management.
 
 
Reporting to the Vice President of Operations – West / Logan Site Leader, the Director of Operations will establish operational priorities, develop high-performing teams, optimize manufacturing processes, and ensure the organization consistently achieves its safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and profitability objectives.
 
 
The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader with strong business acumen, experience managing multiple operational disciplines, and a proven ability to drive results in complex, highly regulated manufacturing environments.
 
 
**What You Will Do**

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for the facility, translating organizational objectives into actionable plans, performance expectations, and measurable results.
* Direct Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Materials Planning functions, ensuring effective coordination, accountability, and alignment with site and corporate objectives.
* Provide indirect operational oversight and strategic partnership to Program Management, ensuring alignment between customer requirements, program execution, operational capacity and business objectives.
* Direct manufacturing operations, production planning, capacity management, and resource allocation, balancing changing customer demand, product complexity, and manufacturing constraints to achieve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity objectives.
* Establish operational priorities, evaluate performance against key metrics, and implement corrective actions to address performance gaps and emerging risks.
* Provide leadership and oversight of engineering activities, including process optimization, technical problem resolution, manufacturing readiness, new product introduction, and product transfers.
* Ensure the effectiveness of quality management systems, regulatory compliance, product conformity, and corrective and preventive action processes while preserving Quality's independent authority over product acceptance and compliance decisions.
* Oversee supply chain and materials planning activities, including procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, material availability, and production support.
* Partner with Program Management and other customer-facing functions to address delivery commitments, operational concerns, customer escalations, and changing business requirements.
* Develop operational budgets, resource plans, capital expenditure priorities, and cost improvement initiatives in collaboration with Finance, supporting achievement of site financial objectives and profitability targets..
* Evaluate operational and financial performance, identifying opportunities to improve profitability, reduce waste, control costs, and optimize resource utilization.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives utilizing Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, root cause analysis, and other structured problem-solving methodologies.
* Ensure manufacturing processes, product traceability, configuration and change control, and supporting documentation comply with applicable customer, industry, regulatory, and company requirements.
* Promote a strong safety culture and ensure operational compliance with applicable environmental, health, and safety requirements.
* Establish and maintain structured operational performance management systems, including KPI reviews, cross-functional accountability, issue escalation, and corrective action follow-through to support timely, data-driven decision-making.
* Build, coach, and develop operational leadership teams, establishing clear performance expectations, succession plans, and workforce competency and development priorities.
* Collaborate with Human Resources on workforce planning, staffing requirements, employee performance, organizational development, and retention strategies.
* Coordinate with Facilities, Security, and other support functions to address infrastructure needs, operational continuity, physical security requirements, and business risks.
* Evaluate manufacturing capacity, technology, equipment, and infrastructure needs to support business growth, operational scalability, and capital investment decisions.
* Identify and mitigate operational risks associated with production disruptions, supplier constraints, quality concerns, regulatory requirements, and customer commitments.
* Represent site operations in corporate leadership discussions, customer interactions, audits, and strategic planning activities, communicating performance, priorities, and resource requirements.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support organizational objectives.

**Requirements**
**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline; an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing operations, including at least five years in a senior leadership capacity overseeing multiple operational functions.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations with accountability for production, engineering, quality, supply chain, and cross-functional business objectives.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, production planning, capacity management, materials management, and operational performance improvement.
* Demonstrated knowledge of manufacturing engineering principles, process controls, technical problem resolution, and new product introduction activities.
* Working knowledge of quality management systems, regulatory compliance, product conformity, corrective action processes, and applicable manufacturing standards.
* Proven ability to develop and execute operational strategies, establish performance objectives, and achieve measurable improvements in quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience utilizing financial metrics, cost management practices, capital planning processes, and profitability analysis to drive operational decision-making.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, and hold accountable cross-functional management teams while promoting collaboration and organizational effectiveness.
* Experience applying Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and structured problem-solving methodologies to complex operational challenges.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and decision-making skills, with the ability to evaluate competing priorities, manage operational risks, and resolve complex business issues.
* Advanced proficiency with business and manufacturing information systems, including ERP/MRP platforms, Microsoft Office applications, and data analysis and reporting tools. Demonstrated ability to interpret operational and financial data, evaluate performance trends, and leverage technology to support strategic planning and informed decision-making.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with employees, senior leadership, customers, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to manage sensitive business information, exercise sound judgment, and maintain confidentiality in accordance with company and applicable security requirements.
* Ability to read, write, speak, and comprehend English sufficiently to interpret technical documentation, communicate operational requirements, and perform essential job responsibilities.
* Ability to work full-time on-site at the assigned company facility in Logan, UT.

**Security Clearance Requirement**
Candidates must possess current, verifiable eligibility for a U.S. Government Secret-level security clearance or be willing and able to complete the necessary documentation to initiate the company-sponsored clearance process within 60 days of hire. The ability to obtain and maintain the required security clearance eligibility is a continuing condition of employment. Employment may continue while an appropriately initiated clearance application is pending, subject to company authorization and applicable security restrictions. A final determination of ineligibility, denial, or loss of required clearance eligibility will result in disqualification from the position and may result in termination of employment, subject to applicable law and company policy.
 
 
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Leadership experience within electronics manufacturing services (EMS), printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), or high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environments.
* Experience with surface mount technology (SMT), through-hole assembly, electromechanical assembly, manufacturing test, and related electronics manufacturing processes.
* Experience supporting aerospace, defense, medical device, or other highly regulated manufacturing industries.
* Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, applicable IPC standards, and customer-specific quality requirements.
* Knowledge of ITAR, controlled technical information, and security requirements applicable to defense-related manufacturing.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or other recognized continuous improvement credentials.
* APICS/ASCM certification, such as CPIM or CSCP, or equivalent supply chain management credentials.
* Experience leading operational transformations, facility expansions, production transfers, or significant manufacturing improvement initiatives.
* Experience utilizing business intelligence platforms, advanced reporting tools, and integrated manufacturing systems to monitor operational performance and support continuous improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated success managing complex customer relationships, operational escalations, and cross-functional business challenges.

**Key Metrics and Focus Areas**

* Workplace safety performance and regulatory compliance.
* On-time delivery performance and production schedule attainment.
* Manufacturing efficiency, throughput, and capacity utilization.
* Product quality, first-pass yield, and cost of poor quality.
* Inventory accuracy, material availability, and inventory turns.
* Supplier delivery, quality, and overall performance.
* Operating cost performance, budget adherence, and profitability.
* Engineering responsiveness, manufacturing readiness, and successful new product introductions.
* Program execution support and fulfillment of customer commitments.
* Continuous improvement results, waste reduction, and operational efficiency.
* Quality management system effectiveness, audit performance, and corrective action closure.
* Workforce productivity, employee development, retention, and leadership effectiveness.
* Operational risk management, business continuity, and capacity readiness.

**Why This Role Matters**
As
**Director of Operations,**
you will play a critical role in shaping the performance, operational capabilities, and continued growth of our North Logan manufacturing facility. Your leadership will directly influence how effectively we deliver complex, high-reliability electronic products to customers operating in some of the world's most demanding industries. This is an opportunity to lead talented teams, strengthen operational performance, implement meaningful improvements, and contribute to the long-term success of a growing manufacturing organization.
 
 
**Benefits – Why Join Spartronics?**
At Spartronics, we recognize that our employees are essential to our success. We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, financial well-being, and professional development of our team members.
 
 
**Benefits May Include**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
* 401(k) retirement savings plan.
* Paid time off and company-paid holidays.
* Company-paid life insurance and disability benefits.
* Employee assistance and wellness resources.
* Professional development and career growth opportunities.
* Opportunities to contribute to innovative products supporting mission-critical industries.

*Specific benefits and eligibility are subject to applicable plan documents and company policies.*
**Physical Requirements and Work Location**

* Ability to work in both office and manufacturing environments, including regular movement throughout production, warehouse, and operational areas.
* Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods, with occasional bending and reaching.
* Ability to occasionally lift, carry, or move materials weighing up to 25 pounds.
* Ability to operate computers and standard office equipment.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment when entering designated manufacturing areas.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Work Authorization & ITAR Requirements**
Due to the nature of certain products, technologies, and customer requirements, this position may involve access to export-controlled technical data or defense-related information subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and other applicable export control laws. Candidates must meet applicable U.S. export control authorization requirements and be eligible to access controlled technical information as required by the position. For this position, additional U.S. Government security clearance eligibility requirements apply, as described above.
 
 
**Equal Employment Opportunity**
*Spartronics is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Veteran/Disabled 41 CFR 60-1.4. We comply with federal Affirmative Action guidelines in all employment opportunities for qualified employees and applicants.Employment at Spartronics is considered at-will, meaning that either the employee or Spartronics may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause, and with or without prior notification.*

records.description:
**Director of Operations & Production**

**Location:**
Redwood City, CA

**Schedule:**
Full-time, onsite

**Industry:**
Precision Manufacturing

**About the Company**

An established precision component solutions provider with a significant manufacturing operation in Redwood City is seeking a Director of Operations & Production. The company serves leading customers across the medical, aerospace, and electronics industries and operates within an ISO 9001/AS9100-certified quality management environment.

The organization is committed to delivering high-quality products, strong customer service, and operational excellence. They believe successful business outcomes begin with strong employees, clear processes, and a culture of accountability.

**About the Role**

The Director of Operations & Production will oversee day-to-day operations and help drive efficiency, productivity, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the business. This person will manage and support multiple departments, including purchasing, shipping, customer service, production planning, inventory, and operational processes.

The ideal candidate will have a strong manufacturing operations background, sharp business judgment, and experience managing cross-functional teams in a time-sensitive production environment. records.description:
**Job Description**
The Director of Indium Phosphide (InP) Wafer Fab Operations is responsible for the overall leadership, startup, qualification, and operation of an Indium Phosphide wafer fabrication facility. This executive leadership role will oversee all aspects of manufacturing operations, including technology transfer, process qualification, production ramp, operational readiness, quality, engineering collaboration, workforce development, and continuous improvement.
 
 
Working closely with Engineering, Process Development, Supply Chain, Quality, Facilities, Product Management, and Executive Leadership, the Director will establish and scale world-class manufacturing capabilities while achieving exceptional performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, yield, and customer satisfaction. This role requires a strategic leader with deep semiconductor wafer fabrication experience and a proven track record of successfully launching and operating advanced manufacturing facilities.
 
 
**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic and operational leadership for all wafer fabrication activities, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality manufacturing operations.
* Lead the startup, commissioning, qualification, and operational readiness of a new Indium Phosphide wafer fabrication facility.
* Develop and execute the manufacturing roadmap to support business growth, customer commitments, and capacity expansion.
* Establish operational metrics, production targets, and performance objectives aligned with corporate goals.

**Production Ramp & Operational Excellence**
 
 

* Lead production ramp activities from development through high-volume manufacturing.
* Drive improvements in cycle time, throughput, equipment utilization, overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), yield, and cost of ownership.
* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Statistical Process Control (SPC), and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Monitor key manufacturing KPIs and implement corrective actions to ensure operational excellence.
* Quality & Compliance
* Foster a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with ISO standards, customer requirements, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
* Lead root cause investigations and corrective/preventive action (CAPA) activities.
* Maintain world-class product quality and manufacturing consistency.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration
* Partner with Supply Chain to ensure material availability and production continuity.
* Collaborate with Facilities to maintain reliable manufacturing infrastructure and utilities.
* Work closely with Product Management, Sales, and Customer Quality to meet customer delivery expectations.
* Provide regular operational updates to executive leadership regarding production performance, risks, and strategic initiatives.

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
* Master’s degree in engineering preferred, Business Administration (MBA), or related discipline.
* Minimum of 15 years of progressive leadership experience in semiconductor wafer fabrication or advanced manufacturing.
* Minimum of 8 years leading manufacturing operations, fab management, or operations engineering organizations.
* Demonstrated experience leading semiconductor fab startup, production ramp, or significant capacity expansion initiatives.
* Experience with compound semiconductor manufacturing, preferably Indium Phosphide (InP), Gallium Arsenide (GaAs), Silicon Photonics, or III-V semiconductor technologies.
* Proven experience managing cross-functional organizations and large manufacturing teams.

**Skills**
**Technical Competencies**

* Deep understanding of semiconductor wafer fabrication processes, equipment, and manufacturing systems.
* Knowledge of lithography, etch, deposition, diffusion, implant, CMP, metrology, wafer testing, and process integration.
* Experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), ERP systems, and factory automation.
* Strong knowledge of statistical process control (SPC), Design of Experiments (DOE), Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), and yield improvement methodologies.

**Leadership Skills**
 
 

* Proven ability to lead through organizational growth, change, and transformation.
* Exceptional strategic planning and execution capabilities.
* Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills.

**Communication & Collaboration**
 
 

* Excellent coaching, mentoring, and talent development abilities.
* Ability to influence across all organizational levels, including executive leadership.
* Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
* Ability to communicate complex technical and operational information to executive leadership.
* Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build effective cross-functional partnerships.
* Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary teams in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

**Working Conditions**

* This role will be based on-site in Fremont, CA.
* Regular use of a computer and other office equipment is necessary.

**Physical Requirements**

* Occasional travel to other sites may be necessary.
* Sitting for extended periods while working on a computer or in meetings.
* Use of hands and fingers for typing, writing, and handling documents.
* Occasional lifting of objects or materials up to 20 pounds for administrative tasks.
* Ability to communicate verbally and in writing.

**Safety Requirements**
All employees are required to follow the site EHS procedures and Coherent Corp. Corporate EHS standards.
 
 
**Quality And Environmental Responsibilities**
Depending on location, this position may be responsible for the execution and maintenance of the ISO 9000, 9001, 14001 and/or other applicable standards that may apply to the relevant roles and responsibilities within the Quality Management System and Environmental Management System.
 
 
**Culture Commitment**
Ensure adherence to company’s values (ICARE) in all aspects of your position at Coherent Corp.:
 
 
**I**
ntegrity – Create an Environment of Trust
 
 
**C**
ollaboration – Innovate Through the Sharing of Ideas
 
 
**A**
ccountability – Own the Process and the Outcome
 
 
**R**
espect – Recognize the Value in Everyone
 
 
**E**
nthusiasm – Find a Sense of Purpose in Work
 
 
*Coherent Corp. is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.*
*If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at*
*talentacquisition@coherent.com*
*.*
**About Us**
Coherent is a global leader in lasers, engineered materials and networking components. We are a vertically integrated manufacturing company that develops innovative products for diversified applications in the industrial, optical communications, military, life sciences, semiconductor equipment, and consumer markets. Coherent provides a comprehensive career development platform within an environment that challenges employees to perform at their best, while rewarding excellence and hard-work through a competitive compensation program. It's an exciting opportunity to work for a company that offers stability, longevity and growth. Come Join Us!
 
 
**Note to recruiters and employment agencies:**
We will not pay for unsolicited resumes from recruiters and employment agencies unless we have a signed agreement and have required assistance, in writing, for a specific opening.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
At East Trailers, we’re looking for a hands-on
**Director of Operations**
who builds strong teams and translates business priorities into safe, reliable and efficient manufacturing performance. Reporting to the CEO, you’ll lead Production, Manufacturing Engineering and Maintenance, driving daily execution and lasting operational improvements.

**What you’ll do**

* Lead manufacturing operations to meet safety, quality, delivery, productivity and cost commitments.
* Establish disciplined daily management, clear priorities and visible performance metrics across production teams.
* Align production schedules, capacity and staffing with customer demand, adapting effectively to changing volumes.
* Drive continuous improvement through standardized work, root-cause problem solving and effective corrective actions.
* Own manufacturing budget execution, improving labor efficiency and managing overtime and operating costs.
* Strengthen preventive maintenance, equipment reliability and facility readiness to support consistent production.

**What we’re looking for**

* A visible, hands-on leader who builds credibility on the shop floor and holds teams accountable.
* A strong commitment to safety, quality and disciplined execution.
* An analytical approach and the ability to turn performance data into clear actions.
* Sound judgment and timely decision-making in a dynamic manufacturing environment.
* Clear communication and effective collaboration across functions.
* The ability to develop leaders, strengthen team capabilities and sustain operational improvements.

**Experience and qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Industrial Technology, Operations Management or a related field; an MBA or advanced degree is preferred.
* 8+ years of progressive leadership experience in complex manufacturing environments.
* Proven experience leading cross-functional operations teams across production, manufacturing engineering and maintenance.
* Demonstrated results improving safety, operational stability, productivity and cost performance.
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, production planning, capacity management and structured problem solving.
* Working knowledge of OSHA requirements and manufacturing safety standards.
* Experience leading in a unionized manufacturing environment is highly preferred.
* Ability to work on-site at our Randolph, Ohio manufacturing facility.

records.title: Operations Director, CAR-T Manufacturing
records.description:
At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com
 
 
As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.
 
 
**Job Function**
Supply Chain Manufacturing
 
 
**Job Sub Function**
Plant Management
 
 
**Job Category**
People Leader
 
 
**All Job Posting Locations:**
Raritan, New Jersey, United States of America
 
 
**Job Description**
**About Innovative Medicine**
Our expertise in Innovative Medicine is informed and inspired by patients, whose insights fuel our science-based advancements. Visionaries like you work on teams that save lives by developing the medicines of tomorrow. Join us in developing treatments, finding cures, and pioneering the path from lab to life while championing patients every step of the way.
 
 
**Learn more at**
**https://www.jnj.com/innovative-medicine**
We are searching for the best talent for an
**Operations Director, CAR-T Manufacturing**
to join our team in Raritan, NJ.
 
 
Are you interested in joining a team that is positively impacting patients' lives by ensuring reliable delivery of our high quality Innovative Medicine products? Apply today for this exciting opportunity to be part of the #CAR-T team!
 
 
**Summary**
The CAR-T Operations Director is a member of the Raritan CAR-T site leadership team and plays a crucial role in leading the overall operations of the 24/7 manufacturing facility. Working closely with the Site General Manager, you will contribute to the efficient and effective functioning of the manufacturing site by ensuring compliance to cGMP practices while overseeing various aspects of production, personnel, and resource management. The position will lead a team of 6-8 direct reports and a broader organization of approximately 200 shift-based personnel.
 
 
The candidate must be comfortable to working in a matrixed environment, both within Johnson & Johnson and with our collaboration partner, Legend Biotech.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide leadership to Operations Execution and Operations Support organizations, including operators, team leaders, supervisors, investigators and trainers, fostering a positive work environment that empowers employees and promotes high-performance teams.
* Provide leadership to drive effective communication and collaboration across all relevant groups to ensure robust production, testing and release of product to patients.
* Implement KPIs and monitor production processes to ensure efficiency, quality, and adherence to production schedules.
* Drive organizational transformation, operations ramp-up and facility approvals of state-of-the-art cell therapy manufacturing facilities
* Maintain high standards of quality, compliance and safety through leadership by example.
* Build a strategy to develop existing talent through broadening experiences and commitment to delivery to the highest standards. Continue to build bench strength in the operations organization and ensure robust succession planning
* Lead operational planning to manage capacity evolution and technology integration for clinical and commercial manufacturing.
* Drive high-quality and efficiency in management of non-conformances.
* Identify and contribute to the development and execution of initiatives that drive root cause identification, continuous improvement, cost reduction, and increased productivity throughout the manufacturing plant.
* Collaborate with the EHS and Quality teams to maintain high standards of compliance, product quality and workplace safety. Foster a culture of safety, compliance, and accountability across the manufacturing plant.
* Provide representation and leadership in regulatory inspections.

**Qualifications**
**Education:**

* A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree is required, preferably with a focus in Science or Engineering. Master’s or higher degree is preferred.

**Required**
**Experience and Skills:**

* Minimum 10 years of combined experience in cGMP manufacturing, operations management, technical transfer, process and equipment validation, quality management or related area is required
* Experience working in a sterile biological/pharmaceutical/cell therapy manufacturing environment is required
* Proven understanding of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP’s) is required
* Strong people leadership including leading direct reports is required
* Relationship/influencing savvy required
* Communicates effectively with people at all levels, including the ability to understand their priorities, and to earn their respect and trust, along with the willingness to provide them with the best decisions in time-sensitive situations required
* Capable of dealing with ambiguity, working and leading in a matrix environment required
* Capable of thriving in a fast-paced growth situation, with ability to adapt to changing environment required
* Ability to balance day to day operational demands with the need to extend and improve the planning horizon to prepare strategically to manage future demands required
* Ability to flex schedule to maintain off-hour communication and connection with 2nd shift employees as needed

**Preferred**

* Lean and Six Sigma Certification

**Other**

* This position is located in Raritan New Jersey and may require up to 10% domestic and international travel.

For more information on how we support the whole health of our employees throughout their wellness, career and life journey, please visit www.careers.jnj.com.
 
 
*If you are under 18 years of age, you (the candidate) may need to obtain the necessary working papers or other documentation required by state law to start the assignment, as well as get a parent’s consent for the background check.*
*Johnson & Johnson is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local law. We actively seek qualified candidates who are protected veterans and individuals with disabilities as defined under VEVRAA and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act.*
*Johnson & Johnson is committed to providing an interview process that is inclusive of our applicants’ needs. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request an accommodation, external applicants please contact us via*
*https://www.jnj.com/contact-us/careers*
*, internal employees contact AskGS to be directed to your accommodation resource.*
**Required Skills**
**Preferred Skills:**
Agile Manufacturing, Business Planning, Developing Others, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Inclusive Leadership, Leadership, Manufacturing Compliance, Manufacturing Safety, Organizational Project Management, Organizing, Plant Operations, Process Improvements, Strategic Supply Chain Management, Tactical Planning
 
 
**The anticipated base pay range for this position is :**
$154,000.00 - $265,650.00
 
 
**Additional Description For Pay Transparency**
Subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees are eligible to participate in the Company’s consolidated retirement plan (pension) and savings plan (401(k)).
 
 
This position is eligible to participate in the Company’s long-term incentive program.
 
 
**Benefits**

records.title: Senior Director Manufacturing
records.description:
Founded over 35 years ago, First Quality is a family-owned company that has grown from a small business in McElhattan, Pennsylvania into a group of companies, employing over 5,000 team members, while maintaining our family values and entrepreneurial spirit. With corporate offices in New York and Pennsylvania and 8 manufacturing campuses across the U.S. and Canada, the companies within the First Quality group produce high-quality personal care and household products for large retailers and healthcare organizations. Our personal care and household product portfolio includes baby diapers, wipes, feminine pads, paper towels, bath tissue, adult incontinence products, laundry detergents, fabric finishers, and dishwash solutions. In addition, we manufacture certain raw materials and components used in the manufacturing of these products, including flexible print and packaging solutions.

Guided by our values of humility, unity, and integrity, we leverage advanced technology and innovation to drive growth and create new opportunities. At First Quality, you’ll find a collaborative environment focused on continuous learning, professional development, and our mission to Make Things Better®.

We are seeking a
**Senior Director, Manufacturing Operations**
for our
**First Quality Baby Products, LLC**
location in
**Macon, GA.**
This position will have operational oversight for the Macon, GA production facility and will be responsible for strategic manufacturing operations leadership for the site. The role will collaborate with Division and site leadership to drive the long-range strategic planning process, including production planning, scheduling, and resource allocation. The role will collaborate with the key business unit partners to drive actions that have a favorable impact on the P&L while focusing on long-term growth. Additionally, the role is responsible for driving a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

**Primary responsibilities include:**

* Foster a culture of health, safety, and quality.
* Develop, implement, and monitor day-to-day operational systems and processes to provide visibility into the goals, progress, and obstacles of key initiatives.
* Manage and mentor staff, fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
* Drive continuous improvement of manufacturing processes and management methods to generate improved plant performance, workflow optimization, yields and efficiencies, and budget commitments.
* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies that align with the company’s overall goals and objectives.
* Implement and enforce quality control processes to ensure products meet or exceed customer expectations.
* Monitor production processes to ensure efficiency, productivity, and profitability targets are consistently met or exceeded.
* Identify areas for process improvement and implement strategies to optimize production workflows and reduce costs.
* Work closely with cross-functional teams to ensure seamless coordination and communication throughout the manufacturing process.
* Direct, inspire and hold leaders accountable to ensure engagement of all functional areas to drive business performance and deliver results.
* Ensure adherence to state and federal regulations regarding all business components.
* Manage operations in support of business growth by ensuring the introduction of new equipment and systems meet safety, quality, cost, consumer, customer, and security requirements.
* Drive recruiting, training and retention efforts in collaboration with Human Resources to ensure training, employee development, and work systems enable all employees to maximize their contribution to business success.
* Consult with and support sales and product development resources to ensure customer and consumer requirements are met or exceeded.

**The ideal candidate should possess the following:**

A strong leader as well as technical problem solver of production processes. This person will be expected to meet high expectations and demonstrate a strong sense of urgency, strive for collaboration but dictate when necessary while possessing unquestioned integrity. Characteristics include:

* Strong demonstrated leadership, communications, and analytical skills.
* Highly collaborative and team oriented.
* Demonstrated ability to work with minimal supervision, effectively work in a fast-paced environment, strong decision-making skills.
* Understanding and experience with customer service & an appreciation for the importance of reliable and consistent customer service.
* Ability to influence and create partnerships with diverse stakeholders.
* Ability to influence, interface and gain credibility across a wide range of levels.
* Understand and be able to interpret and analyze financial and operating statements.
* Strong problem solver with excellent communication skills to speak clearly and persuasively.
* Ability to effectively prioritize, use time efficiently, and develop realistic action plans.
* Ability to identify, motivate, mentor, and develop top talent.
* A working manager willing to “roll up the sleeves” to develop best-in-class operational processes.
* Adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.
* Attention to detail combined with tact and diplomacy.
* Inspires trust, engagement and respect at all levels of the company.
* Strong Change Management leader that motivates the team while driving necessary business/organizational restructuring activities.
* Some travel required.

**What We Offer You**

We believe that by continuously improving the quality of our benefits, we can help to raise the quality of life for our team members and their families. At First Quality you will receive:

* Competitive base salary and bonus opportunities
* Paid time off (three-week minimum)
* Medical, dental and vision starting day one
* 401(k) with employer match
* Paid parental leave
* Child and family care assistance (dependent care FSA with employer match up to $3750)
* Bundle of joy benefit (years’ worth of free diapers to all team members with a new baby)
* Tuition assistance
* Wellness program with savings of up to $4,000 per year on insurance premiums

...and more!

*First Quality is committed to protecting information under the care of First Quality Enterprises commensurate with leading industry standards and applicable regulations. As such, First Quality provides at least annual training regarding data privacy and security to employees who, as a result of their role specifications, may come in to contact with sensitive data.*

*First Quality is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identification, or protected Veteran status.*

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
**Job Description**
The Plant Manager will oversee operations which include environmental, health & safety, quality, production, maintenance, capital planning and execution in a cost-effective manner while meeting all customer requirements.
 
 
**Essential Duties/Responsibilities**
Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.
 
 

* Support, mentor and develop plant management and supervisory personnel through regular coaching and formal development tools.
* Lead all safety improvement initiatives and create a safety-based culture.
* Ensure ongoing compliance with all regulatory agencies including, OSHA, EPA, HACCP and other local and regional agencies.
* Prepare monthly reports, analyze financial budgets and take corrective measures as needed.
* Maintain efficient and timely flow of all raw materials received and ingredients shipped.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts in all areas of responsibility.
* Review and lead local Capital Projects, planning process to ensure compliance and development of assets for ongoing success and improvement.
* Ensure all personnel properly trained and equipment is in good working order to meet ongoing and future business needs.
* Assure all finish product shipped is in accordance with all quality standards and specifications.
* Effectively manage and reduce energy use at facility.
* Manage local purchasing activities.
* All other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* High School diploma or GED equivalent.
* Minimum 3+ years of experience in a supervisory/ management position in an industrial or plant setting.
* Rendering industry experience is a definite plus.

**Preferred Qualifications**

records.title: Manufacturing Ops Mgr / Plant Manager
records.description:
**What You Will Get**

* Competitive hourly pay
* Paid weekly
* Opportunity for annual performance increase
* 401K program with employer matching
* Room for growth and career advancement
* Health insurance
* Dental & vision Insurance
* Paid life Insurance
* Paid short term disability
* Paid vacation and sick time
* 11 paid holidays
* Health & Wellness Programs
* Employee Discount Programs

**What You'll Do**

* Own overall plant operations (production, material handling, inventory, and logistics) to meet throughput, quality, and profitability targets.
* Lead safety culture: conduct/oversee daily safety meetings, enforce ARC 100 and company safety programs, investigate incidents, and implement corrective actions.
* Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal requirements, including environmental and labor regulations.
* Plan and direct daily operations; monitor workflow and KPIs; identify and implement operational improvements and cost savings.
* Oversee maintenance and reliability: ensure preventive maintenance programs are followed, coordinate repairs and downtime planning, and verify maintenance documentation.
* Supervise, coach, and develop plant personnel; manage scheduling, timekeeping, attendance, performance feedback, and disciplinary actions as needed.
* Communicate routinely with Area Manager, Sales, and Dispatch regarding inbound/outbound materials, quantities, trucking needs, and upcoming work.
* Support customer and vendor relationships; ensure product availability and service meet expectations.
* Maintain accurate reporting and documentation; stay current through training and industry best practices.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Requirements**

* Experience: 3+ years in aggregate recycling operations or other process/production environment (5+ years and crushing plant equipment experience preferred)
* Ability to work in all weather conditions.
* Ability to stand for extended periods of time at conveyor belt operation.
* Ability to climb heights of 20 feet on a regular basis.
* Ability to lift, carry, and/or pull 50 pounds on a regular basis.
* Ability to work in dusty, wet, and loud environment.
* Required to wear safety equipment including hard hat, safety glasses, goggles, steel toed boots, ear plugs, gloves and various other similar items as required or needed.

*The statements above describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Employees may be required to perform other job-related duties as requested by management. This job description does not constitute an employment agreement and may be modified to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities.*

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
**Great benefits including: Medical, Dental Vision and Life Insurance; Paid Time Off; Paid Holidays; 401k & ESOP; Profit Sharing; Tuition Reimbursement and more!**

**Salary: $90,000 - $100,000**

**Position Summary:**
The Plant Manager is a dynamic and people-focused leader responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations of the plant while fostering a culture rooted in human-centered leadership. This role emphasizes managing people with empathy and authenticity, celebrating their successes, and cultivating an environment of inclusion and belonging. The RSO Plant Manager is committed to growing and developing a high-performing team while driving operational excellence. Key responsibilities include managing plant operations ensuring the plant is compliant with all safety policies and procedures, driving continuous improvement, and championing Rehrig’s mission and values.

**Key Accountabilities:**

1. **Demonstrate and Ensure Human-Centered Leadership:**
 * Lead with empathy and understanding, prioritizing the well-being and development of all team members.
 * Recognize and celebrate individual and team achievements to foster a positive and motivating work environment.
 * Promote and maintain a workplace culture where all employees feel valued, included, and empowered to contribute.
 * Implement and execute the plant’s People Engagement plan
2. **Ensure Compliance with Environmental, Health, Safety & Sustainability (EHS&S):**
 * Perform frequent compliance reviews. Lock out tag out (LOTO) periodic inspections, site safety checklist, EHS&S calendar action items.
 * Perform frequent Behavior Based Safety Observations (BBSOs)
 * Perform frequent 5S inspections to ensure facility is compliant.
 * Monitor Site EHS&S Scorecard and utilize Velocity EHS to identify leading indicators.
3. **Drive Continuous Improvement:**
 * Build continuous improvement activities into the daily work at the plant by involving the team in Kaizen activity. Utilize Kaizen methodology along with other tools such as Plan Do Check Act (PDCA) and A3 to drive continuous improvement.
 * Monitor KPI Metrics to drive decision-making
 * Develop and help manage capital improvement projects
 * Manage and support site CI tracker to analyze efficacy of CI projects
4. **Maintain Operational Excellence:**
 * Oversee plant operations to ensure high standards of Quality and Productivity are consistently met to standard.
 * Operate within Site budget by managing plant resources effectively

**Qualifications:**

* Experienced in plant management or a similar leadership role for at least 3 years.
* High School diploma required or equivalent.
* Experience in driving continuous improvement initiatives.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Commitment to team development and operational excellence.
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under pressure.

Why Rehrig Pacific?

Rehrig Pacific is a leading manufacturer of integrated sustainable solutions for the supply chain and environmental waste industries with a diverse customer list of industry leaders. We provide end-to-end solutions including returnable plastic products, delivery lifts and sleds, technology to track those assets, and a service team to ensure their longevity. Our team is dedicated to the values, mission, and unique culture within our organization that celebrates our people. We believe in fostering an environment where employees can be their authentic selves and know that they are viewed as integral members of the Rehrig Pacific Family.

Rehrig Pacific Company is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. See also here.
