records.description:
**Build Our Future Together**
Regeneron is currently seeking a Senior Manager Quality Assurance (QA) to join our internal QA Drug Product Manufacturing team. This role is responsible for Quality Assurance oversight of the SA12 Drug Product Manufacturing area, which supports equipment preparation, formulation, and aseptic filling operations. The position partners closely with Manufacturing, Technical Operations, and Quality organizations to ensure product quality, compliance, and continuous improvement across filling operations.
 
 
**When & Where**

* Location: Rensselaer, New York, United States
* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm

**Discover Your Role**

* Provide leadership to multiple teams under your supervision
* Oversee quality of all equipment prep, formulation, and filling (multiple lines)
* Own programs that support the department, such as area walkthroughs
* Support the development and growth of your team, including your people leaders
* Serve as the leadership point of contact for escalation of events and process updates
* Demonstrate leadership in cGMP environments, including speaking to and preparing for regulatory inspections and audits
* Collaborate and communicate effectively cross-functionally
* Think critically and drive continuous process improvement
* Lead a GMP department through a fast-paced, dynamic environment

**The Environment And Physical Rhythms Of The Role**

* Gowning: Full cleanroom attire (Examples may include: including laundered undergarments, gown, facemask, hairnet, safety glasses, safety shoes and booties, latex gloves and the use of sanitizing agents during gowning process including IPA)
* Ability to remove jewelry, make-up and nail adornments when wearing cleanroom attire

**This Role Requires**

* BS/BA in Life Sciences or related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience and 8+ years of relevant experience
* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience
* Experience with drug product manufacturing and/or fill finish is preferred

#REGNQA
 
 
Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.
 
 
Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.
 
 
Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

records.title: Director of Product Development & Industrialization
records.description:
At Horizon Hobby, we inspire dreams and help build memories! Our company is the leader in the global Radio Control industry, celebrating 40 years in 2025! We offer tremendous opportunities for growth and development and a full array of benefits including discounts on our products! We are currently hiring for a Director of Product Development and Industrialization at our Pro-Line office in Banning CA!
 
 
*This is a full time, on-site position at our Pro-Line facility in Banning California. Workings hours will be Monday-Friday 8am-5pm PST.*
**Typical pay for this position is $105,000-$125,000. The final offer for this position will be based on the unique experience and qualifications of the candidate selected. This position may also be eligible for a bonus not included in the base pay range.**
The Director of Product Development & Industrialization will provide strategic leadership for the development, commercialization, and industrialization of proprietary hobby products from concept through production. This role will be leading our Product Development, Product Engineering, and Industrialization resources while overseeing the systems, processes, tooling, molds, manufacturing equipment, and technical capabilities required to deliver innovative, high-quality products to market.
 
 
This role will partner closely with Brand, Sales, Marketing, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, Tooling, and external partners to identify market opportunities, translate customer needs into successful products, and ensure products are designed, developed, and launched efficiently. The role balances technical excellence with business performance, ensuring product investments align with growth objectives, customer demand, profitability targets, and long-term strategic priorities.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
Product Innovation & Strategy
 
 

* Partner with Brand and cross-functional teams to define product roadmaps, priorities, resources, and timelines.
* Drive innovation and development investments that strengthen market position, customer satisfaction, growth, and return on investment.
* Identify and prioritize new product opportunities using customer insight, competitive analysis, market trends, and commercial potential.

Product Development Leadership
 
 

* Lead and develop Product Development, Product Engineering, and Industrialization teams supporting proprietary products.
* Own product development from concept and engineering through validation, launch, and lifecycle management.
* Strengthen quality, scalability, execution, and organizational capability through standards, coaching, succession planning, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Business & Commercial Leadership
 
 

* Monitor portfolio performance and align cross-functional priorities to achieve revenue, profitability, and strategic objectives.
* Contribute to portfolio planning, market expansion, long-range growth, budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation.
* Provide senior leadership with business reviews, development updates, performance metrics, and recommendations.

Industrialization & Manufacturing Readiness
 
 

* Lead new-product industrialization from concept through launch, applying DFM and DFA to optimize quality, scalability, cost, and manufacturing readiness.
* Partner across Engineering, Manufacturing, Tool Room, suppliers, and development teams to resolve challenges and improve processes, tooling, and capacity.
* Track launch, readiness, quality, and productivity performance to drive continuous improvement.

Tooling, Equipment & Technology
 
 

* Define requirements and roadmaps for molds, tooling, fixtures, machinery, automation, and manufacturing technology.
* Lead capital planning and business cases that improve capability, productivity, quality, cost, and return on investment.
* Manage external tooling and manufacturing partners, strengthen internal capabilities, and maintain effective engineering data and technical documentation processes.

Supplier & Partner Management
 
 

* Build strategic relationships with domestic and international manufacturing, tooling, engineering, and supplier partners.
* Evaluate supplier capabilities and performance to improve quality, speed, cost competitiveness, and alignment with business objectives.

*Success in this role requires strong leadership across innovation, engineering, manufacturing, and business functions to continuously improve speed to market, product quality, operational performance, and return on investment*
**Required**
**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, Product Development, or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience in product management, category management, business management, product development, or a related leadership role.
* 5+ years of experience leading and developing teams.
* Demonstrated success growing a product category, business unit, or consumer product portfolio.
* Experience developing and launching successful products from concept through commercialization.
* Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets, forecasting, business cases, and profitability.
* Proven ability to develop business strategies and translate them into measurable results.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
* Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities.
* Ability to travel as required for customer visits, product testing, trade shows, industry events, and supplier meetings.

**Preferred**

* Experience in the RC, hobby products, powersports, automotive aftermarket, consumer products, or related industries.
* Experience working directly with enthusiast communities, racers, influencers, or brand ambassadors.
* Familiarity with manufacturing processes, new product introduction, and global sourcing environments.
* Experience using product lifecycle management (PLM) and project management systems.

**Physical Requirements**

* Occasional lifting of office supplies and materials, up to 20 pounds.
* Ability to sit or stand for extended periods while working on a computer.

*The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job.*
**Benefits & Other Perks**

* Medical, Dental, Vision
* HSA and FSA options
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance
* Life Insurance and Supplemental Life Insurance
* 401(k) with a company match
* Paid Time Off
* Paid Holidays
* Internal Rewards
* Discounts on Products
* Additional Coverage such as accident, critical, hospital and pet insurance

*Horizon Hobby is a progressive, innovative company and, as such, is constantly reevaluating and reinventing the processes and procedures associated with each job. The essential duties and responsibilities of this position may change at any time. In addition, employees may be asked to work on special projects or to assist with other work necessary or important to the operation of Horizon. Your cooperation and assistance in performing such additional work is expected and appreciated.*
**Horizon Hobby, LLC is an equal opportunity and E-Verify employer**

**Location:**
Conrona, CA or Brecksville, OH with a planned transitioning to Wickliffe, OH in 2028.
 
 
*As Lubrizol approaches its centennial in 2028, our Wickliffe campus will become the unified home of Lubrizol’s*
*global headquarters, integrating Lubrizol’s Brecksville site capabilities and employees to the Wickliffe campus.*
**Job Type:**
Hybrid. 4 days on-site
 
 
**Travel Expectancy:**
20 - 40%
 
 
**Salary Range:**
$160,000.00 - $220,000.00 + Bonus
 
 
**Shape the Future with Us.**
At Lubrizol, we’re bringing to life the chemistry behind clean water, efficient transportation, reliable infrastructure, critical medicines, and the products people rely on every day through science, sustainability, and a culture of inclusion.
 
 
As part of our global team, you’ll be empowered to make a real impact - on your career, your community, and the world around you.
 
 
****How You’ll Make An Impact****
The Global Leader, New Product Development – Medical Devices is a senior technical and people leader responsible for medical device new product development, from concept through commercialization. This role owns NPD strategy, talent development, governance, and execution across multiple geographies and development centers, ensuring strong alignment with customer needs, regulatory requirements, and business strategy.
 
 
The role leads a global, multidisciplinary NPD organization, partners closely with Quality, Regulatory, Manufacturing, Commercial, and Executive Leadership, and acts as a senior technical representative to key medical device OEM customers.
 
 
****Required Qualifications That Enable Your Success****

* Define and execute the global medical device NPD strategy aligned with business growth priorities, customer roadmaps, and portfolio strategy.
* Identify and pursue adjacent medical device applications where our technologies and platforms can create differentiated value and drive organic growth.
* Lead capability road mapping to define and build the new technical, testing, and development capabilities the group must invest in to sustain growth and capture high value programs.
* Establish scalable development governance, stage-gate rigor, and portfolio prioritization to ensure consistent execution excellence.
* Oversee complex, multi-site development programs from concept through commercialization, ensuring delivery to cost, schedule, performance, and quality expectations.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory to ensure compliance with FDA, CE/MDR, ISO 13485, and applicable global regulatory requirements.
* Serve as senior technical interface with strategic OEM customers, supporting complex development engagements and long-term partnerships.
* Collaborate with Commercial, Marketing, and Business Development to shape development proposals, technology roadmaps, and differentiated customer solutions.
* Champion design-for-manufacturability, design-for-quality, and design-for-cost principles across global manufacturing platforms.
* Ensure effective transfer of products from NPD to Manufacturing, preserving design intent, robustness, and scalability during launch and ramp-up.
* Lead and develop a global organization of NPD engineers, scientists, and program leaders across multiple regions and sites.
* Build technical bench strength through hiring, development, coaching, and succession planning.

****Required Qualifications That Enable Your Success****

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Biomedical, Chemical Engineering, or related technical discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* 10 or more years of progressive experience in medical device product development in a regulated environment., including experience in thermoplastic precision extrusion and silicone processing.
* Demonstrated experience leading global or multi-site technical teams.
* Strong working knowledge of FDA design controls, ISO 13485, FDA 21 CFR Part 820, and CE/MDR requirements.
* Proven track record delivering complex development programs from concept through commercialization and manufacturing transfer.

****Preferred Qualifications That Drive You Forward****

* Advanced technical degree (MS or PhD).
* Experience with catheter-based or minimally invasive medical device technologies.
* Strong understanding of polymer-based medical devices and associated manufacturing processes.

records.title: Director Engineering (New Product Development)
records.description:
Conair, a member of the Piovan Group, is the leading producer of auxiliary equipment for plastics processing in the world. We make and market over 450 different products, including resin-drying systems, blenders, feeders and material-conveying systems, temperature-control equipment and granulators. Extrusion solutions include gravimetric control systems, film and sheet scrap-reclaim systems and downstream equipment for pipe and profile extrusion. Conair is also a leader in plastics process integration, engineering and installing complete manufacturing systems that help plastics processors manage their valuable raw materials, handle their critical manufactured parts, and improve their process yield.

**Purpose**

The Director of New Product Development (NPD) Engineering is responsible for leading the design and development of Conair's next generation of auxiliary equipment for plastics processing, from concept through production launch. This position leads the NPD Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Advanced Research / Co-op groups and serves as the senior mechanical engineering authority for new products. The Director drives NPD projects through Conair's stage-gate process, manages engineering schedules and deliverables, and mentors and develops a team of engineers and designers. The Director works closely with Product Management, Sustainment Engineering, Manufacturing, and Purchasing to deliver new products that meet customer, cost, quality, and compliance targets. This position is located in Cranberry Township, Pennsylvania.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Drive NPD projects through Conair's stage-gate process from concept through launch, including requirements definition, gate deliverables, design reviews, and gate recommendations.
* Manage engineering schedules, resources, budgets, and deliverables across the NPD project portfolio, including alpha and beta prototype builds and release to production, and report status to engineering leadership.
* Serve as the technical lead and senior mechanical engineering authority for new products: set the design approach, lead design reviews and problem solving, ensure sound design practice (calculations, tolerance analysis, GD&T, materials selection, documentation standards), and identify patentable inventions.
* Lead design for manufacturing and assembly (DFM/DFA), design-to-cost, and value engineering, including designs suited to sheet metal fabrication, weldments, castings, machined and molded components.
* Plan and oversee prototype testing, verification and validation, and DFMEA with the Lab, and ensure new products meet applicable safety and regulatory requirements (e.g., UL, CE, NFPA 79).
* Partner with Product Management to translate voice-of-customer and business-case requirements into product specifications, and support product launches, including trade show display equipment.
* Coordinate mechanical, electrical, controls, and software development, and work with Purchasing and suppliers on sourcing, tooling, and cost targets, to deliver integrated, manufacturable designs.
* Transition new products smoothly into production and Sustainment Engineering with complete and accurate drawings, bills of material, specifications, and manuals.
* Mentor engineers and designers, building technical depth, design judgment, and project skills across the team, and support Conair's engineering co-op program.
* Review, hire, and train engineering staff; set goals, manage performance and workloads, and develop future technical leaders.
* Establish and track key performance metrics, such as gate schedule adherence, product cost versus target, and launch quality, and drive continuous improvement of the NPD process.
* Collaborate with Conair's engineering teams in the U.S., Italy, and India, and cultivate an environment which encourages teamwork, innovation, trust, and customer-inspired motivation.

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering required; Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or MBA a plus.
* Position typically expects 12+ years of mechanical design and product development experience in industrial equipment or machinery, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams; plastics processing auxiliary equipment, extrusion, or injection molding experience strongly preferred.
* Proven record of taking new products from concept through production launch using a stage-gate or phase-gate process.
* Strong hands-on mechanical design background, including sheet metal, weldments, castings, machined and molded parts, mechanisms, pneumatics, and heat transfer, airflow, or fluid systems.
* Strong working knowledge of GD&T, tolerance stack-up analysis, DFMEA, and design verification and validation; familiarity with 3D CAD and PDM/PLM systems sufficient to review designs and guide the team; FEA or simulation experience a plus.
* Demonstrated DFM/DFA, design-to-cost, and value engineering results; experience designing for in-house sheet metal fabrication a plus.
* Familiarity with electrical controls, PLCs, and machine safety standards (e.g., NFPA 79, UL 508A, CE Machinery Directive).
* Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, and develop engineers and designers and to manage schedules, resources, budgets, and competing priorities in a cross-functional organization; working knowledge of ERP systems.
* Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills, sound decision-making, and strong structured problem-solving (e.g., 8D, 5-Why, root cause analysis), with the ability to work effectively with customers, Product Management, and executive leadership.
* Ability to travel 10-15% of the time, including visits to customers, suppliers, trade shows, and Conair facilities, with occasional international travel.

Piovan Group is a world leader in the development and production of systems for the automation of production processes for the storage, transport and treatment of polymers, plastic, and food powders. The Group is close to its customers, on a global basis, through continuous technical assistance and support from the design phase to the installation and start-up of the system.

Customers, People, Innovation. These are the pillars of our philosophy that have led us to grow in a path that began more than fifty years ago, pursuing our development objectives with honesty, integrity, and transparency.

**Piovan Group offers an outstanding compensation and benefits package including profit sharing, bonus plans, 401(k) with company match, medical insurance, dental, vision, life insurance, short- and long-term disability, health club reimbursement, tuition reimbursement, employee assistance, and employee referral bonus program.**

*Piovan Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE) and offers employment opportunities to all qualified persons regardless of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability (except where physical or mental abilities are a bona fide occupational requirement), veteran status, marital status, familial status, sexual orientation, HIV-positive status, possession of the sickle cell trait, genetic characteristics, political views, and any other basis protected by federal, state or local laws.*

records.description:
**Application Close Date**
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.
 
 
At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.
 
 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and require your commitment and detailed attention toward safe and repeatable space flight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.
 
 
We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
 
 
Blue Origin is scaling production of its electric propulsion systems. We are hiring a Director to own the manufacturing outcome for that product line and to carry it from development hardware into rate production.
 
 
You will be the single-threaded leader for Operations of this program: one person accountable for rate, quality, cost, and people, with full authority over the entire in-program production flow.
 
 
This is a build-it role, not a run-it role. You will define the value streams, stand up integration with support organizations, and build the team that runs the line — working concurrently with an active design program rather than behind a frozen one.
 
 
**Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To**

* Own the strategy, roadmap, and priorities for successful manufacturing outcomes of the electric propulsion thruster line — delivery rate, quality, cost, and the people who produce it.
* Build the production organization. Define the value streams, stand up production control and manufacturing engineering, and hire and develop the leadership beneath you as the program scales.
* Own the get-to-rate plan. Define the path from development build to sustained rate production, and demonstrate cycle time at the rate-readiness gate as a committed acceptance number rather than a projection.
* Lead the transition from development build into rate production, including the qualification of tooling, processes, and work instructions required to produce repeatably at rate.
* Drive producibility into the product during design, rather than absorbing it on the floor later. Own the manufacturing view of the bill of materials as the product configuration evolves.
* Establish and own the program's working interfaces with quality, supply chain, material planning, and test operations.
* Build and manage the program's manufacturing operating budget and capital plan, owning responsibility for product delivery at cost and rate.
* Set the safety and quality culture for a new production team, and hold it as the organization grows.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in an engineering or technical discipline.
* 12+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, supply chain, or operations, including 5+ years leading manufacturing organizations.
* Direct, hands-on experience taking a new product or production line from development into rate production.
* Experience carrying a product through a production-readiness or rate-readiness gate, and owning the cycle-time and capability evidence presented at it.
* Experience building an organization — defining structure, hiring leaders, and developing a team through significant growth.
* Line management of both salaried professionals and craft or technician populations.
* Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguity: making defensible assumptions and moving forward on an incomplete definition, then correcting as information arrives.
* Ability to travel frequently, up to approximately 35%, to other Blue Origin sites.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 15+ years of manufacturing and operations experience.
* Propulsion, spacecraft, satellite, or other high-reliability low-volume hardware experience.
* Experience transitioning a product from low-volume, high-mix build into repeatable rate production.
* Demonstrated cycle-time or throughput improvement with measured results.
* Experience standing up production at a new or greenfield manufacturing site.
* Experience managing a build against a bill of materials that changed materially during production ramp.
* Formal lean or continuous-improvement training, with applied results on a production line.
* Master’s degree in engineering or technical field, or MBA.

**Base Pay Range For**
WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30
 
 
**Other Site Ranges May Differ**
**Culture Statement**
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
 
 
**Export Control Regulations**
Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
 
 
**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
* Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
* Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**
Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.
 
 
**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**
Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com. Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

records.title: Director, Innovation & Commercialization Operations
records.description:
**ABOUT US**

At the heart of AG1 lies a commitment to our mission to empower people to take ownership of their health. Since 2010, we've dedicated ourselves to bringing Foundational Nutrition to people around the world.

Our ethos is deeply rooted in science, with an unwavering dedication to continuous improvement. We leverage and contribute to the latest research to deliver a powerful, straightforward solution for optimal health to our customers. We harness the finest ingredients so that every scoop of AG1 gives you the nutrients you need with the simplicity you want in a daily routine.

Likewise, our organization puts the same energy into creating an environment that is a reflection of the cultural values that define who we are and how we work together. These seven values— One Spectacular Life, Customer Obsessed, Radical Ownership, High Performance, Courage, Amazing Humans and Continuous Pursuit of Excellence —are a representation of the high standards we set, and hold ourselves accountable to, when it comes to building our global team.

**THE ROLE**

AG1 is expanding its innovation portfolio across products, formats, and channels. We are seeking an experienced leader to operate, and continuously strengthen our enterprise Stage Gate governance and commercialization process. This role will combine governance design and decision discipline with hands-on cross-functional execution, helping AG1 move products from concept through development, manufacturing readiness, and launch with greater clarity, speed, and accountability.

Reporting to the Chief Legal & Administrative Officer, the Director will have meaningful delegated ownership of the governance model, including recommending and implementing gate standards, decision protocols, performance measures, and improvements. The Director will partner closely with Product Development leadership and functional stakeholders while maintaining an enterprise-wide perspective.

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

Stage Gate Governance & Decision Discipline

* Design, operation, and evolution of the Stage Gate governance framework with the executive owner, including gate criteria, required evidence, decision rights, and escalation pathways.
* Lead high-quality gate reviews focused on decisions and readiness, not routine status updates; document approvals, conditions, owners, and formal closure.
* Maintain a concise gate decision record covering evidence, approvals, conditions, decisions locked or left open, exceptions, and accountable owners; follow conditional approvals through closure.
* Develop and maintain practical standards for decisions that become locked at each gate, including clear controls for material changes after approval.
* Apply proportionate gate requirements for product variants, new flavors, pack sizes, and claims changes, based on risk and complexity rather than a one-size-fits-all process.
* Identify decisions requiring executive intervention, frame options and trade-offs, and recommend an appropriate path forward.

Cross-functional Planning & Execution

* Integrate NPD plans across Product Development, Packaging, Procurement, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, Finance, Marketing, Retail, DTC, and International.
* Establish critical-path plans, realistic functional lead times, dependencies, and clean handoffs; ensure early functional engagement before downstream commitments are made.
* Maintain integrated launch baselines and forecasts; when upstream milestones slip, make the impacts on timing, scope, resources, and risk explicit for the accountable decision-maker.
* Provide visibility into project status, timing, risks, competing resource demands, and launch-readiness decisions.
* Partner with accountable product and functional owners to resolve gaps without displacing their technical or commercial decision authority.

Commercialization Readiness

* Coordinate upstream-to-downstream requirements across formula and claims decisions, packaging specifications and qualification, artwork and labels, sourcing, master data, production, and channel launch activities.
* Define clear readiness expectations for manufacturing, inventory, retailer execution, and DTC launch; ensure deviations are explicitly evaluated and approved.
* Surface the timing, cost, and execution impacts of proposed late changes.

Process Excellence & Adoption

* Build on AG1’s recent Stage Gate redesign work, including streamlined tasks, improved sequencing and redesigned gate meetings, and operationalize changes across active launches.
* Simplify or eliminate duplicative and legacy requirements while protecting critical controls and decision quality.
* Review briefs, approval points, and handoff artifacts to ensure each has a clear purpose, owner, and downstream user; retire redundant documentation.
* Create a reliable system of record for current decisions, approved versions, deliverables, owners, milestones, and changes.
* Establish a practical framework for handling retailer-specific requests and other exceptions, including their incremental cost, capacity, and schedule implications.
* Define useful measures of process effectiveness, such as on-time gate closure, changes to locked decisions, rework, and launch readiness; train teams and drive adoption.

**WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

*Required Qualifications*

* 10+ years in CPG new product development, innovation operations, commercialization, or related cross-functional leadership, ideally including food, beverages, or nutritional products.
* Demonstrated experience owning or materially redesigning a formal Stage Gate or comparable NPD governance framework, not merely participating in gate meetings.
* Experience launching physical consumer products and understanding formulation, regulatory/quality, packaging, supply chain, manufacturing, and commercial interdependencies.
* Strong judgment in setting governance standards while avoiding unnecessary bureaucracy; experience leading decision forums and navigating cross-functional trade-offs.
* Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders without direct authority, implement change, and turn complex workflows into practical operating routines.
* Excellent integrated planning, risk management, facilitation, and executive communication skills.
* Experience facilitating executive gate decisions, setting and tracking conditions of approval, and leading pragmatic change control.

*Preferred Qualifications*

* Experience spanning mature CPG processes and high-growth, entrepreneurial environments.
* Experience with beverage or supplement categories and retail, DTC, Amazon, or international launches.
* PMP certification or equivalent formal training in project or program management methodologies.
* Familiarity with PLM, NPD portfolio tools, and process excellence methodologies.

**WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?**

* Competitive compensation and performance-based incentive plans.
* A 100% remote working environment (excluding Laboratory positions), which has been implemented from day one.
* A strong company culture that is enforced through the hiring process to ensure values alignment and a highly collaborative team.
* A mission-driven approach to everything that we do, with an overall goal to significantly improve our customers’ health and wellness.
* A high-growth, dynamic environment with opportunities for your direct impact to be felt.
* Paid holidays, company-wide reset and reflect days, and unlimited PTO (based on your country of residence).
* In-person team meetups for optimal collaboration, team building and accelerating productivity.
* A work environment and culture that is based on high performance, productivity and continuous improvement.
* The opportunity to work with passionate, high-growth, business-minded colleagues who bring their all to our mission each and every day.
* Access to AG1 products and branded swag.
* Monthly telecom stipend to offset some of the costs of home internet/wifi for eligible team members.
* All other benefits and insurances as required by law, based on your specific country of residence.

AG1 is dedicated to providing equitable and competitive compensation & benefits packages. For this particular role, the base salary range is $145,000 - $180,000 and will ultimately be decided at the offer stage, based on an individual candidate’s level of skills and experience aligned with the needs of this role. Base salary is one component of total compensation for this position. We provide a competitive mix of base salary, performance bonus, and stock option allocation for eligible roles.

*AG1 is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to inspiring fulfilling lives, starting with a focus on health and we believe this starts in the workplace. We do this by providing employees with a safe and welcoming work environment free of discrimination and harassment. We strive to create a diverse & inclusive environment where all team members can thrive, feel a sense of belonging, and make a difference in the world together. We do not discriminate based on age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, pregnancy, veteran status, disability, or any other status protected by law. We are an equal opportunity employer.*

Pursuant to the Los Angeles Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

*Please review our Privacy Policy, including the Job Applicants section, to learn more about how we collect and use personal information in the application process:
https://drinkag1.com/privacy
.*

records.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
records.description:
Domino’s Pizza, which began in 1960 as a single store location in Ypsilanti, MI, has had a lot to celebrate lately: we’re a reshaped, reenergized brand of honesty, transparency and accountability – not to mention, great food! In the rise to becoming a true technology leader, the brand is now consistently one of the top five companies in online transactions and 65% of our sales in the U.S. are taken through digital channels. The brand continues to ‘deliver the dream’ to local business owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores. That’s just the tip of the iceberg…or as we might say, one “slice” of the pie! If this sounds like a brand you’d like to be a part of, consider joining our team!
 
 
**Job Description**
The Director, Continuous Improvement leads the Supply Chain-wide capability for identifying, prioritizing, enabling, and sustaining improvements that increase business performance and organizational effectiveness across functions and end-to-end processes. This role establishes a culture of continuous improvement, advances operational and business process excellence, and enables measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, service, and capacity.
 
 
Working closely with cross-functional Supply Chain leaders, this position standardizes processes, uses data and insights to prioritize opportunities, and implements sustainable solutions aligned with strategic objectives. The Director maintains a strong connection to frontline operations by working directly in Supply Chain Centers and other functional environments to understand processes firsthand and translate observations into meaningful improvements.
 
 
**What You’ll Do**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive Continuous Improvement strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with Supply Chain priorities, and advise Supply Chain leadership on opportunities that improve productivity, efficiency, cost, service, quality, capacity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Lead the deployment of consistent Continuous Improvement methodologies, tools, governance, performance expectations, and resource prioritization across Supply Chain functions.
* Work directly with Supply Chain Centers and functional teams to observe work at the point of execution, identify process variation and non-value-added activities, and implement standardized processes, operating practices, management systems, standard work, and process controls.
* Lead cross-functional transformation and productivity initiatives, including process redesign, technology-enabled improvement, automation, and new ways of working, in partnership with functional leaders, the PMO, Finance, and other stakeholders.
* Establish measurable outcomes, baselines, KPI definitions, reporting standards, dashboards, and processes for tracking, validating, and sustaining financial benefits, productivity improvements, and business value.
* Build organizational Continuous Improvement capability through training, coaching, structured problem-solving, knowledge sharing, and the development of CI team members and functional leaders.
* Lead change management and cross-functional alignment, manage risks and barriers, strengthen process integration, and communicate priorities, progress, results, and recommendations to Supply Chain leadership and key stakeholders.

**What You’ll Bring**
In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:
 
 
Be Curious
 
 

* Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
* Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots
 
 

* Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
* Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High
 
 

* Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
* Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast
 
 

* Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
* Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More
 
 

* Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
* Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations
 
 

* Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino’s Ways of Working.
* Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
* Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
* Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline; an advanced degree or MBA is preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, business transformation, operational excellence, or related disciplines, including demonstrated leadership experience in complex, cross-functional organizations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing Continuous Improvement strategies and delivering measurable business results across multiple functions or complex organizations.
* Strong knowledge and practical application of Lean Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, process optimization, standardization, and change management methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change without direct authority.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience leading Continuous Improvement initiatives in manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or other complex operational environments, including the ability to engage frontline employees, site leaders, and senior executives to diagnose issues, implement solutions, and deliver measurable results.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience identifying, quantifying, and validating productivity improvements, cost savings, and business value.
* Well-developed team building and influencing skills, unquestioned integrity, and the experience and confidence to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
* Experience developing performance management frameworks, leveraging data analytics, and translating insights into actionable business recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to build organizational capability through coaching, talent development, and deployment of Continuous Improvement methodologies.
* Strong strategic thinking, communication, collaboration, and executive presentation skills.
* Experience managing complex improvement portfolios, prioritizing competing business needs, and delivering sustainable outcomes.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated Continuous Improvement expertise is preferred.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including Canada, as business needs require. Expected travel is up to 50%

**Additional Information**
Benefits:
 
 

* Paid Holidays and Vacation
* Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
* No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
* Childcare tuition discounts
* No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
* Fertility benefits
* Adoption assistance
* 401k matching contributions
* 15% off the purchase price of stock
* Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

records.title: Director, Operational Excellence
records.description:
**Job Description**
**Company Overview**
Vertex is a global biotechnology company focused on investing in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases. Across our organization, we work with urgency, rigor, and collaboration to deliver therapies that improve patient outcomes and create long-term value.
 
 
**General Summary**
The Operational Excellence team serves as the process improvement and performance enablement backbone of CMTO, providing the improvement discipline, management systems, and change capabilities required to run, grow, and optimize Vertex’s commercial manufacturing network.
 
 
The Director, Operational Excellence leads the development and execution of CMTO’s Operational Excellence strategy and improvement portfolio. The role identifies and prioritizes performance improvement opportunities, leads structured problem-solving and transformation initiatives, and ensures improvements are implemented and sustained through effective change management, standard work, performance monitoring, and leadership accountability.
 
 
The Director also leads and develops the Operational Excellence team, building organizational capability, setting priorities, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability. The role partners closely with Business Analytics, Network Performance, Manufacturing Operations, MS&T, Business Operations Leads, Quality, Supply Chain, and Finance to use performance insights to identify improvement priorities and deliver measurable business outcomes.
 
 
**Key Duties And Responsibilities**

* Operational Excellence Strategy & Initiative Execution
* Contribute to setting CMTO's operational excellence strategy, priorities, and success measures, aligned to enterprise and functional priorities
* Identify, prioritize, and drive execution of a portfolio of commercial manufacturing improvement and transformation initiatives — partnering with sites and functions while avoiding ownership of routine operations
* Lead initiatives targeting lead-time reduction, launch optimization, yield, and manufacturing success-rate improvements and COGM reduction through structured problem definition, root-cause analysis, options analysis, and ROI calculation
* Lead Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, and structured problem-solving initiatives across technical and business processes
* Develop clear business cases, recommendations, and implementation plans for Operational Excellence initiatives, including expected benefits, resource requirements, risks, and measures of success.
* Manage and Lead the Operational Excellence Team
* Establish and communicate a clear vision, mission, and strategic direction for the Operational Excellence team, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and stakeholder expectations
* Partner with senior leadership to define team priorities, continuously reassessing and adjusting focus based on evolving business needs, operational risks, and strategic objectives
* Set clear performance expectations, goals, and development plans for team members; monitor progress, provide timely feedback, and hold the team accountable for results
* Remove organizational barriers and resolve escalated issues that impede team performance or delivery of key initiatives
* Foster a culture of continuous improvement, collaboration, innovation, and accountability by coaching and mentoring team members in problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills
* Build organizational capability by identifying skill gaps, developing talent, and implementing training and succession plans that strengthen Operational Excellence competencies
* Communicate team objectives, progress, achievements, risks, and resource needs to senior leadership and key stakeholders, ensuring transparency and alignment across organization
* Promote cross-functional collaboration and strong stakeholder relationships to enable successful execution of Operational Excellence initiatives and sustainable business improvements
* Continuous Improvement & Change Execution
* Embed structured problem-solving, continuous improvement, and change execution into CMTO governance and operating rhythms, using performance insights provided by Business Analytics, Network Performance, and functional teams.
* Ensure improvements are implemented and sustained through effective change management, standard work, control plans, performance monitoring, and clear process ownership.
* Identify and deploy digital tools, automation, and process solutions that improve operational performance and the scalability of Operational Excellence practices.
* Community of Practice & Capability Building
* Operate as a community-of-practice leader for manufacturing operational excellence across internal manufacturing and supply chain, driving common standards, methods, and ways of working
* Mentor teams on Lean methods, structured problem-solving, and continuous improvement practices, and benchmark industry best practices to inform innovative approaches

**Knowledge And Skills**

* Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, and team building
* Proven ability to motivate teams and build team unity
* Demonstrated success implementing Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, FMEA, Hoshin Kanri, and Change Management methodologies in GMP environments
* Proven experience leading improvement initiatives targeting lead-time reduction, launch optimization, yield improvement and COGM/COGs reduction
* Experience using operational data and performance insights to identify, prioritize, and measure improvement opportunities.
* Hands-on proficiency in data analysis, root-cause analysis, process analysis, and structured problem-solving
* Ability to quantify the operational and financial benefits of improvement initiatives and communicate clear recommendations to senior stakeholders.
* Experience implementing and sustaining performance management systems, visual management, Standard Work, and Leader Standard Work.
* Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word; experience with process mapping, statistical analysis, and Lean Six Sigma tools preferred.
* Ability to translate complex operational problems into clear improvement priorities, recommendations, and implementation plans.
* Ability to operate effectively in a matrixed environment with strong role clarity, partnering across Network Performance, Business Operations, Manufacturing Operations, MS&T, Finance, and Strategic Sourcing

**Education And Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Life Sciences, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
* Typically requires 8–12 years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, regulated manufacturing, supply chain, MS&T, Operational Excellence, or business transformation environments.
* Minimum 5 years of experience leading Operational Excellence, transformation, continuous improvement, or complex process-improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated experience leading and developing teams.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt required

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.
 
 
**Pay Range**
$181,900 - $272,900
 
 
**Disclosure Statement**
The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law.
 
 
At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations. From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more.
 
 
**Flex Designation**
Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible
 
 
**Flex Eligibility Status**
In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as:
 
 

* Hybrid: work remotely up to two days per week; or select
* On-Site: work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility.

Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time.
 
 
**Company Information**
Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation.
 
 
Vertex is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, or any characteristic protected under applicable law. Vertex is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. Vertex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.
 
 
Any applicant requiring an accommodation in connection with the hiring process and/or to perform the essential functions of the position for which the applicant has applied should make a request to the recruiter or hiring manager, or contact Talent Acquisition at ApplicationAssistance@vrtx.com

records.title: Director, Continuous Improvement Business Partner
records.description:
**Life Unlimited.**
At Smith+Nephew we design and manufacture technology that takes the limits off living. This role does not currently have direct reports but works across the global matrixed teams (across functions and regions) to grow the adoption of 'Our Way to Win' Conitnuous Improvement Strategy for maximum impact and cultural transformation. This role works with leadership teams to align and execute against our strategy, and enables the leadership teams to create a continuous improvement culture that routinely achieves its business goals. This person will own the development of continuous improvement capabilities throughout the organization, driving all business KPIs aligned with revenue, SG&A expenses, marketing, R&D driving overall profitable growth.
 
 
**What will you be doing?**
Partners with Wound leadership team to identify/develop and deliver key performance indicators (KPIs) throughout the organization aligned to the overall functional objectives Respectfully cultivates an action-biased culture of continuous improvement to advance business and functional KPI’s aligned to Smith + Nephew’s corporate goals. Responsible for leading through facilitating/enabling the implementation of 'Our Way to Win' throughout all of the Wound business. Establish and mature a Lean Management System (Tiered Accountability, Visual Management, Gemba Walks, and Leader Standard Work) and other coaching tools to transform the culture. Works with teams to streamline processes to improve business and functional objectives, with a specific focus on customer experience and end-to-end optimization. Provides support to develop Continuous Improvement expertise and capability within the organization at all levels. Improves the decision-making model and problem-solving capabilities within high performance teams to increase the autonomy and pace of change. Provides regular, ongoing reporting and communications to Wound leadership regarding status of implementation and maturity. Collaborates with Continuous Improvement teammates to leverage and share standard methodologies, and drive improvements to the company level 'Way to Win' Roadmap, tools, and technology.
 
 
**What will you need to be successful?**

* Four-year university degree required (business, marketing, or engineering, preferred); Master’s Degree required.
* Leadership roles from disciplines such as Sales, Marketing, Strategy Development and Deployment, Lean/Operating System/Business System
* Proven track record for developing, training, and coaching teams across cultures
* 12 years in process improvement and/or lean related experience
* Minimum of 8+ years of experience and “hands on” track record of implementing successful lean based business systems including elements such as:

+ Strategy Deployment and A3 Thinking
+ Lean Management Systems (Tiered Accountability, Visual Management, Gemba Walks, Leader Standard Work)
+ Value-Stream Mapping
+ Kaizen events
+ Expertise in problem solving utilizing a formal program/process
+ Implementation of KPI Management across functions and businesses

* Med-Tech or Healthcare experience a plus
* Experience in Change Management, and able to act as an influential change agent
* Microsoft Office expertise

**KNOWLEDGE SKILLS & ABILITIES:**

* Broad knowledge of multi-functional, multi-site, global organizational processes and financial business methods
* Demonstrated skill and confidence in proactively building relationships with top tier partners/leaders both internally and externally
* Demonstrated experience and leadership in managing comprehensive continuous improvement approaches/methodologies to advance an organization’s strategy and goals
* Strong ability to anticipate future needs of the organization and make decisions in a changing environment
* Great communicator, demonstrated ability in solid written, oral, and presentation-giving skills
* Ability to effectively work with different cultures in a global, matrixed environment
* High ethical standards to support a professional business code of conduct
* Passion for driving improvement and leading change in complex environments
* A holistic thinker who can look enterprise-wide to integrate and streamline systems for optimal benefit
* Able to drive strategic thinking and continuous improvement in both operational and non-operational areas, including connecting cross-functional resources to remove waste along the extended value streams
* Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to connect with and positively influence leadership and all levels of the organization
* Energetic, flexible, collaborative and proactive leader who welcomes challenges
* Manages time and resources effectively through strong organization, multi-tasking, and time management skills
* Works independently as a self-starter committed to delivering performance results
* Analyzes information to make sound business decisions taking prudent business risks as appropriate
* Strong analytical skills
* Ability to work independently and as a part of a team to seek resolution to problems
* Acts as an influential change agent
* Able to travel domestically and internationally up to 50% as needed

**You Unlimited.**

* The anticipated base compensation range for this position is $181,500 - $213,500 USD annually. The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate will be based on multiple factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge/skills, experience, and geographic location. Compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate. In addition to base pay, we offer competitive bonus and benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), tuition reimbursement, medical leave programs, parental leave, generous PTO, paid company holidays, 8 hours of volunteer time annually, and a variety of wellness offerings such as EAP.
* Inclusion + Belonging: Committed to Welcoming, Celebrating and Thriving. Learn more about our Employee Inclusion Groups on our website https://www.smith-nephew.com/
* Your Future: 401k Matching Program, 401k Plus Program, Discounted Stock Options, Tuition Reimbursement
* Work/Life Balance: Flexible Personal/Vacation Time Off, Paid Holidays, Flex Holidays, Paid Community Service Day
* Your Wellbeing: Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Account (Employer Contribution of $500+ annually), Employee Assistance Program, Parental Leave, Fertility and Adoption Assistance Program
* Flexibility: Hybrid Work Model (For most professional roles)
* Training: Hands-On, Team-Customized, Mentorship
* Extra Perks: Discounts on fitness clubs, travel and more!

Smith+Nephew provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or disability.
 
 
Stay connected by joining our Talent Community.
 
 
We're more than just a company - we're a community! Follow us on LinkedIn to see how we support and empower our employees and patients every day.
 
 
Check us out on Glassdoor for a glimpse behind the scenes and a sneak peek into
**You. Unlimited.**
, life, culture, and benefits at S+N.
 
 
Explore our website and learn more about our mission, our team, and the opportunities we offer.

Ready to make a measurable impact on operational performance and profitability? We’re looking for a strategic, hands-on leader to drive continuous improvement, optimize production, and strengthen margins at a meat or poultry processing facility.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Lead Lean, Continuous Improvement, and Six Sigma initiatives to reduce costs, minimize waste, and improve productivity.
* Identify opportunities to improve yields, labor efficiency, production flow, and overall profitability.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, and Finance to drive process improvements and capital projects.
* Establish KPIs, analyze performance data, and present improvement strategies to senior leadership.
* Lead cross-functional teams in implementing best practices while maintaining safety, quality, and service standards.

* Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering or a related field.
* **Required: Experience in a meat or poultry processing facility.**
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification and hands-on Lean implementation experience.
* Experience with process engineering, time and motion studies, project management, and root cause analysis.
* Strong analytical skills, including advanced Excel, Minitab, AutoCAD, and SQL.
* Proven ability to influence teams and deliver measurable operational and financial results.

records.title: Director of Quality Management
records.description:
Overview:

**Select Specialty Hospital - Cincinnati**

**Critical Illness Recovery Hospital (LTACH)**

**Director of Quality Management**

 

* Bonus incentives
* Extensive onboarding and training program
* Customizable health insurance packages

**Who We Are**

Our hospital is a critical illness recovery hospital committed to providing world-class inpatient post-ICU services to chronic, critically ill patients who require extended healing and recovery. We help patients during some of the most vulnerable, painful moments of their lives – and our team plays a central role in providing compassionate, excellent care every step of the way.

Responsibilities:

We are looking for a valued employee who will be Champions of the Select Medical Way, which includes putting the patient first, helping to improve quality of life for the community in which you live and work, continuing to develop and explore new ideas, providing high-quality care and doing well by doing what is right.

* Coordinating all survey activities to assure that the facility maintains accreditation, certification, and licensure.
* Organizing monthly interdisciplinary QAPI Team meetings with activities, per QAPI Calendar
* Receiving and reviewing quarterly quality improvement reports.
* Assisting the Medical Director and Quality Program Director with development and implementation of medical staff quality improvement activities.
* Leading the hospital team in the performance of RCA, at least annually, and for every level 3-4 incident, unless otherwise indicated.
* Completing monthly quality related data entry, analysis and reporting.

records.title: Director Quality
records.description:
### **Activités**

**SUMMARY:**

Reporting to the President, C.E.O., Directs and coordinates activities of personnel at all Hutchinson Sealing Systems facilities engaged in Quality Management System to prevent or eliminate defects in new or existing products or process by performing the following duties personally or through subordinates. This position is designated as a sensitive function for quality, engineering, manufacturing, supplier, audit, compliance, and operational information, including quality performance data, customer requirements, product and process development information, audit findings, corrective actions, supplier performance records, and proprietary company information. The incumbent is responsible for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets in accordance with company policies and customer requirements.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

* Analyzes, evaluates, and presents information concerning factors such as quality performance, production capabilities, manufacturing problems, customer quality trends, and quality planning of new products for consideration by other members of the management team.
* Presents and evaluates alternative methods and procedures to establish standardized quality systems based on best practices.
* Participates with other top management personnel in formulating and establishing company policies, operating procedures, and goals.
* Participates in review of product development activities and APQP milestones.
* Conducts Quality System Management review meetings with top management to assess performance and compliance to customer quality requirements.
* Reviews technical problems and procedures of departments and recommends solutions to problems or changes in procedures.
* Confers with engineers and managers about quality assurance of new products and process to improve manufacturing capability.
* Reviews technical publications, articles, and abstracts to stay abreast of technical and quality system developments in industry.
* Travel required on a frequent basis to suppliers and customer facilities as well as other Hutchinson facilities.
* Provides internal quality system audit of Hutchinson Sealing Systems locations.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

Master's degree (M.A.) or equivalent; or four to ten years’ related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Qualifications may be waived by management. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:**

None.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Manages subordinates in department. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of this unit. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complains and resolving problems.

**TEAM SKILLS:**

Hutchinson is built around teamwork. This position requires the use of good team skills such as cooperation, information sharing, task sharing, timely completion of assignments, good listening and communication skills and overall respect for other team members.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:**

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret common scientific and technical journals, financial reports, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community. Ability to write speeches and articles for publication that conform to prescribed style and format. Ability to effectively present information to top management, public groups and/or boards of directors.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:**

Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference, and fundamentals of plane and solid geometry and trigonometry. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

**COMPUTER SKILLS:**

Ability to use word processing, spreadsheet applications. Must be familiar with internet research, Microsoft Office software, and the use of e-mail.

**REASONING ABILITY:**

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close, vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

**HEALTH AND SAFETY:**

Must actively support our Health Safety and Environmental policy, immediately report all Safety hazards and correct them when able to safely do so, participate in all required Safety Training, meetings, inspects, and use all required PPE.
