records.title: Senior Director, Strategy & Operations, Point of Care, Remote
records.description:
Working in the Office of the Chief Medical Officer and reporting to the VP of Point of Care & Risk Stratification, the Senior Director of Strategy & Operations, Point of Care, will lead day-to-day operations, partnerships, go-to-market efforts, and wraparound support services to maximize the impact of Aledade’s value-based care insights to our partner practices.

The team is looking for a high-output generalist with a strong business analyst toolkit, looking to rapidly take ownership of complex content with high visibility, working across multiple stakeholders. Candidates that thrive managing multiple deadlines on tight timelines and learning content quickly are best positioned to succeed; successful team members in the same function primarily have backgrounds in consulting and generalist healthcare strategy & operations roles.

To start, the role will focus on 1) scaling the deployment of our point of care tools and 2) broadening and deepening the insights available in our point of care tools, to maximize the impact of Aledade’s insights on our patients’ health outcomes and partner practices’ success in their value-based care contracts.

At the end of their first year, a successful leader in the role will own end-to-end accountability for 1) proactive identification, development, and execution of Point of Care deployment improvement opportunities, including field, practice, and clinician education, deployment automation and monitoring, and go to market approach and materials, 2) strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact, 3) goal setting, metric identification and development, and impact evaluation for our point of care tools, 4) identification, evaluation, contracting, and cross-functional execution of net new vendor and external partnerships that support insight delivery and impact.

Additionally, this role will 1) provide direction and expert guidance to junior team members owning individual initiatives, including incentive and adoption programs, educational efforts, hotspotting, monitoring, and alerting development, practice and user-level prioritization and triage, and 2) coordinate with cross-functional product, analytics, technology, performance, care programs, and other senior leaders across Aledade to advance point of care tool adoption and impact.

The role is expected to start as a senior individual contributor, but is expected to grow into a people manager in the near term.

### **Primary Duties:**

In collaboration with cross-functional product, analytics, technology, performance, care programs, and other senior leaders across Aledade:

* Own single-threaded accountability for proactive identification, development, and execution of Point of Care deployment improvement opportunities, including field, practice, and clinician education, deployment automation and monitoring, and go to market approach and materials

* Lead strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact

* Drive goal setting, metric identification and development, and impact evaluation for our point of care tools

* In support of maximizing insight delivery and impact, lead the evaluation, contracting, and cross-functional execution of net new vendor and external partnerships

* Direct and support other Transformation team members’ ideation and execution of strategic initiatives related to point of care deployment and impact

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in Economics, Business, Healthcare, or a related field
* 12+ years of progressive professional experience, or 7+ years progressive professional experience with a Master’s Degree, strongly preferred
* 6+ years of experience in healthcare
* 2+ years of experience in value-based care

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Advanced exploration of emerging AI tools, with additional preference given to individuals that have demonstrated ability building, scaling, and/or teaching AI tooling to broader teams
* Expert Excel skills required, including the ability to work with large, complex, & often incomplete data sets; conduct one-off complex analyses quickly; and utilize Index / Match, XLOOKUP, FILTER, and other advanced formulas
* Advanced PPT skills required, including storyboarding skills, ability to translate complex analyses and concepts into engaging slides, and ability to draft executive-level materials with limited direction
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, as well as the ability to build strong relationships and work with individuals at all levels of the organization, tailoring communication style as appropriate based on audience
* Excellent project management skills, including proven track record leading complex, cross-functional initiatives in health care operations settings
* Strong strategic planning and analytical skills
* Strong “business analyst” toolkit, including abilities to independently prioritize, solve problems via hypothesis-driven analytical methods, manage across multiple responsibilities and projects, execute with attention to detail, and overcome ambiguity
* Poise, confidence, and maturity interacting with key stakeholders, including senior leaders
* Commitment to confidentiality and discretion in appropriately handling sensitive information is required

Sitting for prolonged periods of time. Extensive use of computers and keyboard. Occasional walking and lifting may be required.

Aledade PBC, a public benefit corporation, exists to empower the most transformational part of our health care landscape - independent primary care. We were founded in 2014, and since then, we've become the largest network of independent primary care in the country - helping practices, health centers and clinics deliver better care to their patients and thrive in value-based care. Additionally, by creating value-based contracts across a wide variety of health plans, we aim to flip the script on the traditional fee-for-service model. Our work strengthens continuity of care, aligns incentives and ensures primary care physicians are paid for what they do best - keeping patients healthy. If you want to help create a health care system that is good for patients, good for practices and good for society - and if you're eager to join a collaborative, inclusive and remote-first culture - you've come to the right place.

Flexible work schedules and the ability to work remotely are available for many roles

Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it's a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn't been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

**Overview**

Scout Motors is seeking an Employee Operations Leader to build and lead the infrastructure that powers exceptional employee experiences at scale. This leader will own Scout's HR service delivery, systems ecosystem, and data governance — the operational backbone of the HR function.

As Scout grows, this role will be responsible for ensuring that every employee has seamless access to HR support, that our HR technology is configured and governed to support accurate data and reliable operations, and that our processes are disciplined, efficient, and continuously improving. This leader will partner closely with the Chief Human Resources Officer, HR centers of excellence, IT, Finance, and business leaders to build a high-performing HR operations function fit for a fast-scaling company.

#### **What you'll do**

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

Leadership & Team Development

* Lead, develop, and coach a team spanning HR operations, HR systems architecture, and LMS administration.
* Set a clear vision for HR operations and inspire the team to deliver consistent, high-quality service to employees and people leaders.
* Create a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and operational excellence within the team.
* Partner with the CHRO and HR leadership team to align operational priorities with the broader HR strategy.
* Champion inclusion, collaboration, and Scout's cultural values within the team and across the function.

HR Service Delivery & Operations

* Oversee Scout's HR service delivery model including Tier 0 self-service tools with the use of AI, resources, knowledge bases, and exception-handling protocols.
* Ensure employees and managers have timely, accurate access to HR support and information.
* Set and monitor SLAs, service metrics, and quality standards for HR operations.
* Lead continuous improvement of service delivery processes to improve the employee and people leader experience, with heavy focus on ensuring HR data quality and enabling self service capabilities.
* Manage escalation pathways for complex or sensitive HR inquiries, ensuring consistent and compliant resolution.

HR Systems & Technology

* Own Scout's HR technology ecosystem, including HRIS, LMS, ATS, and potential future talent marketplace platforms.
* Partner with IT, vendors, and HR centers of excellence to evaluate, implement, and optimize HR technologies.
* In collaboration with IT and potentially other vendors, establish agentic AI as the first level of engagement (Tier 0) for employees and people leaders to respond routine inquiries
* Where necessary, establish a workflow for inquiries that require greater consideration and action from HR Partners or other Subject Matter Experts.

* Ensure integrations between HR systems are stable, accurate, and aligned with business needs.
* Stay current on HR technology trends and proactively identify opportunities to modernize or streamline the HR tech stack.

Data, Reporting & Governance

* Own Scout's HR data strategy, reporting infrastructure, and workforce analytics capabilities.
* Establish data governance frameworks, standards, and audit processes that ensure data quality, accuracy, and compliance.
* Partner with Finance, Legal, and business stakeholders to deliver workforce reporting and insights that inform people and organizational decisions.
* Build dashboards and reporting tools that give leaders visibility into the health and performance of the workforce.

* This role will be based out of the **Scout Motors corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC**.

#### **What you'll bring**

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You'll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You'll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

* Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree, MBA, or advanced HR-related degree preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive HR experience with significant experience in HR operations, HRIS, or shared services leadership.

* Strong analytical skills and comfort with HR data, metrics, reporting, and business intelligence tools.
* Experience managing cro$180,000.00 - $220,000.00s-functional projects and leading teams through technology implementations or process change.
* Exceptional organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to balance strategic vision with hands-on operational execution.
* Demonstrated grit, curiosity, and resourcefulness in navigating ambiguity, solving complex problems, and turning obstacles into practical, scalable solutions.
* High integrity, sound judgment, and a commitment to inclusion, fairness, and respect.

**About David AI**
------------------

At David AI, our vision is to bring impactful AI into billions of lives through voice. Our mission is to help the world's leading AI companies build better voice models and agents. We're building the data and evaluation infrastructure behind those models.

Founded in 2024, we're a fast-growing Series B company backed by NVIDIA, Meritech, First Round, YC, and others, with ~70 people across San Francisco and New York City.

**About our Data Operations team**
----------------------------------

Our Data Operations team powers David AI's Data Factory, transforming raw audio into high-quality training datasets for leading AI labs. Our mandate is to spin up new data pipelines and run them at a massive scale.

This means starting from a model capability we want a model to unlock, experimenting with different shapes of data and collection strategies, and validating them with researchers. Once an approach works, we industrialize it, building pipelines that can process audio with reliability, quality, and efficiency. We are relentless operators who thrive in ambiguity, equally comfortable prototyping novel workflows as we are managing large-scale production systems.

**About this role**
-------------------

As **General Manager of Data Operations** at David AI, you will lead one of the most critical functions at David AI. You’ll own a major slice of our Data Factory: the engine that powers high-quality, scalable data production. You’ll lead the team responsible for building and scaling pipelines, from 0 1 experiments that unlock new model capabilities to 1 N industrialization that processes data reliably and efficiently.

**In this role, you will**
--------------------------

**Ingram Content Group (ICG)**is hiring a **Sr. Manager Operations** to support our **Distribution** team in **Jackson, TN**. The Sr. Manager, Operations manages the daily operations of an assigned area within the Distribution Center and serves as a key partner to the Director, Operations. Want to join a key team that helps the world read?

At Ingram, the Operations team serves a key role within the organization. We ensure that our distribution centers and manufacturing facilities function at maximum efficiency. Safety is a core value in our operations environment. We emphasize this through training, education, and accident prevention programs. Process Improvement is another core value, and through innovations such as voice and Radio Frequency (RF) technologies, as well as feedback from our associates, we work toward constant improvement.

records.description:
As the
**Director of Quality**
, you will lead the quality strategy and continuous improvement efforts across all Bison manufacturing sites. You will be responsible for ensuring that the products meet or exceed customer expectations, industry standards, and regulatory requirements while driving overall quality performance and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to establish and maintain effective quality systems, drive process improvements, and ensure compliance with industry certifications.
  
  
This position can be based at either our
**Whitsett, NC**
or
**Reynosa, MX**
facility.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
  
  

* Leadership & Strategy

+ Develop and execute a strategic quality plan in alignment with business unit goals.
+ Lead, mentor, and develop a team of quality professionals across two locations, ensuring consistency in processes and objectives.
+ Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

* Quality Management Systems (QMS)

+ Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and improvement of the QAD Elements QMS and other relevant Quality Management Systems at both locations. Ensure compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry-specific quality standards (e.g., FDA, ISO, AS9100, etc.).
+ Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of quality management systems and propose enhancements to improve overall performance.

* Process & Product Quality

+ Collaborate with sales, operations, engineering, and supply chain teams to identify drive resolution of quality issues, ensuring process and product integrity.
+ Support root cause analysis and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) for internal and external quality issues.
+ Oversee first article inspections, process capability studies, and validation/qualification activities to ensure robust manufacturing processes.

* Continuous Improvement

+ Lead Lean Six Sigma or other continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing defects, enhancing efficiency, and improving overall quality.
+ Implement data-driven decision-making tools (e.g., SPC, FMEA, Control Plans) to monitor and improve process capabilities.
+ Facilitate cross-functional value stream mapping sessions and quality workshops to drive process improvements.

* Customer & Supplier Relations

+ Serve as the main point of contact for customer quality issues, audits, and feedback, ensuring timely and effective resolution.
+ Oversee supplier quality management, including audits, performance monitoring, and supplier development initiatives.

* Metrics & Reporting

+ Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to quality performance, including scrap/rework, defect rates, customer complaints, and audit findings.
+ Regularly report quality performance metrics to senior leadership, highlighting trends and recommending corrective actions.

* Regulatory Compliance & Audits

+ Lead internal and external audits, ensuring the sites comply with relevant standards and certifications.
+ Ensure the manufacturing facilities are audit-ready at all times and coordinate responses to audit findings.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in quality management within a manufacturing environment, with at least 5 years in a leadership role.
* Demonstrated experience with quality management systems (ISO 9001, AS9100, FDA, or equivalent) and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma).
* Demonstrated ability and willingness to use AI tools to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and to reduce costs. The successful candidate must be able to identify appropriate AI use cases and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.
* Proven track record of driving quality improvements across multi-site operations.
* Ability to travel as needed to the BU manufacturing sites (up to 30%)
* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization.
* Proficiency in quality tools such as SPC, FMEA, 8D, and Root Cause Analysis.

**Compensation**
Employee Type: Salaried
  
  
Currency: USD
  
  
Salary Minimum: 135,000
  
  
Salary Maximum: 185,000
  
  
Incentive: Yes
  
  
Disclaimer: Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.
  
  
For more information on AMETEK's competitive benefits, please click here.

**Summary**
Provides strategic leadership and direction for the Quality organization, ensuring that quality systems, processes, and practices support business objectives, customer requirements, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence. Establishes quality strategy, policies, objectives, and performance expectations and provides leadership across functions to drive continuous improvement, strengthen quality performance, mitigate risk, and support business growth.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and direction for the Quality organization, establishing priorities, objectives, and performance expectations aligned with business and operational goals.
* Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the site's Quality Management System and associated quality policies, procedures, and controls.
* Serve as the site's senior quality leader and management representative for applicable ISO 9001, AS9100, and ISO 13485 quality management systems.
* Ensure continued compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, industry, and certification requirements, including applicable FDA, ITAR, ISO, and IPC requirements and standards.
* Provide leadership for quality planning related to processes, products, customers, and business requirements, with consideration for broader corporate quality objectives.
* Establish and monitor quality metrics and performance indicators. Identify trends, risks, and systemic issues and lead actions to improve quality performance.
* Provide quality performance, risk, and improvement recommendations to site and organizational leadership.
* Lead the Material Review Board (MRB) process and provide oversight for the disposition and control of nonconforming material and product.
* Provide leadership and oversight for corrective and preventive actions, root cause analysis, and systemic problem resolution in partnership with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and other functions.
* Lead quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, improving process capability, increasing throughput, and strengthening overall operational performance.
* Drive a culture of continuous improvement and quality ownership throughout the organization.
* Provide oversight of internal and external audit activities, certification requirements, customer audits, and resulting corrective actions.
* Partner with Supply Chain and suppliers to evaluate supplier quality performance, address quality risks, and ensure supplier quality systems meet business and customer requirements.
* Oversee the calibration system and applicable preventive maintenance controls to ensure compliance and effectiveness.
* Ensure appropriate training and organizational capability related to workmanship standards, acceptance criteria, quality systems, and regulatory/customer requirements.
* Support environmental management requirements, including applicable ISO 14001 responsibilities and site environmental management activities.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Program Management, and other functions to identify and mitigate quality and operational risks and improve customer outcomes.
* Provide quality leadership and expertise in support of new products, customers, programs, processes, and business opportunities.
* Promote awareness and understanding of regulatory, customer, and quality requirements throughout the organization.
* Lead, develop, and mentor Quality leaders and team members, building organizational capability and ensuring appropriate talent development and succession planning.
* Support corporate and site Lean/6S objectives and integrate quality principles into continuous improvement initiatives.
* Support and follow all applicable Quality Management System requirements related to quality, environmental, health, safety, and security.
* Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

**Job Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Advanced knowledge of quality management systems and quality principles within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485, and other applicable regulatory and customer quality requirements.
* Working knowledge of FDA, ITAR, IPC, and applicable electronics manufacturing standards and requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to translate business objectives into quality strategies, priorities, metrics, and improvement initiatives.
* Strong knowledge of corrective action, root cause analysis, risk management, process improvement, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Ability to analyze quality and operational data, identify trends and systemic risks, and develop effective corrective and preventive strategies.
* Strong business acumen with the ability to balance quality, customer, operational, financial, and business considerations.
* Demonstrated ability to influence decisions and drive results across functions without relying solely on direct authority.
* Strong leadership and organizational capability, including experience building, developing, and leading professional and technical teams.
* Ability to communicate effectively with customers, regulatory bodies, auditors, suppliers, and senior leadership.
* Strong written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and applicable electronic manufacturing and quality systems.

**Experience/Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Operations, or a related technical discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible quality, engineering, or manufacturing experience, including significant leadership responsibility.
* Demonstrated experience leading a quality organization within a complex manufacturing environment.
* Experience managing multiple concurrent technical, quality, and operational priorities.
* Demonstrated experience influencing cross-functional leaders and driving organization-wide quality and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience interacting with customers, auditors, regulatory organizations, and senior business leadership.
* Demonstrated balance of strategic thinking, strong analytical capability, and effective execution.
* Strong business judgment, attention to detail, and written and verbal communication skills.

records.description:
**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.
  
  

* Perform all documentation in compliance with ALCOA++ principles and site SOPs.
* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
* Minimum 5–10 years of mid to senior management experience in a manufacturing or process environment
* Demonstrated understanding of the responsibilities and functions of key departments within a pharmaceutical or industrial manufacturing facility
* Strong knowledge of cGMP compliance, technical operations, and quality systems within a manufacturing environment
* Proven ability to identify, develop, and inspire leaders at multiple levels of the organization
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to present strategy and performance clearly to site and functional leadership

**Preferred**

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

**Physical Requirements**
The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**
The work environment characteristics described below are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of this role.
  
  

* Regular work in a standard office environment, with frequent entry into the production area of a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility.
* Production environment may include moving mechanical parts, fumes or airborne particles, extreme heat, wet or humid conditions, low levels of toxic or caustic chemicals, and outdoor weather conditions.
* Noise level in the work environment is typically moderate.

records.title: Director of Manufacturing Operations, AD&S
records.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
  
  
**About The Role**
We’re hiring a Director of Manufacturing Operations to oversee all production within our Air Dominance & Strike division, from rapidly maturing prototypes through full-rate production at scale.
  
  
In this role, you will be responsible for managing a team of highly talented managers, line supervisors, and technicians who manufacture both our current key autonomous products, Fury, Barracuda, and Roadrunner, and our emerging capabilities. This is a highly dynamic role that requires both technical and frontline people management skills. This role is at the forefront of delivering exceptional customer experiences, fostering team development, and overseeing operations at Arsenal-01 and HQ.
  
  
As a Director in the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization, you must be a technical leader with the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. This role is crucial in ensuring that both manufacturing sites and operations align with the division's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, in addition to balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's manufacturing operational success.
  
  
Success in this role demands consistent achievement across hardware production, team management, manufacturing operations, and financial goals. The ideal candidate combines technical acumen with effective communication, strong time-management skills, and a passion for leading transformative change. The ideal candidate should be energetic, highly organized, and deeply committed to scaling innovative products. While individual contributions are valued, teamwork is crucial for achieving the highest level of success while maintaining our Anduril culture above all.
  
  
*Please note: This role will be based at Arsenal-01 in Columbus, OH. A successful candidate will be expected to work out of Columbus, OH. Based on eligibility, relocation assistance may be available. There will likely be 25% - 50% travel required for the role.*
**What You'll Do**

* First and foremost, deliver outcomes for the Air Dominance & Strike Production organization
* Create a clear vision for Manufacturing Operations

+ You are a key leader in supporting and strengthening the vision of AD&S Production
+ Manage the portfolio of projects necessary to achieve your vision for Manufacturing Operations

* Collaborate successfully with leaders across our production organization

+ Leaders include Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Planning, Quality, and Supply Chain

* Deliver quality products, on-time and at cost

+ Own attainment for both current and emerging programs

* Own the culture on the floor

+ Be a stakeholder in all programs, policies, etc. that affect life on the floor
+ Maximize for what’s right both for Anduril’s future and maintaining a strong team culture
+ Coach, mentor and support Manufacturing Operations Managers and Production Supervisors
+ Create and maintain a high bar for excellence

* Clearly communicate up and out

+ Provide consistent and high-quality briefs both up, to Anduril Senior Leadership, and out, to AD&S Customers

* In summary, show up every day with a high level of urgency, ownership, and enthusiasm to get the job done

**Required Qualifications**

* 6+ years experience managing manufacturing and production operations
* 3+ years in a supervisor or production operations management role at the Director level or above
* 3+ years of experience as a manager of managers
* Experience managing operator / technician workforce of 100+ within direct organization
* Experience working directly and communicating with designers and engineers
* A full understanding of the product life cycle (NPI to scaled production), LEAN manufacturing principles, and change management
* Extremely reliable, organized, and detail-oriented with excellent verbal & written communication skills
* You have a passion for employee development and enjoy the process of training and developing both new hires and veteran production staff
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor or Master’s degree in a technical field (engineering, business, or applied science)
* Working knowledge of AS9100 standards and OSHA laws

US Salary Range
  
  
$190,000—$252,000 USD
  
  
**Benefits**
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
  
  
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.
*For more information, Explore Our Benefits.*
**Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
  
  
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
  
  

* No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

* What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

**Data Privacy**

records.description:
**Company Information**
*At Richelieu Foods, we are dedicated to a culture of belonging for everyone. Driven by our values of ownership, respect, and growth, we put people, safety, and quality above all else -- delicious pizza, outstanding service, and solid customer relationships are what happens as a result.*
*Richelieu Foods, Inc. is a leading national private label and contract packing food manufacturer focused on frozen pizza. We have two manufacturing facilities located in IL and WI. We provide products to many national retailers, wholesalers, distributors, club and mass stores, as well as industrial accounts including other food manufacturers.*
**Job Summary**
At Richelieu Foods we are making Great Food from Great People. We are looking for an experienced Director of Plant Operations who is comfortable driving transformation while reinforcing a culture of support and development. The Director of Plant Operations will report directly to the Senior Director of Operations with significant exposure to the Richelieu Senior Leadership Team. The Director of Plant Operations will lead the manufacturing operations for the facility, producing quality products in a people and food-safe manner, at or below budgeted cost. The position will be responsible for ensuring plant operations follow all regulatory, quality and safety standards. This role will be responsible for driving continuous improvement initiatives, striving to deliver zero loss and 100% employee engagement in support of Richelieu’s integrated manufacturing strategy.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Create a high-performance operations team by recruiting and developing teams with an appropriate mix of experience, capabilities, and skills to consistently meet company goals and departmental initiatives in the most cost-effective manner. Ensure effective succession planning for all pivotal positions.
* Create and efficiently manage four key divisions of operations: 1) Manufacturing 2) Maintenance 3) Materials and 4) Operational excellence. Understand the financial impacts of various sourcing, labor, materials and overhead strategies on the business and act accordingly to maximize returns.
* Support new projects for the business, engaging suppliers to help the team understand any costs and design implication. Ability to engage and collaborate cross-functionally to facilitate commercialization of new products and partnering closely with the leadership team to support the broader activities and initiatives.
* Manage KPI's to include (but not limited to): Safety, Quality, People, Service, and Cost
* Manage technology and process improvement projects to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the operations function.
* Plan, organize and direct the manufacturing operations ensuring the plant meets the daily production schedule, producing products that meet or exceed established standards.
* Establish and communicate clear metric targets and results. Develop and execute plans that drive improved operational performance.
* Participate in the development, implementation & evaluation of business goals that deliver strategic business objectives.
* Develop and execute job training programs that build the capability of the factory and leadership team members, including skill-based pay for the factory team and succession planning for the leadership team.
* Teach and deploy lean six-sigma tools such as daily direction setting, 5S, equipment center lining, defect handling and root cause failure analysis that drive towards zero loss and 100% employee engagement.
* Manage budget and cost controls considering changes in demand (volume), business seasonality and required service levels.
* Identify manufacturing cost drivers and proactively adjust manpower and department expenses to achieve budget commitments.
* Daily focus on yields with a particular focus on raw and pack materials. Actively participate in the KPI calls to report on results and improvement plans.
* Ensure the plant meets OSHA requirements and continually improve safety record by addressing both physical safety issues as well as employee safety attitudes. Cultivate a safety culture. Ensure compliance with all food regulatory requirements and adherence to food safety and GMP's.
* Maintain superior scores on all SQF or other third-party audits (customer driven).
* Ensure all products meet product specifications and consumer / customer complaints are fully investigated and addressed.
* Participate in the development of the strategic plan for the factory including the development of the annual operating budget and quarterly forecasts.
* Inspire the team and be the voice of the company’s core values, to motivate and capture personal commitment in creating a pathway to both their individual and our collective long-term success and growth.
* Develop a strong discipline of role clarity and hold self and team members accountable for performance and collaboration with the whole enterprise establishing and maintaining an inclusive and diverse culture that provides a positive employee experience and ensuring proactive performance management based on feedback, coaching and mentoring.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive operations experience in a high volume, high growth, food manufacturing environment
* 5+ years of management experience
* Formal training in all aspects of SQF, Food Safety & Quality, FDA’s FSMA program, including Food Safety, Good Manufacturing Practices, Food Plant Sanitation, FDA Regulations and AIB.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* USDA Experience preferred.

**Essential Skills And Abilities**

* Superior analytical skills to anticipate manufacturing requirements and develop contingency plans that eliminate or reduce disruption to operations.
* Strong time management and organizational skills with the ability to deliver to deadlines with strong follow-up skills, problem resolution, and strategic thinking.
* Excellent communication and presentation skills (written and verbal) and the ability to interact with all levels of the organization.
* Demonstrated leadership ability with highly effective interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to resolve conflicting interests and obtain cooperation.
* Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to respond to changing situations despite deadlines and pressure.
* Strong Food and Safety knowledge including legal compliance of federal, state and local food and safety laws and regulations.
* Excellent Team-building skills and possess the ability to gain consensus and deliver results with and through people.
* Ability to provide clear direction.

**Working Conditions**

* On-Site: This role requires 100% onsite attendance to perform the essential functions of the role

**Pay And Benefits**
The following information is provided in accordance with applicable state and local laws. Compensation is based on experience, geographic locations, and other legally permitted factors. The expected compensation range for this role is $170,000 and $200,000. This role is also eligible for an annual incentive plan bonus.
  
  
Benefits for this role include medical, dental, and vision insurance; pre-tax spending accounts; 401K with company match; paid time off; short-term and long-term disability; and life insurance.
  
  
**Disclosures**
This job description is not intended, nor should it be construed to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, skills, or working conditions associated with the job. It is intended only to be a general description of the essential functions common to positions of this type.

**Redmond-Bend, OR**
area is seeking a

records.title: Director of Manufacturing
records.description:
Director of Manufacturing

  
POSITION SUMMARY
  

Weaver Popcorn is seeking an experienced manufacturing leader to direct the
**Malden, Missouri**
operation and strengthen safety, quality, service, cost performance, throughput, and associate development. The Director of Manufacturing provides strategic and hands-on leadership for plant operations, maintenance, sanitation, scheduling, grower partnership, and continuous improvement while ensuring reliable execution of annual operating priorities.

  

This leader will establish clear performance expectations, develop plant leadership and frontline capability, optimize equipment and labor effectiveness, and partner across Quality, Field Operations, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, and Continuous Improvement to deliver sustainable operational and financial results.

  
HOW WILL YOU HELP US GROW?Manufacturing & Operational Leadership
  

  
* Lead the Malden manufacturing operation with accountability for safety, quality, service, cost, throughput, schedule attainment, sanitation, labor effectiveness, and overall plant performance.
  
* Establish clear operational standards, performance goals, equipment expectations, and operating cost objectives aligned with the annual plan.
  
* Drive reliable production output and efficient growth by ensuring the right equipment, staffing, operating systems, and performance measures are in place.
  
* Lead regular operating reviews with plant leadership to evaluate productivity, downtime, quality, staffing, schedule attainment, and corrective actions.
  
* Ensure manufacturing systems, procedures, and policies are consistently deployed, understood, and followed across assigned operations.
  
* Align internal manufacturing capabilities with customer needs, production schedules, raw-material availability, and growth expectations.
  

  
Safety, Quality & Food Manufacturing Compliance
  

  
* Provide visible leadership for a safe workplace and hold leaders accountable for proactive hazard identification, corrective action, training, and compliance.
  
* Partner closely with Quality leadership to ensure compliance with food safety and quality requirements, including HACCP, GMPs, sanitation standards, product controls, and applicable regulatory and customer requirements.
  
* Support disciplined investigation and sustainable corrective action for safety events, quality deviations, operational failures, customer concerns, and recurring performance issues.
  
* Ensure plant practices support audit readiness, traceability, sanitation effectiveness, and consistent production of safe, conforming product.
  
* Reinforce the authority and responsibility to stop or correct work when safety, food safety, quality, or regulatory requirements are not being met.
  

  
Continuous Improvement, Reliability & Capital
  

  
* Deploy Lean manufacturing, Statistical Process Control, and structured problem-solving methods to improve throughput, yield, reliability, labor efficiency, and cost performance.
  
* Identify operational failures and constraints, establish root causes, implement corrective actions, and verify sustained effectiveness.
  
* Develop and maintain meaningful manufacturing KPIs and equipment-efficiency measures that support timely, fact-based decisions.
  
* Partner with Maintenance and plant leaders to improve equipment reliability, preventive maintenance effectiveness, space utilization, and production capacity.
  
* Jointly establish capital expenditure priorities and lead effective execution of approved capital and process-improvement projects.
  
* Challenge existing practices, standardize successful improvements, and build continuous-improvement capability throughout the operation.
  

  
Grower, Supply Chain & Cross-Functional Partnership
  

  
* Collaborate with Field Operations to support grower relationships, contracted acreage plans, raw-material supply, and growth objectives.
  
* Partner with Supply Chain and plant scheduling teams to balance customer requirements, inventory, capacity, labor, and raw-material availability.
  
* Work with Finance and Information Technology to strengthen business processes, operating data, management reporting, budgeting, and decision-support tools.
  
* Contribute the manufacturing perspective to companywide initiatives led by Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, Quality, and other functional leaders.
  
* Communicate operational risks, priorities, tradeoffs, and performance clearly to senior leadership and cross-functional partners.
  

  
People Leadership & Talent Development
  

  
* Lead, coach, and develop plant leaders and assigned functional leaders; establish clear goals, accountabilities, performance expectations, and development plans.
  
* Build a culture of excellence, ownership, accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement at every level of the operation.
  
* Develop internal talent, strengthen succession readiness, and partner with Human Resources to recruit and retain a capable workforce.
  
* Build associate competency through effective training, qualification, coaching, and skills-development programs.
  
* Use a visible, participative leadership style that communicates direction, listens for understanding, addresses conflict directly, and earns followership.
  

  
WHAT DO YOU NEED TO HAVE?
  

  
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Technology, Business, Operations Management, or a related field.
  
* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including at least 10 years in a Plant Manager or comparable senior manufacturing leadership role; food or agricultural processing experience strongly preferred.
  
* Demonstrated success applying Lean manufacturing, Statistical Process Control, root-cause analysis, and structured problem-solving methods to improve throughput, equipment efficiency, labor productivity, yield, and cost performance.
  
* Experience leading workplace safety, food manufacturing quality systems, sanitation, GMPs, HACCP-based programs, and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.
  
* Proven financial acumen, including budgeting, P&L accountability, capital prioritization, and analysis of manufacturing KPIs and cost drivers.
  
* Demonstrated success developing leaders, strengthening organizational capability, managing change, and building accountability in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
  
* Ability to travel regionally approximately 15% and remain available outside normal business hours when operational needs require support.
  

  
Preferred Qualifications
  

  
* Leadership experience in popcorn, corn, grain, ingredient, food processing, or a related agricultural manufacturing environment.
  
* Experience leading capital projects, technical teams, maintenance-reliability programs, and high-engagement employee relations.
  
* Formal training or certification in Lean, Six Sigma, safety, continuous improvement, or project leadership.
  
* Experience partnering directly with growers or agricultural supply networks.
  

  
WHERE & WHEN WILL YOU WORK?
  

This role operates across office, agricultural, warehouse, and food manufacturing environments and requires regular presence in production areas. The typical schedule is Monday through Friday; however, the Director of Manufacturing must be available outside normal business hours, including occasional evenings or weekends, when safety, quality, customer, staffing, equipment, or other operational needs require support. Regional travel of approximately 15% is expected, with additional travel based on business needs.

  
WHAT DOES SUCCESS LOOK LIKE?
  

  
* Strong, sustained performance in safety, quality, service, cost, throughput, schedule attainment, and customer satisfaction.
  
* Improved equipment reliability, operating efficiency, labor effectiveness, yield, and cost performance supported by clear KPIs.
  
* Consistent execution of manufacturing, sanitation, food safety, quality, and operating standards.
  
* Disciplined problem solving that reduces recurring failures and produces measurable, sustained improvement.
  
* A capable and accountable plant leadership team with clear goals, stronger bench strength, and active development plans.
  
* Effective partnership across Quality, Field Operations, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, and Continuous Improvement.
  
* Credible, visible leadership that builds ownership, engagement, and confidence throughout the Malden operation.
  

  
HOW WILL WE HELP YOU GROW?
  

  
* Competitive compensation.
  
* Three weeks of paid time off in the first year.
  
* 401(k) plan with a company match of 100% of employee deferrals up to 10%.
  
* Health, vision, dental, life, and disability insurance beginning the first day of the month following 30 days of employment.
  
* Education reimbursement of up to $15,000 per year.
  

  
EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY
  

Weaver Popcorn is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and associates. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to any status protected by applicable law.

  
  

The role responsibilities are many, various, and not limited to those written in this document.

**Job Description**
The Director of Indium Phosphide (InP) Wafer Fab Operations is responsible for the overall leadership, startup, qualification, and operation of an Indium Phosphide wafer fabrication facility. This executive leadership role will oversee all aspects of manufacturing operations, including technology transfer, process qualification, production ramp, operational readiness, quality, engineering collaboration, workforce development, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Working closely with Engineering, Process Development, Supply Chain, Quality, Facilities, Product Management, and Executive Leadership, the Director will establish and scale world-class manufacturing capabilities while achieving exceptional performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, yield, and customer satisfaction. This role requires a strategic leader with deep semiconductor wafer fabrication experience and a proven track record of successfully launching and operating advanced manufacturing facilities.
  
  
**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic and operational leadership for all wafer fabrication activities, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality manufacturing operations.
* Lead the startup, commissioning, qualification, and operational readiness of a new Indium Phosphide wafer fabrication facility.
* Develop and execute the manufacturing roadmap to support business growth, customer commitments, and capacity expansion.
* Establish operational metrics, production targets, and performance objectives aligned with corporate goals.

records.description:
**About Veeco**
You probably don’t realize it, but what we do at Veeco touches the lives of every person, every day. It’s a bold statement, but it’s true. From the smartphones in our pockets that access the world’s collective knowledge, to the cloud-based services where all that information lives, to high-speed wireless communication and computing power needed to drive artificial intelligence, augmented and virtual reality, gaming and so much more, our technology is all around us.
  
  
We design, develop, manufacture, and service highly complex, cutting-edge machines used by our customers to create the essential devices that drive the digital age, connect the world, and improve the human experience. Along with the world’s leading technology companies, many of which are household names, we help solve their most difficult material science challenges, enabling technologies for a more connected, sustainable, and convenient world.
  
  
We’re looking for material difference-makers to join our growing team. Interested? Learn more at www.veeco.com/careers .
  
  
**Overview**
Veeco is hiring a Director, Manufacturing Operations, who is excellent in execution, accountability, and leadership development. In this role, you’ll lead a manufacturing organization responsible for delivering Veeco's laser annealing and lithography products. The Director of Manufacturing Operations reports directly to the VP of Global Operations and serves as a key member of the San Jose Operations leadership team. This onsite position requires an operations executive with extensive experience leading manufacturing operations with expertise in manufacturing, international supply chain, operations and strategic planning.
  
  
This is a demanding and highly visible role that requires foresight, superb execution in a fast-paced, challenging, high-tech environment, with exceptional organizational development and leadership skills.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Direct the Sub-assembly, Assembly, and Test teams to meet corporate strategies and business objectives in Veeco’s San Jose factory.
* Foster a world-class safety culture with strong focus on proactive safety.
* Achieve world-class quality metrics for in-box and out-of-box quality.
* Take direct accountability for on-time-shipments and meeting customer commitments.
* Establish budget and resource plan for site manufacturing operations.
* Ensure continuing compliance to all quality and safety standards including ISO certifications.
* Develop a world-class organization – training, mentoring, coaching and leading. Critically assess department staff abilities and take action to ensure long-term health, productivity, and a high-performance culture.
* Establish a roadmap for productivity improvements and run continuous improvement/ lean programs.
* Lead Production related quality investigations/improvement plans via structured problem solving/ 8D analysis, and Shift-Left activities.
* Execute product transition plans for both existing and new products including insourcing/outsourcing efforts at both factory and supplier worldwide locations.
* Be a progressive thinker and role model: enable efficiency enhancing tools such as Lean Manufacturing and cycle time reduction through automated test methods to easily detect/correct manufacturing issues.
* Implement and improve Modular Final Test strategy to enable parallel work and cycle time reduction.

**Qualifications**
Bachelor's degree in engineering or operations management and a minimum of 12 years of experience with increasing responsibility in an operations leadership role managing a large organization (>30 people) is required. Experience with Quality Management techniques like Lean, Value Stream Mapping, Six Sigma, 8D with proficiency using data analytics and statistical process control is also required.
  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities**

* Experience with complex capital equipment manufacturing—particularly within semiconductor or related high‑tech industries—is strongly preferred
* Demonstrate situational leadership and understand when to lead or delegate
* Strong financial background coupled with solid business acumen
* Practical mindset relative to manufacturability operations and business processes
* Leverage process discipline and data‑driven insights to ensure high product quality, whether manufacturing is performed internally or through contract manufacturing and supplier partnerships
* Act as a dynamic leader who brings a strong sense of ownership, integrity, and collaboration, with the drive and creativity to deliver results in a fast‑paced environment
* Capable of inspiring others by creating, articulating and implementing a vision for manufacturing
* Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high‑performing teams through thoughtful assessment, recruiting, coaching, mentoring, and ongoing talent development
* Design for Manufacturability (DfM) training/experience a plus
* Experience with SAP and world-class MES systems is a plus
* This position may have occasional domestic and international travel

**Salary And Benefits**
The expected salary range for this position is $182,000-$230,000, plus a bonus opportunity. We will consider your location, experience, and other job-related factors when determining your pay.
**If your salary requirements exceed the advertised range and you remain interested in Veeco, we encourage you to apply or email your resume to**
**recruiting@veeco.com .**

* 401(k) with Company Match
* Holiday, Vacation, and Sick Time
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Commuter Benefits
* Life and Accident Insurance
* Disability Insurance
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Identity Theft Remediation
* Emergency Travel Assistance

Veeco is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, and other legally protected characteristics. Veeco is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities.
  
  
**Notice To Applicants**
All communication about open positions and hiring will come from someone with a @veeco.com email address. You will always have multiple interviews and meet several team members (in-person or virtually) before we present an offer. We may also check references or conduct a background investigation as part of the offer process. * Proficient with personal computers and Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook.

records.description:
The Signal Hill power plant is strategically located in Wichita County, Texas, near the rapidly expanding Dallas/Fort Worth metropolitan area. This 77 MW electric power generation facility utilizes GE gas combustion turbines, along with associated heat recovery steam generators and an ABB steam generator. Signal Hill plays a critical role in supplying power to the ERCOT market during periods of peak demand and supply volatility. The facility was honored with the 2014 Certificate of Recognition by the City of Wichita Falls, Texas, for its outstanding achievements in environmental excellence, including pollution prevention, waste minimization, and water conservation.
  
  
We are seeking an experienced and dedicated Plant Manager to oversee the operations of the Signal Hill power plant. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in power plant management and a commitment to operational excellence, safety, and environmental stewardship. As Plant Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of the facility, while maintaining compliance with all regulatory requirements.
  
  
**Responsibilities:**

* Manage and oversee all aspects of plant operations, including safety, maintenance, production, and personnel management.
* Ensure compliance with all environmental, health, and safety regulations, and promote a culture of safety and environmental responsibility.
* Monitor plant performance and implement strategies to optimize efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness.

**Job Description**
**Please note that this position is not available for visa sponsorship, and we are unable to take over existing employment visa sponsorships.**
TransMedics is transforming organ transplant therapy with the Organ Care System (OCS)—the first portable warm-perfusion platform that keeps donor organs functioning outside the body. It's technology built to give more patients a chance at a transplant, and more transplant teams the confidence to say yes to an organ they'd otherwise have to turn away.
  
  
The
**Sr. Director of Manufacturing Engineering**
is a pivotal leadership role within TransMedics Supply Chain organization, leading Advanced Operations (New Product & Technology Introduction), Sustaining Engineering, Manufacturing (Process) Engineering, and Technical Field Service. Building on TransMedics strong foundation of engineering excellence, this leader will drive the step-change required to enable the company's next phase of growth—ensuring our engineering practices, systems, and infrastructure deliver world-class results, from product quality and reliability to manufacturing performance, efficiency, and scalability.
  
  
This is a build role, not a maintain role. TransMedics growth trajectory demands a leader who can set multi-year transformation strategy and organizational design—while staying close enough to the floor to walk a line, dig into a process deviation, or unblock a launch when it matters. We're looking for someone equally comfortable owning a transformation roadmap and rolling up their sleeves alongside the team. This leader will also play a key role in building the team's reputation as a strong destination for engineering talent—attracting good people and giving them room to grow into bigger roles as the company scales.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the Manufacturing Engineering organization — oversee Advanced Operations, Sustaining Engineering, Manufacturing (Process) Engineering, Technical Field Service, and related functions.
* Drive step-change transformation — advance engineering practices, systems, and infrastructure to enable the next phase of TransMedics growth.
* Ensure world-class quality & performance — deliver excellence in product quality, manufacturing process performance, efficiency, and scalability.
* Advance manufacturing innovation — implement transformational processes using best-in-class development, advanced technologies, automation, and robotic-assisted manufacturing.
* Embed Design for Excellence (DfX) — make DfX, including Design for Manufacturability (DFM), a core enabler of product quality, cost efficiency, and scalability, with a strong focus on simplification and part-count reduction.
* Develop and inspire talent — build and scale a high-performing engineering team while fostering growth, development, and a culture of excellence.
* Stay hands-on — be willing to get into the details on the floor—a process deviation, a line issue, a launch at risk—when the team needs it.
* Position TransMedics as a talent destination — help establish the company as a premier destination for top engineering talent in the U.S.
* Collaborate cross-functionally — partner with peers across R&D, Quality, and the broader Supply Chain organization to support TransMedics mission and strategic goals.

**Strategic Focus Areas**

* Engineering Transformation — deliver step-change improvements in practices, systems, and infrastructure.
* Product Quality & Reliability — ensure world-class outcomes across current and future products, including our hardware fleet.
* Manufacturing Innovation & Scalability — leverage automation, robotics, and advanced processes to scale efficiently.
* Design for Excellence (DfX/DFM) — embed design principles that drive quality, cost efficiency, and simplification (e.g., part-count reduction).
* Talent & Leadership Development — attract, grow, and retain top engineering talent while building a culture of excellence.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration — partner with the broader enterprise to enable TransMedics mission.

**Management Responsibilities**

* Manages a team of direct reports across the verticals referenced above, including performance reviews and professional development planning.
* Oversight of design contractors, co-ops, and interns as needed.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (Biomedical, Mechanical, Electrical, or equivalent).
* 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience in medical devices or other regulated manufacturing environments.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* MBA
* Proven experience leading multi-disciplinary engineering organizations through complex growth and transformation initiatives.
* Demonstrated success in the strategic focus areas above.
* Expertise in regulatory frameworks and compliance systems.
* Experience leveraging technology platforms (MES, ERP, and digital tools) to enhance manufacturing and engineering outcomes.
* Strong financial acumen, project planning, and capital management capabilities.

**Work Environment**

* Office and manufacturing floor environment.

As part of our long-term growth plans, TransMedics is excited to announce our plan to relocate our headquarters (HQ) to Somerville, MA by 2028. We chose this location because we believe it is a place where innovation will thrive. Our new state-of-the-art headquarters is designed to support collaboration, creativity, and discovery. We believe this will be a place where we can continue to do things few thought possible in organ transplantation to help patients.
*Specific timing and role impact may vary.*
TransMedics, Inc. is a commercial-stage medical technology company transforming organ transplant therapy for patients worldwide. Our mission is to help save more patients’ lives by increasing access to viable donor organs for those who are awaiting an organ transplant. To accomplish this mission, we partner closely with transplant stakeholders worldwide and help expand their access to healthy donor organs, while delivering the highest quality technology, service, clinical care and outcomes.
  
  
Driven by a passion for improving patient care, we make the impossible possible and keep our employees at the center of everything we do. Together, we strive to enhance the quality of life for transplant recipients and their families, fostering hope and healing in the journey toward better health.
  
  
**Maximize your potential at TransMedics, Inc.**
www.TransMedics.com
  
  
TransMedics is committed to equitable and transparent compensation. The expected base salary range for this role is $220,600-$314,050, which represents the company’s current good-faith estimate of compensation for this position. Actual salary will depend on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate experience, qualifications, skills, and the specific work location.
