records.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.
  
  
With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.
  
  
The Director of Process Engineering is responsible for leading the development, optimization, and scale-up of manufacturing processes to support Mott Corporation's growth across Semiconductor, Aerospace & Defense, and Industrial markets. This role drives process stability, improves yield and cost performance, and ensures successful industrialization of new products.
  
  
Reporting to senior operations leadership, the Director will lead a team of process engineers and collaborate closely with Operations, R&D, and Quality to deliver reliable, scalable manufacturing processes for highly technical and mission-critical applications.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Market-Aligned Process Development

Lead process engineering efforts aligned to Mott's three core markets, ensuring each manufacturing environment meets its unique requirements:
  
  

* Ultra-high purity, contamination-free manufacturing for Semiconductor customers
* High-reliability and regulated production for Aerospace & Defense programs
* Efficient, scalable production for Industrial markets
* Ensure all processes meet customer, regulatory, and product performance requirements
* Drive alignment between process capability and market-specific technical demands
* Process Optimization & Manufacturing Support

Own process performance metrics and drive continuous improvement across all assigned manufacturing areas:
  
  

* Yield and First Pass Yield (FPY) improvement
* Throughput optimization and cycle time reduction
* Scrap and rework reduction programs
* Lead root cause analysis and structured problem-solving for manufacturing and quality issues
* Standardize and document processes, work instructions, and best practices
* New Product Introduction (NPI) & Scale-Up

Partner with R&D and cross-functional teams to accelerate new product industrialization:
  
  

* Lead Design-for-Manufacturability (DFM) reviews and production readiness activities
* Support transition from R&D to production, ensuring robust and repeatable processes
* Implement and enforce APQP, PFMEA, and process validation disciplines
* Collaborate across functions to accelerate time-to-market for new programs
* Process Capability & Technology Development

**Drive Advancement Of Core Manufacturing Technologies**

* Develop and improve manufacturing processes in advanced materials processing (e.g., powder metals, sintering, purification)
* Optimize precision machining and fabrication capabilities
* Enhance cleaning and assembly processes for high-spec environments
* Support evaluation and implementation of new equipment, tooling, and automation
* Drive continuous improvement in process capability and repeatability
* Continuous Improvement & Performance Management
* Lead Lean and Six Sigma initiatives to improve productivity and reduce cost
* Establish process KPI dashboards and drive accountability to performance targets
* Identify and execute cost-out and efficiency improvement initiatives
* Team Leadership & Development
* Lead, coach, and develop a team of Process Engineers
* Build technical capabilities aligned to Semiconductor, A&D, and Industrial needs
* Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement
* Partner with leadership to recruit and retain top technical talent
* Cross-Functional Collaboration

**This Role Demands Tight Integration With The Broader Organization**

* Operations — support daily manufacturing execution and escalation resolution
* R&D / Engineering — ensure smooth technology transfer and DFM alignment
* Quality — ensure process control, validation, and regulatory compliance
* Engage in customer-facing technical discussions for complex applications as needed

**Key Performance Metrics**
Success in this role will be measured against the following metrics:
  
  
**Key Metric Description**
**Yield / FPY Improvement**
First Pass Yield targets across Semiconductor, A&D, and Industrial lines
  
  
**Process Capability (Cp/Cpk)**
Statistical process control where applicable; drives repeatability
  
  
**Cycle Time Reduction**
Throughput improvements and bottleneck elimination
  
  
**Scrap & Cost Reduction**
Waste elimination via Lean and Six Sigma initiatives
  
  
**NPI Launch Success & Speed**
On-time, on-spec new product introductions with validated processes
  
  
**Process Stability & Repeatability**
Standardized work instructions and documented best practices
  
  
**Qualifications**
Required Qualifications
  
  

* 10–15 years of progressive experience in process engineering within a manufacturing environment
* Proven experience in at least one of the following sectors:
* Semiconductor or high-purity manufacturing
* Aerospace & Defense or regulated production environments
* Advanced industrial / engineered product manufacturing
* Strong background in process development, scale-up, and industrialization
* Demonstrated expertise in root cause analysis and structured problem-solving (e.g., 8D, DMAIC)
* Hands-on experience with continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma)
* Proven track record of leading and developing technical engineering teams
* Experience with APQP, PFMEA, and process validation disciplines

**Preferred Experience**

* Exposure to multiple target markets (Semiconductor, A&D, and Industrial) within a single organization
* Familiarity with filtration, flow control, or advanced materials products
* Experience in cleanroom or contamination-sensitive process environments
* Background in highly regulated or high-spec production settings
* Experience operating within multi-site or global manufacturing organizations
* Advanced degree (M.S. or MBA) in a relevant engineering or business discipline

**Leadership Attributes**
**The Successful Candidate Will Demonstrate The Following Characteristics**
**Execution-Focused**
Drives tangible process improvements with measurable, trackable outcomes
  
  
**Technically Strong**
Capable of diagnosing and solving complex, multi-variable manufacturing challenges
  
  
**Hands-On Leader**
Engages directly with the factory floor and engineering teams — not a remote leader
  
  
**Collaborative**
Works effectively across functions; builds trust with Operations, R&D, and Quality peers
  
  
**Continuous Improvement Mindset**
Relentlessly improves processes and performance; never satisfied with the status quo
  
  
**Talent Builder**
Invests in the growth and development of team members at all levels
  
  
**About Mott Corporation**
Mott Corporation is a global leader in the design and manufacture of precision porous metal products and advanced filtration solutions. With decades of innovation, Mott serves customers across the most demanding markets — including Semiconductor, Aerospace & Defense, Life Sciences, and Industrial applications — where performance, purity, and reliability are non-negotiable.
  
  
Mott's manufacturing capabilities include advanced powder metallurgy, sintering, precision machining, and controlled-environment assembly — making process engineering a strategic and highly visible function within the organization.
  
  
This is an opportunity to join a company where engineering excellence directly translates to customer and business outcomes — and where the Director of Process Engineering plays a central role in that value chain.
  
  
**Mott Corporation is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.**
Are you ready to join a different kind of company where our people, our culture, and our commitments are centered around providing trusted solutions that improve lives around the world?
  
  
**Total Rewards**

**Benefits Package**
Our comprehensive U.S. benefit offerings include: Health benefits, 401(k) retirement savings program with company match, PTO, and more. More information on our benefits and rewards can be found on our career page: https://www.idexcorp.com/careers/our-benefits-and-rewards/

records.description:
At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com . Follow us on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and Instagram .
  
  
**Welcome to BWXT**
We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.
  
  
**Position Overview: Director of Engineering – Enrichment Operations**
As the Director of Engineering for BWXT Enrichment Operations, you will lead the full engineering function responsible for delivering a production‑ready centrifuge product and a high‑precision, highly automated factory capability. You will oversee engineering strategy from early concept through prototype/pilot phases to full‑rate production, establishing core systems engineering and systems integration practices to ensure disciplined requirements management, interface control, verification/validation, and seamless subsystem integration. This role is pivotal in standing up a modern digital factory, enabling high‑volume production with aerospace‑grade quality and nuclear regulatory rigor.
  
  
**Location**
On-site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee
  
  
**Your Day-to-Day as the Director of Engineering**
Engineering Leadership & Organization
  
  

* Build, scale, and lead a multidisciplinary engineering organization spanning manufacturing, process, facilities, automation, industrialization, and precision systems.
* Serve as the technical authority for manufacturability, scalability, risk management, and readiness.

Systems Engineering (SE)
  
  

* Establish a modern systems engineering capability that includes requirements management, architecture development, interface control (ICDs), configuration management, verification and validation, and model-based systems engineering/digital thread practices.
* Define “Definition of Done” at each development gate and ensure complete, build-ready Product Readiness Packs (e.g., BOMs, routers, test plans).

Systems Integration (SI)
  
  

* Lead end‑to‑end integration of subsystems into the centrifuge product and supporting systems.
* Develop integration plans, lab capabilities, fixtures, and test regimes to validate subsystem and system-level performance.
* Collaborate with the CTO and ORNL Design Authority to align qualification evidence and change packages; support seamless integration with CMDF pilot builds and transfer to CMF industrialization.

Factory Design, Construction & Startup
  
  

* Lead design, build, and commissioning of a high‑precision manufacturing facility.
* Integrate automation, robotics, and digital factory systems to enable high throughput, traceability, and tightly controlled processes.

Manufacturing Excellence & DFx
  
  

* Deliver engineering solutions capable of automotive‑pace production with aerospace‑grade quality.
* Drive design for manufacturability, assembly, quality, cost, and industrialization (DFM/DFA/DFQ/DFC).

Quality, Safety & Compliance
  
  

* Ensure all engineering designs and processes meet nuclear regulatory, DOE, safety, and BWXT quality requirements.
* Embed compliance gates, audit readiness, and pre‑release checks throughout development.

Program Controls & Schedule
  
  

* Partner with Business Operations and Program Controls to maintain a resource‑loaded critical path schedule.
* Support earned value management (EVM) discipline and weekly KPI reviews (SPI/CPI, cost variance, schedule adherence).

Supply Chain & Technical Readiness
  
  

* Define technical acceptance criteria for supplier parts, processes, tooling, and special manufacturing steps.
* Support supplier onboarding speed, delivery performance, and technical readiness to protect schedule-critical components.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
  
  

* Work closely with CMDF (prototype/pilot operations), CMF (full-rate industrialization), the CTO/Technology organization, and Operations.
* Drive the transition from low‑rate initial production (LRIP) to full‑rate production (FRP) on cost and schedule.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (advanced degree preferred).
* Fifteen (15+) years of progressive engineering leadership in high‑precision, highly regulated manufacturing environments (nuclear, aerospace, defense, automotive, semiconductor, or similar).
* Demonstrated experience designing, building, commissioning, and scaling a high‑precision manufacturing facility to high‑volume production.
* Strong expertise in advanced manufacturing, automation, precision machining, assembly, metrology, and inspection systems.
* Must be a U.S. citizen capable of obtaining and maintaining a DOE Q clearance; active clearance preferred.
* Proven ability to lead large, multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced, highly technical environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with automotive‑scale manufacturing and assembly; Lean/Six Sigma leadership.
* Hands-on experience deploying Industry 4.0, digital thread, digital twin, and smart factory systems.
* Experience guiding organizations from prototype/pilot phases to high‑rate production in startup‑like or greenfield environments.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive compensation and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.
* Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance (as applicable).
* Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs, leadership training, and support for continuing education.
* An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates diverse perspectives and enables collaboration across all generations.
* The opportunity to shape a mission‑driven organization advancing the future of energy and national security.
* Continuous learning and development opportunities to support long‑term career growth.

records.description:
**The Role**
Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.
  
  
Moderna is strengthening its presence in Norwood, Massachusetts, a cornerstone of our manufacturing and operational excellence. Our Norwood campus translates mRNA science into scalable impact, supporting the global delivery of our medicines. We welcome talent ready to drive innovation and make a meaningful difference for patients worldwide.
  
  
This is an opportunity to lead at the intersection of DNA Manufacturing, Cell Bank operations, Operational Excellence, technology transfer, quality, digital capability, and manufacturing performance, helping translate complex technical and business priorities into reliable execution.
  
  
You will lead a highly capable team while owning the continuous improvement agenda for DNA Manufacturing, using operational data, structured problem solving, and cross-functional leadership to identify risks, unlock capacity, strengthen processes, and deliver sustainable improvements.
  
  
As a member of the DNA Leadership Team, you will influence priorities beyond your immediate function, solve complex and ambiguous challenges across organizational boundaries, and help build the manufacturing capabilities, culture, and digital ways of working needed for the next stage of Moderna’s operations.
  
  
**Here’s What You’ll Do**

* Lead, develop, and coach a team of Specialists and Senior Specialists with broad expertise across DNA and Cell Bank manufacturing processes, building a highly capable and adaptable team that can address evolving operational priorities.
* Own and continuously improve the DNA Manufacturing continuous improvement and Operational Excellence program, including the identification, prioritization, execution, and benefits realization of improvement opportunities.
* Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning DNA Manufacturing and partner organizations, establishing clear objectives, governance, execution plans, decision-making mechanisms, and accountability for delivery.
* Own the strategy and execution of manufacturing change controls associated with area improvements, ensuring changes are effectively planned, assessed, implemented, embedded, and sustained within manufacturing operations.
* Provide manufacturing leadership and execution support for technology transfers, serving as the Manufacturing representative, coordinating manufacturing readiness activities, and providing project management across cross-functional teams to enable successful transfer and execution.
* Lead the use of operational data, performance indicators, manufacturing trends, and operational insights to proactively identify emerging risks, improvement opportunities, capacity constraints, and priorities for DNA Operations.
* Establish and continuously evolve effective operational performance management mechanisms, including dashboards, routine performance reviews, action tracking, and escalation processes for emerging issues.
* Serve as a GMP leader and manufacturing subject matter expert, providing support for investigations, operational events, risk assessments, change implementation, and other quality system activities as required.
* Partner closely with Manufacturing Science & Technology (MSAT), Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Digital, CMC Development, Planning, and other stakeholders to integrate technical, quality, supply, and business priorities into effective manufacturing execution.
* Support the organization’s ongoing state of inspection readiness, ensuring the team, processes, documentation, change activity, and improvements within the role’s scope are prepared to effectively support regulatory inspections.
* Build organizational capability in continuous improvement, structured problem solving, project execution, data-driven decision making, and change management, strengthening the organization’s ability to respond effectively to evolving manufacturing needs.
* Serve as a member of the DNA Leadership Team, contributing to strategy, organizational priorities, operational performance, workforce engagement, and the resolution of issues affecting the broader DNA Operations organization.
* Foster a positive, collaborative, accountable, and inclusive working culture across DNA Manufacturing, acting as a visible leader and role model while supporting the overall performance and well-being of the organization.
* Act as a trusted advisor and problem solver for DNA Operations leadership, proactively identifying opportunities and taking ownership of complex or ambiguous challenges that cross traditional functional and organizational boundaries.
* Work with Digital and cross-functional partners to explore how Generative AI and other advanced digital tools can strengthen operational insights, structured problem solving, knowledge access, performance management, and decision making, while operating within appropriate manufacturing, quality, and data-governance requirements.
* Drive success through the team’s ability to execute complex initiatives, deliver sustainable improvements, effectively manage change, enable successful technology transfers, use data proactively to identify opportunities and risks, and continuously strengthen the capability and overall performance of DNA Manufacturing.

**The key Moderna Mindsets you’ll need to succeed in the role:**

* “We act with dynamic range, driving strategy and execution at the same time at every step.”
* “We digitize everywhere possible using the power of code to maximize our impact on patients.”

**Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, manufacturing, or another relevant technical discipline or an equivalent combination of education and relevant industry experience.
* Demonstrated experience in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, technical operations, manufacturing sciences, operational excellence, or a related environment.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop people, including creating clarity, setting priorities, coaching performance, and building organizational capability.
* Proven ability to influence and lead effectively within a complex matrix organization, including situations where successful execution requires alignment of stakeholders outside the individual's direct authority.
* Demonstrated ownership and successful execution of complex, cross-functional projects or programs, from problem definition and strategy through implementation and sustained results.
* Experience with GMP manufacturing and quality systems, including change control and other mechanisms used to implement and sustain changes in a regulated environment.
* Experience supporting technology transfer, manufacturing readiness, process implementation, or other cross-functional technical programs.
* Strong understanding of continuous improvement and operational excellence principles, with demonstrated ability to translate them into measurable improvements in manufacturing performance.
* Demonstrated ability to use data, trends, and performance indicators to identify problems, establish priorities, and drive decisions and improvement.
* Strong communication, stakeholder management, and organizational leadership skills, with the ability to communicate effectively from the manufacturing floor through senior leadership.
* Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity, connect technical and business considerations, and take ownership of problems that do not fit neatly within traditional functional boundaries.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and inspection readiness activities preferred.

**Schedule:**
Monday–Friday; flexibility may be required to support critical manufacturing activities, technology transfers, regulatory inspections, or significant operational events.
  
  
**Our Working Model**
As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model.
  
  
This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.
  
  
Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.
  
  
**Pay & Benefits**
**At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work.**
**That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.**

* Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
* A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
* Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
* Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
* Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
* Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $130,800.00 - $209,400.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.
  
  
**About Moderna**
Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.
  
  
By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.
  
  
We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.
  
  
If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.
  
  
**Equal Opportunities**
Moderna is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry or citizenship, ethnicity, disability, military or protected veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital or familial status, or any other personal characteristic protected under applicable law. Moderna is a place where everyone can grow. If you meet the Basic Qualifications for the role and you would be excited to contribute to our mission every day, please apply!
  
  
Moderna is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. We consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.
  
  
**Accommodations**
We’re focused on attracting, retaining, developing, and advancing our employees. By cultivating a workplace that values diverse experiences, backgrounds, and ideas, we create an environment where every employee can contribute their best.
  
  
Moderna is committed to offering reasonable accommodations to qualified job applicants with disabilities. Any applicant requiring an accommodation in connection with the hiring process and/or to perform the essential functions of the position for which the applicant has applied should contact the Accommodations team at leavesandaccommodations@modernatx.com.

**Job Summary**

This role ensures effective execution of the manufacturing schedule, adherence to established procedures, compliance with safety requirements, and timely communication and coordination with cross-functional departments.

* You will ensure compliance with Company safety policies and procedures, as well as applicable Occupational Safety & Health Administration (OSHA) and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requirements.

* You will investigate batch upsets or nonconformances and prepare a formal report.
* You will implement corrective and preventive actions to minimize defects, product contamination, and material or component mix-ups.

**Senior Manager, Quality Assurance (QA)**

  

**Discover Veranova:**

  

At Veranova, we believe people are our most important asset, and we are dedicated to building the most talented workforce in our industry. Our commitment to uncompromising focus on quality, compliance, safety, and excellence in delivery shapes everything we do. We are not just looking for skills; we are seeking innovative individuals who have a mindset open to learning and growth, and a desire to make a difference. Every role at Veranova plays a part in delivering an exceptional customer experience through ownership and integrity.

  

Veranova is a global leader in the development and manufacturing of complex active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for pharma and biotech customers. With deep technical expertise and impressive flexibility, we develop solutions and processes that support and accelerate innovation.

  

Join us on our mission to enable current and next-generation therapeutics to improve and save the lives of patients.

  

**Role Overview:**

  

The Sr Manager, QA is responsible for leading the Veranova Quality Assurance team, managing quality oversight of the manufacturing process and associated operations. This includes leading and managing multiple QA teams for batch record review, batch disposition, and on the floor QA support to ensure GMP compliance across all stages of manufacturing, as well as disposition and release of starting materials and customer facing Quality program leads for each client. The person filling this role will be responsible for the leadership, development and training of team members within their oversight as well as providing supportive leadership and strategic direction to operate with and maintain compliance to regulatory and industry quality standards. The role is expected to build strong collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders to drive compliance and continuous improvement of GMP operations.

  

The position is 100% on site 1st shift at our Devens, MA facility.

  

**Core Responsibilities:**

  

  
* Evaluate and implement systems, methods, techniques, and solutions to complex quality compliance issues.
  
* Interface with Clients for project planning, and problem resolution with a strong customer service approach.
  
* Lead or support implementation of critical compliance systems and provide recommendations to operations management.
  
* Recommends the stop of any manufacture and/or distribution of a product if necessary.
  
* Manages the review, approval, and ensures delivery of Quality Assurance related training content and programs including new Quality Assurance initiatives for continuous improvement.
  
* Analyzes trends associated with data, proficiency testing, equipment/supply/reagent defects and supports development of solutions as appropriate.
  
* Direct and advise the Quality Assurance group to achieve long and short-term goals and objectives.
  
* Develops, improves, and revises Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Quality Policies as required/needed.
  
* Ensures the review and approval of equipment qualification protocols and results.
  
* Participates in internal auditing programs to assure compliance with regulatory requirements and company standards.
  
* Partner collaboratively with Production, Maintenance, and QC for all Quality decisions within the scope of the role.
  
* Additional assignments/ duties to support team objective and contribute to the Veranova mission may evolve based on business needs.
  

  

**Qualifications:**

  

  
* BS or MS in Chemistry, Engineering or related field required.
  
* Must have a minimum of 10 years of experience in Quality Assurance in an FDA regulated industry. Experience in an API in GMP environment is preferred.
  
* Minimum of 7 years of supervisory experience required; Proven ability to lead and coach, and motivate employees, clearly communicate job requirements, and effectively manage performance of staff.
  
* Must have established experience in Analytical and Quality Control support of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API).
  
* Knowledge and previous experience with GMP, ICH Q7, and 21 CFR Part 11; Expertise in FDA regulations, GMPs, and Quality Systems relevant to pharmaceutical manufacturing.
  
* Experience with hosting and/or regulatory facing inspection responsibilities is required.
  
* Knowledge of Inventory Management, LIMS, Quality Management software systems experience desired.
  
* Must be a change agent and have strong interest in succession planning and professional development of their team(s); Ability to change priorities in response to company demands while continuing to deliver exceptional work quality through leadership by example.
  

  

**Salary Range:**

  

The salary range for this role is $155,000–$175,000. This range represents a good‑faith estimate of the compensation we expect to offer for this position at the time of posting. Actual compensation will be based on factors such as relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and internal equity. In exceptional cases, compensation may exceed the stated range.

  

All full-time employees are eligible to participate in our annual incentive bonus program. Bonus targets vary by career level and are based on individual and company performance.

  

**Our Commitment:**

  

  
* Health & Wellness:
  Comprehensive health & wellness benefits. Access to mental health resources and wellness programs. Generous PTO and holiday pay policies.
  
* Financial Wellness:
  Veranova is committed to fair and transparent compensation practices. This includes a competitive base salary, eligibility for performance-based bonuses, and an attractive 401(k) Plan with company match. Salary ranges reflect the scope and expectations of the role, and are based on market data, internal equity, and role-specific factors. Final compensation may vary depending on experience, skills, education, and business needs.
  
* Professional Development

* Inclusive Culture:
  At Veranova, an inclusive culture is integral to our values. We welcome people with diverse experiences and perspectives who share our mission to improve and save lives. Even if you don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply. Veterans, first responders, and those transitioning from military to civilian life bring valuable skills that strengthen our team.
  

  

**Additional Information:**

  

Applicants for this role must be authorized to work in the United States without further employer sponsorship.

records.description:
Innovation starts from the heart. Edwards Lifesciences is the leading global structural heart innovation company, driven by a passion to improve patient lives. With millions of patients served in over 100 countries, each team makes a meaningful contribution by improving patient outcomes and discovering lasting solutions for unmet patient needs. Our
**Senior Manager, Quality Engineering**
position is a unique career opportunity that could be your next step towards an exciting future.
  
  
The Senior Manager, Quality Engineering is a people leadership and manufacturing role responsible for providing quality and compliance oversight. This leader will manage and develop a team of Quality Engineers while partnering closely with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities, Maintenance, and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturing activities are performed safely, effectively, and in compliance with applicable quality system requirements.
  
  
The position will oversee quality and compliance activities supporting the plant’s major production areas, including THV manufacturing, TMTT manufacturing, advanced catheters, and metals. The successful candidate will strengthen NCR and CAPA execution, improve investigation quality, monitor operational quality metrics, and establish effective communication and continuity.
  
  
**How You'll Make an Impact:**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of Quality Engineers supporting manufacturing operations, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and individual development plans.
* Provide quality and compliance oversight for manufacturing activities, ensuring operations are performed in accordance with approved procedures, quality system requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Oversee the initiation, investigation, review, approval, and timely closure of nonconformance reports, including evaluating investigation quality, root cause determination, corrective actions, and product or process risk.
* Own and provide leadership for CAPAs, including investigation strategy, root cause analysis, action planning, implementation, effectiveness verification, and sustainable closure.
* Lead the deployment, implementation, and continuous improvement of quality management systems and manufacturing quality processes aligned with ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820.
* Review and approve test method validations, measurement system analyses, and manufacturing process validations, including IQ, OQ, and PQ documentation.
* Monitor quality metrics, trends, investigation performance, and quality data reviews; identify emerging risks and provide actionable recommendations to Operations and Quality leadership.
* Support internal and external audits by ensuring operations remain inspection-ready, responding to auditor questions, and leading or supporting actions resulting from audit observations.
* Partner with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, Maintenance, and Supply Chain to resolve quality issues, maintain compliant production, and strengthen operational controls.
* Establish effective shift-to-shift communication and escalation processes to ensure timely transfer of quality, production, and compliance information.
* Provide quality leadership for supplier-related issues, as applicable, including investigation support, corrective actions, and supplier performance concerns.
* Promote a culture of quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management.
* Develop and implement quality processes that improve product compliance, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.
* Other incidental duties as assigned.

**What You'll Need (Required):**

* Bachelor’s degree with relevant Quality Engineering, Quality Management, or Manufacturing Quality experience within a highly regulated environment; or equivalent experience based on Edwards’ criteria.
* Demonstrated people leadership experience managing and developing engineers or other technical quality professionals.
* Experience deploying, implementing, or sustaining quality management systems within a regulated manufacturing environment, including working knowledge of ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820 requirements.
* Strong experience leading CAPAs, nonconformance investigations, and structured root cause analysis, including evaluation of investigation quality and effectiveness.

**What Else We Look For (Preferred):**

* Engineering or Scientific degree
* Medical device manufacturing experience
* Experience providing quality oversight for manufacturing or production operations, including partnering directly with Operations and Engineering to resolve compliance and product quality issues.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret quality data, monitor operational quality metrics, recognize adverse trends, and escalate significant risks.
* Experience with microbiology principles or microbiological controls in a regulated manufacturing environment.
* Experience supporting cleanroom qualification, environmental controls, or manufacturing operations performed within controlled environments.
* Supplier quality or supplier management experience, including supplier investigations and corrective actions.
* Experience reviewing or approving test method validations and measurement system analysis studies.
* Experience reviewing or approving manufacturing process validations, including IQ/OQ/PQ.
* Experience supporting internal, external, or regulatory audits.
* Experience leading quality activities across multiple manufacturing technologies, product lines, or production areas.
* Knowledge of statistical methods, process capability, measurement systems, risk management, and continuous improvement tools.
* Demonstrated success strengthening team capability, improving organizational effectiveness, and leading change within a manufacturing quality organization.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence decisions and communicate effectively across technical, operational, and leadership audiences.

records.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
  
  
**About The Team**
The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril's fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build collaborative combat aircraft, missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are scaling production of autonomous aircraft across our manufacturing facilities. Manufacturing Engineering drives process development, production readiness, and the transition from prototype to rate — ensuring that what Design engineers create can be built reliably, repeatedly, and at scale.
  
  
**About The Job**
Anduril is seeking a Senior Manager of Manufacturing Engineering to lead ME strategy and execution across the Autonomous Airpower portfolio. This is not a single-program role — you will be the manufacturing engineering voice across every aircraft program in the portfolio, from early concept through full-rate production. You will work directly with chief engineers, program managers, and the growth team to shape what gets built, how it gets built, and whether it can be built on cost and on schedule.
  
  
You are the first person from the ME organization that program managers and growth leads turn to when evaluating emerging capabilities. You provide the manufacturing perspective on what is realistic and achievable — grounding engineering ambitions in production reality. You understand every phase of the aircraft lifecycle: DFM input during design, participation in design reviews, prototype and first-article builds, LRIP standup, and the transition to full-rate production. You know what it takes to go from a clean-sheet aircraft concept to hardware rolling off a production line.
  
  
You will build and lead a team of manufacturing engineers, set the technical direction for the ME organization, and represent manufacturing engineering to directors and executives. This role requires someone who has lived aircraft manufacturing — not managed it from a distance — and who can move fluidly between a factory floor conversation and an executive review.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Lead manufacturing engineering strategy and execution across the full Autonomous Airpower portfolio, spanning multiple aircraft programs in various stages of maturity
* Serve as the primary ME point of contact for program managers and the growth team on emerging capabilities — providing early-stage assessments of manufacturability, cost, schedule, and production feasibility
* Partner with chief engineers and design leadership during all phases of engineering development, from concept trades and DFM input through design reviews, prototype builds, LRIP, and full-rate production
* Build, develop, and lead a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers across disciplines — structures, mechanical systems, fluid systems, propulsion, avionics, and harnessing
* Drive cross-functional alignment between engineering, supply chain, manufacturing operations, program management, quality, and leadership to ensure production readiness across programs
* Own the ME cost and schedule position for your portfolio — developing estimates, tracking execution, identifying risks, and presenting status to directors and executives
* Represent manufacturing engineering in executive reviews, program gate reviews, and customer-facing discussions, translating production realities into clear, actionable information for senior leadership
* Establish manufacturing engineering standards, processes, and best practices that scale across programs and production sites
* Evaluate and advise on make-vs-buy decisions, capital investments, and production strategies based on deep knowledge of aircraft manufacturing capabilities and constraints
* Drive production readiness across the portfolio — MBOMs, process maturity, tooling readiness, rate-readiness assessments — ensuring programs are set up to succeed at each production milestone

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering
* 12+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace or defense, with significant time spent on aircraft programs
* Deep, hands-on knowledge of aircraft manufacturing across multiple disciplines — structures/composites, mechanical systems, fluid systems, avionics, harnessing, or propulsion
* Experience across the full aircraft production lifecycle: DFM, design reviews, prototype/first-article builds, LRIP, and full-rate production
* 5+ years of experience leading and developing manufacturing engineering teams
* Demonstrated ability to assess emerging programs and provide credible manufacturing cost, schedule, and feasibility inputs
* Experience presenting manufacturing status, risks, and recommendations to director-level and executive audiences
* Strong cross-functional leadership — proven ability to drive alignment across engineering, operations, supply chain, program management, and business leadership
* Experience managing manufacturing engineering budgets and cost positions across multiple programs
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience standing up new aircraft production lines from scratch — from facility planning through rate production
* Experience working directly with growth or business development teams to shape proposals and production strategies for new aircraft programs
* Experience with autonomous aircraft, UAV, or advanced air vehicle programs
* Knowledge of EVMS, earned value reporting, and program control fundamentals
* Experience with Manufacturing Readiness Levels (MRL) and Manufacturing Readiness Assessments (MRA)
* Experience working with Teamcenter, SAP, Oracle, or similar PLM/ERP platforms
* Master's degree in Engineering, Business, or related field
* Active U.S. Secret security clearance

US Salary Range
  
  
$183,000—$243,000 USD
  
  
**Benefits**
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
  
  
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.
*For more information, Explore Our Benefits.*
**Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
  
  
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
  
  

* No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* Please always verify communications:

+ Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
+ Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

* Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

**Data Privacy**
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
  
  
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

records.description:
**About Us**
Spellman High Voltage Electronics Corporation, a family owned business for over 75 years, takes pride in powering progress in health, security and quality of life. We are key partners with the world’s leading medical devices, semiconductor, scientific analytics and industrial systems manufacturers. When they want to push the limits of what’s possible with high voltage applications, they turn to us to make it happen.
  
  
While Spellman is not a household name, our products are used to make and often power many of the most advanced technologies that make modern life possible. With design and manufacturing sites in North America, Europe and Asia, we have become the preferred provider of high voltage power solutions for OEMs pushing the boundaries of technology around the world by designing and producing the products they need to power progress.
  
  
The primary role of the Senior Manager, NPI will provide leadership to a diverse team of engineers and provide support in the design, documentation, analysis, and coordination of release for products being transferred from design to production. The Senior Manager, NPI will contribute to the success of projects as well as the team. In this role, the Senior Manager, NPI will balance the work within the team, coach the team through technical challenges, and act as a role model in the organization. The Senior Manager, NPI will be expected to provide technical input to the leadership team to support business decisions.
  
  
This leader, with their team develops and implements operations requirements for design transfer across all product portfolios and collaborates with development, manufacturing and technical support teams to assure that all aspects of design for quality and manufacturability (DQM) are utilized for robust design development, transfer and ultimately scale up. Assures appropriate test method validations and product specifications are developed and implemented. Individual is also responsible for managing new part number creation and appropriate work instruction development. Will work cross functionally to ensure repeatability and reproducibility of the manufactured products within product and process capabilities and meeting of desired specifications.
  
  
Provides leadership of design transfer activities of products also engages in technology transfer activities involving product end of life or transfer to other Spellman High Voltage Electronics manufacturing sites.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Establishes overall team direction and goals, and sets direction of resources toward completion of goals, in conjunction with Senior Leadership in both Development and Operations. Promotes an open, collaborative environment focused on teamwork
* Establishes and maintains design transfer project milestones and timelines
* Supports robust design specification development and validation activities during design transfer, working closely with counterparts in the development team.
* Oversight for all NPI deliverables to the customer and expected team output
* Communication with all members of the NPI team to monitor project status, scope changes, and KPIs
* Work with the Product Development teams to ensure that all new products have been put through the adequate testing and best practices have been used
* Work collaboratively with peers and other cross-functional team members including define sub-system design requirement specifications and design architectures
* Manage and collaborate across multi-technical disciplines and cross-functional teams
* Plan, manage, and delegate project resource requirements, schedules, and task activities.
* Resolve problems using solutions that involve new techniques, technologies, or concepts.
* Effective application of engineering excellence processes and techniques (DFMEA, PFMEA, DOE, DVP&R, boundary diagrams, DFM/A, Technical Design Reviews, fault tree and risk assessment, SCRUM, etc.)
* Lead a team of NPI Manufacturing Engineers, in collaboration with other organizations, to support production of complex products with responsibilities including but not limited to:
* Establish group and individual objectives, priorities, and metrics
* Ensure production of products meets expected output
* Ensure quality requirements are fulfilled and maintained
* Provide technical support for failure analysis and root cause investigation of product failures.
* Analyze manufacturing lines from a risk perspective (pFMEA) to incorporate and validate critical tests used in manufacturing.
* Assume responsibility for the validation of manufacturing equipment and processes leveraging standard qualification approaches (IQ/OQ/PQ/DQ/PPQ).
* Provide production line support for day-to-day engineering issues on production and NPI lines.
* Identify and implement continuous improvement projects with respect to first pass yield, cycle time reduction, product reliability, capacity enhancements, and cost reduction.
* Liaise between project management, engineering, and manufacturing functions to ensure project goals are on track
* Adherence to applicable QMS policies and procedures
* Ensure the team sets and meets reasonable deliverable expectations Review and approve engineering changes
* Facilitate problem-solving efforts and continually improve processes
* Understand, lead, and coach in DFX concepts, pFMEA, problem-solving, and transfer efforts
* Lead in the decision-making process for production planning and layout
* Evaluate and estimate the required and proposed engineering tasks (headcount or hours) Understand the product funnel and needs for NPI resources during the early phases of development
* Other duties as assigned by management

**Requirements**

* Minimum of 15 years of demonstrated experience in people management and leadership role
* Minimum of 10 years experience in electronics manufacturing and knowledge of Design Control guidelines
* Minimum of 10 years leading/managing New Product Introduction Teams; including hiring, employee development, managing subordinate managers, project planning, and coordination in a matrixed organization
* Strong Conflict resolution and negotiation skills
* Strong written and verbal communication skills

records.description:
Beehive Industries is dedicated to
**Powering American Defense**
by revolutionizing the design, development, and delivery of jet propulsion systems to support the warfighter. Founded in 2020, the company is headquartered in Centennial, Colorado, with additional facilities in Knoxville, Tennessee, Loveland Ohio, and Mount Vernon, Ohio. **Role Overview**
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering will own end-to-end manufacturing engineering strategy and execution across the product lifecycle, from new product introduction (NPI) through production ramp and rate manufacturing.
  
  
This role unifies distributed Centers of Excellence (NPI, Additive, Machining, Assembly & Test) under a single technical vision, ensuring seamless part transitions, robust process definition, and achievement of cost, quality, and rate targets.
  
  
The Senior Manager will bring deep expertise in additive manufacturing and serve as a key partner to Design Engineering, using data-driven insights to influence design decisions, drive DFM/DFAM, and optimize lifecycle cost, while leading and mentoring a team of Manufacturing Engineers across multiple sites.
  
  
**What You'll Do...**

+ Own manufacturing engineering across the full product lifecycle: NPI through production ramp and rate manufacturing
+ Ensure robust manufacturing release readiness, including CTQs, process capability, and transfer gates
+ Lead transition to production, including rate readiness, line balancing, and tooling/fixture readiness

* Multi-Site Integration & Standardization

+ Align NPI, Additive, Machining, and Assembly & Test COEs under a unified operating model [AB1]
+ Establish cross-site standards for process definition, handoffs, data traceability, and work instructions
+ Drive repeatability, scalability, and efficiency across geographically distributed teams

* Additive Manufacturing & Technical Leadership

+ Serve as the technical authority for additive manufacturing

+ Drive DFAM adoption and ensure outputs are optimized for downstream manufacturing processes

* Design Partnership & DFM

+ Partner with Design Engineering to influence designs using manufacturing data
+ Drive DFM/DFAM and lifecycle cost optimization
+ Establish feedback loops from NPI and production to continuously improve design and manufacturability

* Process Excellence & Performance

+ Develop and standardize tooling strategies, process flows, and validation plans
+ Drive improvements in yield, throughput, cost, and automation
+ Ensure robust process validation prior to production release and sustained operational performance

* Team Leadership

+ Provide technical leadership, mentorship, and direction to Manufacturing Engineers across sites and COEs

* Experience across NPI, prototyping, production ramp, and high-rate manufacturing

records.description:
As Senior Manager of R&D Vehicle Production, you will run the prototype vehicle lines at our factory in Fremont, CA. Your team is responsible for building and testing R&D vehicles for mileage collection and software validation, plus early builds of our next-generation ground-up vehicles. You will own assembly, diagnostics, testing, and End-of-Line (EOL), and help carry new vehicles into serial production.
  
  
Prototype builds surface new hardware and software issues every day. Success in this role depends on working closely with hardware and software engineering teams to resolve them fast, so you can meet production goals. You will set priorities, hold owners accountable, and escalate decisively when an issue blocks the build.
  
  
Reporting to the Senior Director of Manufacturing Engineering and General Assembly, you will be a key leader in Zoox Manufacturing Operations. You will partner closely with Vehicle Development, Software, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and the teams operating our test fleet.
  
  
**In This Role, You Will**

* Own diagnostics, functional testing, and EOL validation. Deliver vehicles to fleet and engineering teams safely, complete, and on time.
* Implement repeatable build processes and keep accurate hardware and software configuration records for every vehicle. Ensure each vehicle meets quality and product specifications.
* Prepare and manage the line's OPEX, CAPEX, and headcount budgets. Identify investments that improve throughput, quality, and flexibility.
* Ensure MES and QMS support prototype builds, including traceability and issue tracking. Drive continuous improvement through the Zoox Production System.
* Hire, train, and develop technicians, leads, and supervisors. Set clear expectations and evaluate performance.
* Build a culture that puts employee and product safety first, in partnership with EHS. Enforce safe practices for high-voltage systems and pre-production vehicles.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Management, or a related field.
* 15+ years of experience in vehicle or complex electromechanical assembly manufacturing (e.g., automotive, aerospace, robotics), including prototype, pilot, or NPI builds.
* 5+ years of experience leading production teams, including supervisors or managers.
* Proven ability to lead hardware and software engineers to resolve build issues under schedule pressure, often without direct authority.
* Working knowledge of vehicle systems (mechanical, electrical, high-voltage, embedded software) and how they are built, diagnosed, and tested.
* Experience transitioning new products from prototype into serial production.
* Familiarity with MES, ERP, and QMS, and with structured problem-solving (e.g., 8D, root cause analysis).
* Clear communicator who can present build status, risks, and trade-offs to executives.

**Bonus Qualifications**

* Experience with autonomous, electric, or other software-defined vehicles.
* Experience building or retrofitting R&D or test-fleet vehicles.
* Experience applying lean principles in low-volume, high-mix production.

$195,000 - $293,000 a year

records.description:
**Location:**
North of Boston, MA (on-site)
  
  
**About The Company**
Our client is a growing, private equity-backed food manufacturer producing fresh, ready-to-cook proteins and meal solutions for leading grocery retailers and foodservice customers nationwide. Their products, including hand-crafted, value-added meats combined with fresh vegetables and seasonings, have earned a strong position in the specialty section of the grocery store. The company is growing, and leadership is now investing in operational excellence to support the next phase of that growth.
  
  
The Opportunity
  
  
This is a newly created role and the company's first dedicated continuous improvement leader. You'll partner closely with plant leadership to build a CI function from the ground up across a 250-person production floor. The operation is high-mix and labor-intensive: much of the product is assembled by hand, the product is perishable, and daily needs change based on customer demand. This is not machine-paced manufacturing, and it calls for someone who knows how to improve operations where people, not equipment, drive output.
  
  
Leadership is excited about this role and fully behind it. The right person will have the independence and support to make a real, measurable impact on cost, yield, and how work gets done.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Lead cost-out initiatives across the plant, with a focus on labor productivity, yield, and waste reduction
* Build the KPI and metrics foundation the operation currently lacks, including labor standards, yield tracking, and performance dashboards
* Shorten the loop between labor planning and actual results so the team can manage to standard daily
* Rethink how manual work is organized and performed, including line layout, staffing models, work methods, and labor standards for high-mix hand assembly
* Identify and attack sources of product loss, giveaway, and waste in a perishable environment
* Drive structured root cause analysis and make sure fixes stick
* Introduce practical Lean and Six Sigma tools and build a CI culture where none exists today
* Work hands-on on the floor alongside supervisors and team members, coaching and training as you go
* Partner with quality and food safety to make sure improvements support regulatory and customer requirements
* Use NetSuite and Power BI to turn operational data into clear, actionable reporting

What We're Looking For
  
  

* 5+ years of continuous improvement, operational excellence, or industrial engineering experience in manufacturing, with progressive leadership responsibility
* Proven success improving labor-intensive, high-mix, manual assembly operations. This is the most important requirement.
* Food manufacturing experience strongly preferred, especially fresh, perishable, or protein processing environments
* Strong working knowledge of Lean and Six Sigma. Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
* A track record of building metrics, labor standards, and accountability systems from scratch
* Documented cost savings and yield improvements you can speak to in detail
* An independent, self-directed style: someone who can assess an operation, set a plan, and execute without a lot of structure around them
* A hands-on leader who is comfortable on the production floor and earns credibility with frontline teams
* Experience with NetSuite and Power BI, or similar ERP and BI tools
* Bilingual in English and Spanish is a strong plus
* Must be local to the Greater Boston / North Shore area or willing to relocate. This role is on-site.

Why This Role
  
  

* Build the CI function from the ground up with real ownership and visible impact
* Leadership and investors who are committed to the investment and eager to support it
* A growing company with room for advancement as the business scales

**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained
* Build CI capability within site leadership and frontline teams through training, coaching, kaizen leadership, and development of local change agents
* Establish common operational KPI definitions and review routines that enable benchmarking and the sharing and scaling of best practices across Komline
* Support acquisition integration by assessing operational maturity, identifying improvement opportunities, and integrating acquired sites into Komline’s operating system
* Provide regular enterprise-level reporting to the COO on CI pipeline, benefits realization, site maturity, risks, and resource priorities
* Promote a culture of accountability, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong partnership with decentralized business leadership

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, operational excellence, industrial engineering, or related leadership roles
* Demonstrated success leading Lean / continuous improvement across multiple sites or business units
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management, kaizen, standard work, value-stream mapping, structured problem solving, and performance management
* Proven ability to influence GMs, Plant Managers, and functional leaders without relying on direct authority
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable financial impact
* Excellent leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and executive presentation skills
* Ability to travel approximately 50%+, depending on site and project needs

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Lean leadership certification or equivalent and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
* Experience in multi-site industrial, engineered-product, capital-equipment, or process-equipment manufacturing
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or deploying a common operating system across decentralized businesses
* Experience with plant layout, flow optimization, capacity improvement, and working-capital initiatives
* MBA or advanced technical/operations degree

**Equal Opportunity Statement:**
Komline is an EEO employer – M/F/Vets/Disabled

records.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. The Senior Manager, Quality Investigation/CAPA leads the US Pharmaceutical Distribution team responsible for quality investigations, temperature excursions, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and suspect or illegitimate product reviews. The manager provides day-to-day direction, technical guidance, and coaching to help the team complete accurate, timely, and risk-based work. This role also supports quality systems, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across the distribution network.

  
  

**Compensation: The salary for this role is targeted between $140,000 and $145,000 yearly with an annual bonus opportunity.**

**Key Responsibilities**

* Leads and develops the Investigation/CAPA team. Sets priorities, assigns work, monitors workload and performance, and provides regular coaching and feedback. Ensures investigations, CAPAs, regulatory notifications, trend reports, and self-audits are completed on time and meet quality requirements.
* Keeps Investigation/CAPA processes current and practical. Updates procedures, work instructions, training, and tools so the Quality team and distribution centers follow a consistent approach.
* Provides oversight for complex product quality investigations, temperature excursions, complaints, quarantines, critical events, and suspect or illegitimate product cases. Guides investigation strategy, root cause analysis, risk assessment, escalation, product disposition support, and final conclusions.
* Implements approved improvements to quality systems and processes, including electronic quality management system updates and standardized tools. Works with affected USPD teams and locations to put changes into practice.
* Tracks investigation and CAPA performance, including aging, timeliness, effectiveness, and recurring trends. Shares findings with leadership and adjusts priorities or starts corrective action when needed.
* Ensures the team consistently applies FDA, DEA, Drug Supply Chain Security Act, Good Distribution Practice, current Good Manufacturing Practice, data integrity, and internal quality requirements. Partners with Enterprise Quality, Operations, distribution centers, Transportation, Recall, Global Security, and other groups to resolve issues.
* Represents Quality on audits, inspections, projects, and cross-functional initiatives. Presents technical information clearly, coordinates assigned work, and follows through on commitments.
* Manages the team’s approved operating expenses, including applicable electronic quality management system costs.
  

  

**Minimum Requirement**

Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 9+ years of professional experience and 1+ years of supervisory and/or management experience.

  
  

**Education**

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, or a related field.

  
  

**Critical Skills**

* At least 9 years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical quality, investigations, CAPA, regulated distribution, cold-chain operations, quality systems, or another highly regulated environment.
* At least 1 year of direct people-management or supervisory experience, with demonstrated ability to set expectations, manage performance, coach employees, and build team capability.
* Experience leading complex investigations and CAPAs, assessing risk, resolving quality or compliance issues, and driving timely, effective outcomes.
* Working knowledge of applicable FDA requirements, including 21 CFR and the Drug Supply Chain Security Act, as well as applicable DEA requirements and the Controlled Substances Act.
* Knowledge of Good Distribution Practice and current Good Manufacturing Practice principles, root cause analysis, quality risk management, data integrity, and audit or inspection readiness.
* Experience implementing, validating, or migrating electronic quality management systems.
* Strong technical writing, analytical, project leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
* Ability to manage competing priorities, use sound judgment, and work effectively across a large, matrixed organization.
* Knowledge of wholesale pharmaceutical distribution or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and quality data analysis tools.
* Ability to work remotely while maintaining regular collaboration with distribution centers, Central Fill Pharmacy locations, and corporate partners.
* Ability to travel domestically, including occasional overnight travel, approximately 10% to 15%.
* Ability to work from home within approximately a two-hour drive of a USPD distribution center.
