records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
**Job Description**
Tremco Construction Products Group (CPG), part of RPM International Inc., unites industry-leading building envelope solutions manufacturers, service providers and trusted brands—including Tremco, Nudura, Dryvit, Willseal, Weatherproofing Technologies, Inc. and Weatherproofing Technologies Canada—to deliver comprehensive, integrated building systems. With operations spanning North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, India and Latin America, Tremco CPG has a global presence supported by regional businesses and distributors who understand local market needs for commercial, industrial and residential construction and restoration projects.
 
 
**Tremco is currently looking for a Plant Manager in our Columbus, GA facility.**
The Plant Manager manages daily production operations to meet Safety, Quality, Service and Cost objectives. Ensures supply chain execution in the provision of finished goods. Establishes and/or executes operating policies and procedures to achieve EH&S standards, compliance, production schedules, product quality standards, customer expectations/satisfaction and operational cost targets.
 
 
**Tremco’s Expectations For All Leaders**

* Embodies the company's core values of transparency, trust, and respect by demonstrating integrity, commitment, responsible entrepreneurship, and moral courage.
* Applies the company’s policies and adheres to processes to ensure compliance and organizational best practices.
* Demonstrates a commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in all areas of responsibility such as hiring and promotion decisions.
* Effectively and efficiently onboards new employees.
* Conducts annual performance evaluations and provides ongoing performance feedback, maintaining clear and timely documentation.
* Coaches and manages employees using the company’s philosophy and tools to ensure talent is developed and retained. Constructs succession plans to ensure sustainability and continuity of area of responsibility.

**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Oversee the safety of staff, visitors, equipment, and facility in accordance with the North American Manufacturing Safety Program.
* Ensure the execution and compliance of EHS requirements including the management, storage and disposal of hazardous materials.
* Optimize process efficiency, throughput, and yield.
* Provide the support necessary to develop team members, operate equipment, solve process problems, and direct outcomes.
* Lead the manufacturing team to meet established goals leveraging Lean manufacturing practices.
* Own and drive operational outcomes to meet financial objectives and business goals.
* Ensure staff is competent to perform all required functions.
* Manage, coach and develop to ensure talent is developed and retained.
* Determine organizational objectives and defines structure.
* Interface with senior management to ensure manufacturing goals are consistent with strategic direction.
* Develop long and short-term plans for capital investment and supervise plans for implementation.
* Oversee, either directly or indirectly, investigations of labor, cost and process variances and deviations.
* Participate in annual budget preparation.
* Manage the plant budget, costs, and profitability.
* Control expenses such as raw materials, energy consumption, and labor and drive cost-savings initiatives and operational improvements.
* Ensure preventative and predictive maintenance programs, minimize downtime, and oversee major repairs, shutdowns, and equipment upgrades.
* Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and teamwork.
* Support innovation in chemical processes and technologies.
* Ensure efficient inventory management, procurement and logistics.

**EDUCATION REQUIREMENT:**
The educational minimal requirement for the Plant Manager position is a Bachelors’ Degree.
 
 
**Experience Requirement**

* 7+ years chemical or process manufacturing experience with hands-on work with production, operations, or plant engineering
* Progression through roles such as: Process Engineer, Production Supervisor, Operations Manager, Maintenance or Reliability Manager
* 5+ years' experience managing teams of operators, engineers, and supervisors

**Other Skills, Abilities, And Qualifications**

* SAP/ERP experience
* Lean methodologies
* Ability to apply excel, word, and SAP applications to daily job responsibilities.

**Benefits And Compensation**
The salary range for applicants in this position generally ranges between $150,000 - $200,000. This range is an estimate, based on potential employee qualifications, operations, needs, and other considerations permitted by law.
 
 
The Company offers a variety of benefits to its employees, including but not limited to health insurance, paid holidays, paid time off, 401(k) Savings and Trust & Plan with company match, Company Pension Plan, Performance Based Bonus/Commission, and continuing education.
 
 
***All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.***

records.title: Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering
records.description:
**Job Summary**
The Director of Manufacturing Process Engineering is a hands-on leadership role and the process authority for how Butcher Power Products’ switchboard and switchgear products are built. The person in this role must be the subject-matter expert who can also do the work — capable of designing and improving manufacturing processes and line layouts, building routings and process documentation, and personally leading process and PFMEA reviews — so they can teach and develop the manufacturing engineering team and set the standard for process quality. This role owns how products are built rather than what is designed; however, deep familiarity with the product and the production floor is essential. The Director must understand the design intent released by Product Engineering and the realities of the floor in order to engineer processes that are efficient, repeatable, and capable. This role works hand in hand with Product Engineering as the manufacturing voice in the design process, partners with Quality on process controls, and supports Production and Planning rather than owning them.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Hands-On Process Engineering: Personally design, document, and improve the manufacturing processes, routings, work instructions, and line layouts that build the product. This is a working role: the successful candidate stays actively engaged in process design and technical problem-solving alongside the team rather than delegating all hands-on work.
* Process Authority & Technical Review: Lead, critique, and approve the team’s process designs, routings, PFMEAs, and control plans; set and enforce the standard for process quality, capability, and engineering rigor through formal process reviews.
* Mentorship & Teaching: Coach, train, and develop manufacturing engineers and technicians in process design, tooling, DFM/DFA, Lean and Six Sigma, time studies, and structured problem-solving, raising the technical capability of the whole team.
* Leadership & Management: Lead and manage the manufacturing engineering team, including hiring, development, workload balancing, priorities, and performance.
* Process Strategy & Standardization: Own manufacturing process strategy and standardization across product lines, and define the tooling and capital equipment roadmap.
* Product Engineering Partnership (DFM): Work closely and continuously with Product Engineering as the manufacturing voice in the design process — provide manufacturability and assembly feedback at design reviews before release, jointly resolve producibility issues, and ensure released designs transition cleanly into production.
* Process Controls & Quality Partnership: Own the manufacturing side of PFMEAs and control plans in partnership with Quality Engineering; ensure processes are capable, controlled, and continuously monitored.
* Continuous Improvement: Drive Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen across the function to improve throughput, cycle time, yield, and cost.
* Capital, Tooling & Automation: Plan and justify capital equipment, tooling, and automation investments, and provide financial management of the manufacturing engineering capital and tooling budgets.
* New Product Introduction (NPI): Lead the process side of NPI — develop and validate the processes, tooling, and routings that bring newly released designs into production.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Production, Planning, Quality, Project Management, and Product Engineering on capacity, scheduling, and material flow, supporting these functions rather than owning them.
* Safety & Compliance: Ensure manufacturing processes across the function comply with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards, including UL 891, NEC, and ANSI.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial, or Mechanical Engineering.
* 8+ years of progressive process engineering (or directly related) experience, including significant time spent personally developing and improving manufacturing processes.
* Hands-on proficiency in SolidWorks for process documentation, line layouts, and reviews; the ability to design tooling and fixtures in CAD is a plus.
* Strong proficiency developing routings, work instructions, process documentation, and process controls.
* Proven ability to lead formal process and PFMEA reviews and to mentor and train engineers and technicians.
* Experience hiring, developing, and managing a manufacturing engineering team.
* Strong working knowledge of PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and process capability (Cpk).
* Deep knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong understanding of the products being built and of how design intent translates into manufacturing process — sufficient product familiarity to engineer the right processes.
* Working knowledge of UL 891 and related standards (NEC, ANSI) as they affect manufacturing processes.
* Experience planning and justifying capital equipment and tooling investments, including financial management of budgets.
* Hands-on fabrication and machining experience is a plus.
* Automation experience is a plus.
* Experience with structured problem-solving methods such as 8D or A3 is a plus.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, particularly Microsoft Dynamics 365 (D365).
* Excellent leadership, project management, and problem-solving skills.
* Strong communication and interpersonal abilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Hands-on manufacturing process design and improvement (CAD)
* Process authority and engineering quality standards
* Technical mentoring, teaching, and team development
* Close partnership with Product Engineering (DFM)
* Process strategy, standardization, and tooling roadmap
* Design-for-manufacturability partnership
* Process controls, PFMEA, and capability
* Continuous improvement and Lean/Six Sigma
* Capital planning, automation, and financial management
* New product introduction (process side)
* Cross-functional collaboration and communication

records.title: Director of Manufacturing Launch
records.description:
Job Type
 
 
Full-time
 
 
**Description**
BLOX designs, manufactures, and constructs buildings and delivers them as products across the country. DesignManufactureConstruct is the system we use. DMC moves complexity to the left: work the industry solves in the field, we move to the factory; work the factory struggles with, we eliminate at design. Manufacturing runs as a visually controlled, continuous-flow pull system, managed to takt with the minimal buffers required to stabilize flow. The BLOX system works, proven through multiple products and launches. Our next step is to encode that experience into a manufacturing launch system that is repeatable, teachable, and capable of supporting the scale ahead of us. That means converting what our best people know into standard work, tooling, interfaces, controls, and training. It also means knowing which parts of the system are load-bearing, where volume creates pressure, and having the judgment to strengthen or replace what no longer serves the work. Growth will test every system. Our job is to be ready first.
 
 
The Director of Manufacturing Launch owns manufacturing setup in Launch, from design and first-of-a-kind production through ramp to stabilization, until a building can be consistently produced as a Product. Launch runs as a horizontal through the verticals, and it has three leaders: design, manufacturing, and program management. You are manufacturing. You control line setup, standard work, tooling, takt, and training. You do not control product design, supply chain, construction, or the customer, but you work with and influence all. Each of the three launch leaders builds a team beneath them, all held to one goal. You build the manufacturing launch team, and you resolve manufacturability while the work is still in design. Then you document the baseline, train the operations team, transfer the role, and repeat. Nothing gets thrown over a wall. A line is not finished until the people running it can run it without you.
 
 
**Requirements**
We are completing the launch and stabilization of a major product, with a strong pipeline behind it. Current-line attainment and new-product launch are distinct jobs, and this role exists so both can be done well. Your mandate is to build on what BLOX has already learned and make launch repeatable. We are looking for:
 
 

* A manufacturing expert. Layout, flow, takt, tooling, line-side setup. Has built lines, not just improved them.
* A process expert. Standard work, first-pass yield, the discipline to prove a method before scaling it and to replace it when the evidence says you should.
* A systems thinker. Understands design, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and field installation, and resolves problems where they are best eliminated.
* A team builder. Hires, teaches, and promotes engineers who outgrow the org chart.
* A simplifier. Drives to the simple answer on the far side of the complex one, and does the work to get there.

Our team is strong. They built this system and accomplished more, faster, than most teams ever attempt, and they are accountable for attainment on the line running today. Our growth now supports separating manufacturing launch leadership from steady-state operational leadership.
 
 
We build like a startup and operate like a manufacturer: if you have only worked where the plant, the budget, and the org chart already existed, this will be uncomfortable. Five years out: a billion dollars, the same system running across multiple factories, DMC at meaningful scale, and a system capable of helping reshape the fastest-growing sector in building. DMC belongs to the industry, not to us, so what you encode here does not stay here. This is not a place to move a thousandth in a decade. Here, you matter.
 
 
The seat: Director of Manufacturing Launch, reporting to the COO in close partnership with the CEO. Based in Birmingham, Alabama, with occasional travel to launch sites.
 
 
**Benefits**
BLOX offers the full spectrum of comprehensive benefits including health, dental, and vision insurance. We also offer flexible spending accounts, paid time off, short term disability, long term disability, life insurance and a 401k plan.
 
 
It is the policy of BLOX LLC to use ability and willingness to contribute to our team effort as the criteria for making employment related decisions, regardless of an individual’s race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or other protected status. In addition, we strictly prohibit the harassment of any employee because of his/her race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity), disability, or other protected status.

Our next step is to encode that experience into a manufacturing launch system that is repeatable, teachable, and capable of supporting the scale ahead of us.

The Director of Manufacturing Launch owns manufacturing setup in Launch, from design and first-of-a-kind production through ramp to stabilization, until a building can be consistently produced as a Product.

records.title: Sr. Manager, Optimus Operations
records.description:
**What To Expect**
The Senior Manager, Optimus Operations sets the vision and strategic path for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering within a major shop at Tesla’s new Optimus Factory in Austin, Texas. Openings span operations leadership across multiple shops—including Plastics, Machining, Actuators, and Assembly. Each role leads their shop teams and cross-functional partners to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production/Delivery, and Cost KPI targets.
 
 
This role is responsible for production and resource planning; coaching, mentoring, and developing leaders; launching new Optimus manufacturing processes and programs successfully; and daily tactical planning and execution to achieve the build plan and meet safety, quality, rate, and cost targets. The person in this role must guide the team through complex issues, distill large volumes of data to solve problems, and drive day-over-day continuous improvement in a high-volume, high-precision factory environment.
 
 
This Senior Manager provides hands-on support, leadership, and direction on all operational, team morale, and equipment-related matters. The person in this role builds teams that work cohesively and perform at the highest level—keeping Tesla’s mission and the goals of the Optimus program in mind—while partnering closely with peer shop leaders and factory leadership across the Austin Optimus Factory.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Set the vision and strategic path for Production and Maintenance in an assigned Optimus shop and lead the team to Safety, People, Quality, Production, and Cost KPI targets
- Drive tactical planning to hit the production build plan with the highest safety, quality, and yield, including identifying bottlenecks and addressing availability, efficiency, and yield constraints
- Launch new Optimus programs and lead production ramps and product/process design changes through resource planning, program management, and partnership with NPI, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain
- Guide the team through root cause analysis, first-principles thinking, and data-driven problem solving while maintaining standardized work and quality/safety compliance
- Coach, mentor, and develop Production, Maintenance, and Engineering leaders, instill process standardization and training, and drive continuous improvement
- Lead the maintenance organization on equipment availability, preventive and predictive maintenance, spare parts strategy, and uptime improvements for shop-critical assets
- Build a high-performing team with clear goals and feedback, improve morale with HR, and collaborate with peer shop Senior Managers to share best practices
**What You'll Bring**- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering preferred, or equivalent experience
- 7–10 years of leadership and manufacturing experience, preferably in automotive, robotics, plastics, precision machining, electromechanical assembly/actuators, general assembly, or another highly technical manufacturing environment
- Analytical, detail-oriented, self-driven critical thinker who communicates proactively and works well in a fast-paced, multicultural factory environment
- Experience with process-improvement methodologies, DOE/statistical methods, lean and world-class manufacturing practices, and standing up or ramping new factories, shops, or production lines
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work under pressure, juggle competing priorities, and meet tight deadlines
- Ability to use structured problem-solving methods such as 8D, fishbone diagrams, and 5-Why analysis to resolve production problems
- High-level leadership and decision-making skills with a strong sense of urgency in a greenfield/new-factory ramp, plus proficiency in MS Office, Visio, CAD, SPC, data-analysis tools, Jira, Tableau/BI dashboards, and project-management tools
**Benefits**
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
 
- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
- Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
- Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
- Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
- Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
- Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
- Tesla Babies program
- Commuter benefits
- Employee discounts and perks program
- Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
, Tesla

records.title: Sr Manager, Manufacturing - Electronics
records.description:
**About Advanced Energy**
Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for mission-critical applications and processes. AE’s power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.
 
 
Position Summary
 
 
The
**Senior Manager, Manufacturing**
is responsible for leading manufacturing operations across multiple AE locations, with a focus on
**complex electronic and electromechanical products and assemblies**
. This role ensures production efficiency, product quality, delivery performance, safety, and cost effectiveness while providing strategic and hands-on leadership to manufacturing supervisors and production teams.
 
 
Success in this role requires strong people leadership, strategic thinking, and significant practical experience in
**electronics, semiconductor, optics or high-tech manufacturing**
.
 
 
**Qualifications**
Required
 
 

* 8+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 3 years in a manufacturing leadership role.
* Demonstrated manufacturing experience in electronics, electromechanical systems, semiconductor equipment, or other complex technical products.
* Practical knowledge of electronics manufacturing processes, such as PCB/PCBA assembly, electronic and electromechanical assembly, production testing, troubleshooting, inspection, and repair/rework.
* Experience managing manufacturing environments requiring disciplined process control, traceability, quality management, and configuration/change control.
* Demonstrated success applying Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, root-cause analysis, and structured continuous-improvement methods.
* Strong working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems and production-planning processes, including material requirements, capacity planning, scheduling, and inventory management.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop manufacturing supervisors and production teams.
* Experience partnering with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product/Program teams to resolve production issues and support new product introductions.
* Strong communication, analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 25%.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

**Preferred**

* Experience manufacturing high-mix, low-to-medium-volume electronic or electromechanical products.
* Experience with semiconductor capital equipment, precision electronics, power electronics, optical systems, or other technically complex equipment.
* Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), design transfer, production ramp, and product lifecycle changes.
* Familiarity with IPC workmanship standards applicable to electronic assemblies.
* Experience with metrology, calibration, and inspection systems.
* Knowledge of applicable ISO quality-management standards and regulatory requirements.
* Experience leading manufacturing operations across multiple sites and/or internationally.
* Experience managing complex projects and cross-functional teams.

**COMPENSATION:**
*As required by multiple state pay transparency laws, Advanced Energy provides a reasonable range of compensation for each job posting. Actual compensation is influenced by an array of factors including, but not limited to, skill set, level of experience, and specific office location. The range of starting pay for this role is $150,000 to $190,000 per year.*
**BENEFITS:**
As part of our total rewards philosophy, we believe in offering and maintaining competitive compensation and benefits programs for our employees to attract and retain a talented, highly engaged workforce. Our compensation programs are focused on equitable, fair pay practices including market-based base pay, an annual pay-for-performance incentive plan for eligible positions, and a discounted Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
 
 
In addition to our competitive compensation practices, we offer a strong benefits package in each of the countries in which we operate. In the U.S., we offer a rich benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Medical - multiple medical plans are available to choose from
* Short and long-term disability and life insurance
* Health savings and flexible spending accounts
* Generous time off policy starting with 3 weeks of paid vacation, 7 days of paid sick time, and 12 paid holidays
* 8 hours of paid volunteer time off
* 8 weeks of paid parental leave for both Moms and Dads
* Company matched 401(k)
* Tuition reimbursement
* Expanded mental health coverage and employee assistance programs
* Other voluntary benefits include critical illness, accident and hospital indemnity, pet insurance, identify theft, and legal assistance

records.title: Senior Manager, Quality – Development Programs (R5315)
records.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.
 
 
**Job Description**
The Senior Manager of Quality is responsible for establishing and leading all quality activities for a complex aerospace development program from prototype through production readiness. This role serves as the primary quality leader embedded within the program team and partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Flight Test, and Program Management to ensure products are designed, developed, tested, and transitioned to production with quality, reliability, and mission success as foundational objectives.
 
 
The Senior Manager of Quality will build and lead a multidisciplinary quality team while implementing scalable quality systems, risk management processes, problem-solving disciplines, and development quality practices appropriate for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense technology organization.
 
 
This position requires balancing speed of development with disciplined engineering rigor to support aggressive program schedules while ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and company requirements.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Development Quality Leadership
* Serve as the quality leader for XBAT development.
* Establish quality strategy, objectives, and metrics aligned with program milestones.
* Integrate quality requirements into the product development lifecycle.
* Ensure quality considerations are incorporated during system architecture, design reviews, verification, validation, and qualification activities.
* Partner with Engineering leadership to identify and mitigate technical and programmatic risks.
* Drive a culture of proactive quality and continuous improvement throughout the program.

**Design & Configuration Quality**

* Ensure quality requirements are appropriately captured in product definitions, specifications, and design documentation.
* Participate in design reviews, change control boards, and configuration management activities.
* Ensure full configuration and traceability for all material installed into prototype aircraft.
* Evaluate engineering changes for quality and production readiness impacts.
* Support requirements verification and validation planning.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, design-for-quality, and design-for-reliability initiatives.

**Risk Management & Reliability**

* Lead quality participation in program risk management activities.
* Establish and maintain FRACAS processes for development and flight test phases of the program.
* Facilitate root cause and corrective action investigations for design, manufacturing, supplier, and field failures.
* Support reliability growth planning and execution.
* Monitor defect trends, failure modes, and reliability metrics to identify systemic risks.

**Verification, Validation & Test Quality**

* Develop quality oversight strategies for laboratory, ground, and flight test activities.
* Ensure test results, anomalies, and nonconformances are appropriately documented and dispositioned.
* Support qualification and certification efforts.
* Establish processes for managing test escapes, failures, and corrective actions.

**Nonconformance & Corrective Action Management**

* Lead Material Review Board activities for development hardware.
* Establish scalable processes for nonconformance management.
* Drive root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methodologies.
* Ensure timely and effective corrective and preventive actions.
* Track effectiveness of corrective actions through closure.

**Production Readiness & Industrialization**

* Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams to transition products from prototype to production.
* Define quality requirements for production readiness reviews.
* Support development of inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and control strategies.
* Ensure lessons learned from development are incorporated into production processes.
* Lead quality planning activities supporting low-rate initial production and rate increases.

**Quality Management System**

* Develop and implement quality processes supporting aerospace development programs.
* Ensure compliance with AS9100, customer requirements, and internal procedures.
* Drive continuous improvement of development quality processes.
* Support internal and external audits as required.
* Establish scalable systems that support future production growth.

**Leadership & Team Development**

* Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing quality organization.
* Recruit and develop quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians.
* Establish clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.
* Promote a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and collaboration.
* Develop organizational capabilities to support future company growth.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Aerospace Engineering, or related technical discipline.
* 10+ years of experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, space, or other highly regulated industries.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical quality organizations.
* Experience supporting complex product development programs from concept through production transition.
* Strong knowledge of quality systems, engineering development processes, and aerospace manufacturing.
* Experience leading root cause investigations and corrective action programs.
* Experience with risk management, reliability engineering, and failure analysis.
* Working knowledge of AS9100 quality management systems.
* Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience supporting UAV, aerospace, defense, aviation, autonomous systems, or advanced technology programs.
* Experience leading quality organizations during rapid company growth.
* Background in systems engineering, reliability engineering, or development engineering.
* Experience with flight test programs and qualification testing.
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or equivalent certification.
* Familiarity with government defense programs and customer quality requirements.

#LE
 
 
**Full-time Regular Employee Offer Package**
Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity
 
 
**Temporary Employee Offer Package**
Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)
 
 
Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.
 
 
Compensation Range: $162,243 - $243,365

records.description:
**Ford Energy**
is a newly formed, wholly-owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Company dedicated to accelerating U.S. energy independence. Leveraging Ford’s century of manufacturing excellence and world-class battery energy storage systems (BESS) technology, Ford Energy designs, manufactures, and services grid-scale and commercial DC battery energy storage systems (BESS). Ford Energy is uniquely positioned to capture the growing demand for reliable, US-built energy storage systems. We are not just building batteries; we are building the infrastructure for the next generation of the American grid.
 
 
Why Ford Energy?
 
 
At Ford Energy, you have the backing of an industrial manufacturing powerhouse with the agility of a dedicated energy startup offering industry leading technology. We offer a competitive compensation package including performance-based bonuses, Ford vehicle discounts, and the opportunity to shape the energy strategy of one of the world's most iconic brands.
 
 
In this position...
 
 
The Senior Manager Quality Assurance will serve as the senior quality leader and executive champion for Ford Energy quality culture. This highly visible leadership role is responsible for leading a team of engineering supervisors and quality engineers while owning the end-to-end quality operating model across the full development lifecycle. Beyond technical execution, you will be responsible for the financial protection of the subsidiary by managing the total "Cost of Quality" and warranty exposure. You will ensure that Ford Energy’s solutions are technically sound, safety and regulatory compliant, and capable of meeting customer expectations in production and in the field, serving as the primary quality interface for both internal and external executives.
 
 
What you'll do...
 
 

* Quality System Ownership & Governance

+ Own the quality operating model, quality gates, escalation paths, and KPI structure for Ford Energy.
+ Establish and enforce the high-level quality standards and technical rigor that the engineering, manufacturing, and service organizations must live by.
+ Manage the "clock speed" of the quality organization, providing data-driven insights that influence product strategy and launch decisions.

* Strategic Quality & Financial Accountability

+ Manage the total "Cost of Quality" (CoQ) for the subsidiary, including the mitigation of warranty spend and long-term liability.
+ Develop and own the quality standards and audit processes for global licensing partners and international cell suppliers to ensure consistency across the supply chain.
+ Represent Ford Energy Quality in discussions with internal and external executives, providing technical recommendations and risk assessments to support commercial decisions.

* End-to-End Technical Quality (The "V" Model)

+ Drive rigorous Failure Mode Avoidance (FMA) processes, ensuring quality is designed into requirements, architecture, and system integration.
+ Oversee validation strategy, factory acceptance readiness, and analysis of field usage/diagnostics data.
+ Lead Root Cause Analysis for complex system failures, supporting fast-response containment and recurrence prevention.

* Regulatory, Certification & Manufacturing Support

+ Lead the strategy and execution for regulatory compliance and certification testing (e.g., UL, IEC).
+ Manage customer certification and accreditation processes to ensure project "bankability" and customer confidence.
+ Provide technical leadership for End of Line and Factory Acceptance Testing processes to ensure production units meet all requirements before shipment.

You'll have...
 
 

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.
* 10+ years of experience in Quality Assurance, Systems Engineering, or Product Development within the energy or automotive sectors.
* 3+ years of leadership experience managing engineering teams.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional issue resolution and communicate complex technical quality risks to executive-level stakeholders.
* Expertise in Failure Mode Avoidance tools (DFMEA, PFMEA).
* Deep understanding of high-voltage battery systems or power electronics.
* Experience managing the "Cost of Quality" and warranty analytics for large-scale industrial or automotive programs.
* Direct experience with global supplier quality or managing quality standards for technology licensing agreements.
* Direct experience with stationary Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).
* Black Belt or Master Black Belt certification in Six Sigma or equivalent methodologies.

Even better, you may have...
 
 

* Master’s degree in Engineering or an MBA.
* Experience with grid-scale certification standards (UL, IEC, NFPA).
* Leadership Attributes

+ Strategic Culture Builder who sets the tone for technical excellence and accountability across the organization.
+ Executive-level communicator capable of translating technical quality risks into business and financial impacts.
+ Operationally strong leader capable of scaling a quality organization in a fast-paced startup environment.
+ Technical visionary with a "Safety-First" mindset who prioritizes long-term asset performance.

* Location & Travel

+ Flexible Location: This position is hybrid-friendly for candidates with a proven ability to deliver results outside of a traditional office environment.
+ Travel Expectations: This role may require travel to manufacturing sites, supplier locations, and customer installations to ensure quality standards are met.

You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!
 
 
This position is leadership level 5 and ranges from $141,700-268,300.
 
 
Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value.
 
 
For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/LL5FE
 
 
**Company: As Ford establishes a wholly owned subsidiary focused on Battery Energy Storage Systems, this role will initially be employed by Ford and is expected to transition to the subsidiary within one year.**
Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
 
 
This position is hybrid. Candidates who are in commuting distance to a Ford hub location may be required to be onsite four or more days per week.
 
 
Candidates for positions with Ford Motor Company must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire.
 
 
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, age, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status or protected veteran status. In the United States, if you need a reasonable accommodation for the online application process due to a disability, please call 1-888-336-0660.

records.description:
**Company And Opportunity Overview**
WNA’s vision is to be a leading entrepreneurial player in terms of market share, agility, and game-changing solutions. WNA is a solution provider, creating value along the supply chain of our customers, from online purchase to their customers.
 
 
WNA is headquartered in the Charlotte Metro Area, North Carolina. With around 500 employees and ~$200M of sales, WNA focuses on the retail and distribution market segments with marquee customers such as Walmart, Amazon, and the majority of large grocers and retailers.
 
 
In addition to being the largest manufacturer of shopping carts in North America, WNA has three additional main product segments as well as a Service business, providing turnkey solutions for customer guidance (Access Systems), Shelving & Fixtures, and Material Handling products.
 
 
Access Solutions provides sophisticated customer guidance and loss prevention systems for major retailers. With German-engineered products and a strong installed base, this segment focuses on protecting existing market share while expanding into adjacent opportunities in smart retail, autonomous store technology, and digital integration.
 
 
Additionally, WNA offers a range of digital solutions integrated into our products, including advanced shopping cart containment systems, smart exit gate technology, and innovations for autonomous and semi-autonomous retail stores. We are continuously expanding and enhancing our digital offerings to meet evolving customer needs and drive industry advancement.
 
 
WNA is part of the Wanzl Group, headquartered in Germany, and has 12 plants in 8 countries, providing comprehensive, solutions-driven service and expert knowledge of local markets for customers across the globe through their 360° service.
 
 
**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Manage a team of 5-10 Engineers, CAD Designers, & Engineering Technicians
* Drive LEAN implementation / LEAN transformation.
* Recommend and manage capital projects from concept through appropriation process, to project management and implementation for current production improvement.
* Select, develop, and train the Manufacturing Engineering Team
* Provide needed technical support and lead shop floor problem solving using world-class problem-solving methodologies.
* Create and maintain shop floor layouts, fostering material flow optimization.
* Creating and maintaining Manufacturing BOMs and Routings in ERP system
* Support Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) driven by R&D
* Support Industrialization in developing & implementing new production methods/processes.
* Process Capability Studies
* Standard Work Analysis, for both Direct and Indirect Labor
* Create test protocols, document and track results.
* Support for Operations, support for Tooling and Maintenance, Look for Efficiency Projects to increase Capacity, OEE, Reduce costs (Labor, Material, OH, etc.) and drive projects in consequence, review PMs, Cycle Times analysis, Downtime analysis.
* Develop Set-up technicians.

**Skills And Experience**

* BS in Engineering from an accredited university
* Minimum of 5 years engineering experience in a Manufacturing Environment, Design/R&D, & demonstrated engineering project leadership experience.
* LEAN and Six Sigma training preferred.
* Experience implementing LEAN Manufacturing projects.
* Proficient in use of software - CAD (SolidWorks), MS Project, MS Office, etc.
* Strong problem solving / analytical skills including identifying potential problems and developing effective solutions.
* Demonstrated Leadership skills.
* Minimal travel

postedPay.title: JASSM Production Chief Engineer Sr. Manager

records.description:
**Standard Job Description**
This position is for a Chief Engineering Sr. Manager for the JASSM program in the Strike Systems program area. The successful candidate will report to the JASSM Program Chief Engineer programmatically and lead the Engineering & Technology (E&T) team supporting JASSM production. The candidate will work closely with the JASSM Chief Engineering staff to coordinate tasks and share lessons learned, and with other Strike Systems Chief Engineers to support cross-program collaboration.
 
 
**What You Will Be Doing**
As the JASSM Production Chief Engineer, you will be responsible for:
 
 

* Leading the E&T team supporting JASSM production, working with suppliers and factories to sustain production operations and meet program and corporate milestones.
* Providing Technical and Programmatic leadership/oversight on production rate increases in support of both USG and FMS customers.
* Providing leadership and oversight for transition to production of new JASSM variants and second source suppliers.
* Developing a productive partnership and trusting relationship with the JPO customer through effective communication and collaboration.
* Partnering with Program Management, Production Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality to communicate engineering assessments and align engineering priorities with program needs.
* Guiding Engineering team, IPT leads and cross-functional teams in program planning, scheduling, trade studies, design concepts, verification, and critical life cycle reviews.
* Ensuring program staffing is appropriate from an E&T perspective.
* Collaborating with Engineering Excellence management to ensure program milestones are successfully completed.
* Supporting and leading program technical reviews and participating in monthly E&T meetings, staff meetings, and other critical program activities.
* Sharing lessons learned and coordinating tasks with the entire Chief Engineer staff

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide technical leadership for production execution, transition to production, and supporting proposal activities.
* Protect system integrity and reliability while supporting opportunities to improve production efficiency and reduce cost.
* Develop and execute engineering plans, schedules, and trade study analyses that support production commitments.
* Lead or support customer briefings, weekly IPT status updates, Technical Interchange Meetings, Technical Readiness Reviews, and other critical program reviews.
* Lead technical investigations with urgency, communicate results to program leadership and the customer, and participate in Failure Review Boards, Risk Management, and Mission Success Reviews.
* Support technical reviews internally, with the customer, and external stakeholders, and at supplier locations.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Have a minimum of a bachelor’s degree in engineering from an accredited college or university, with existing professional experience.
* Experience and demonstrated skill set with missile systems design, development, and production support.
* Must possess ability to plan and lead the technical teams/efforts associated with Complex Missile Systems.
* Candidate will be required to communicate technical status and issues internally to program leadership, technical leadership and functional leadership as well as externally to the USG customer.
* Must be available for occasional domestic travel.
* Candidate must have a Secret clearance..

**Desired Skills**

* An advanced degree in engineering from an accredited college or university is desired.
* Prior experience at Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control is highly desired.
* Candidate should have wide experience/familiarity in collaborating with the Engineering & Technology functional organization.
* Ability to interface with the USG Customer office and global supply base.
* Ability to support technical reviews internally, with the customer, and external stakeholders, and at supplier locations.
* Experience in leading Failure Analysis and Failure Review Boards.
* Experience leading technical teams through major proposal efforts.

**Pay Information**
Full-Time Salary Range: $182500.00 - $338900.00
 
 
At Lockheed Martin, we know mission success starts with taking care of our people. Our Total Rewards program is designed to attract top talent, support your well-being, and help you grow—both professionally and personally.
 
 
The salary range for this position is as listed on the requisition. Please note that the salary information listed is a general guideline only. Lockheed Martin considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/ training, key skills as well as market(work location) and business considerations when extending an offer.
 
 
**Benefits offered:**
Medical, Dental, Vision, Flexible work arrangements and schedules (e.g., 4x10), 401(k) match, Paid time off, Holidays, Parental Leave, EAP, Flexible Spending Accounts, Education Assistance, Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, and Long-Term Disability.
 
 

* Annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs may be offered depending on the position. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and can vary from year to year and are tied to a range of performance metrics.
* For (Washington state applicants only) Non-represented full-time employees: accrue at least 10 hours per month of Paid Time Off (PTO) to be used for incidental absences and other reasons; receive at least 90 hours for holidays. Represented full time employees accrue 6.67 hours of Vacation per month; accrue up to 52 hours of sick leave annually; receive at least 96 hours for holidays. PTO, Vacation, sick leave, and holiday hours are prorated based on start date during the calendar year.

records.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
records.description:
Work Model: This role can be performed remotely from an approved location, with flexibility based on business needs and applicable requirements.
 
 
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
 
 
Regal Rexnord Business System (“RBS”) plays a pivotal role in driving organizational change and process improvement to achieve our business objectives. The
**Linear Motion Division**
(“LMD”) within the AMC segment is seeking a
**Director of RBS**
. Reporting to the President of the Division, this position will drive the implementation, maturity, and cultural adoption of RBS and continuous process improvement across the division.
 
 
This leadership position is focused on the deployment of RBS across the Division to drive both short and long-term goals and will partner closely with LMD’s leadership team, as well as the AMC RBS team. The right candidate will drive operational excellence, develop CI capability, and ensure alignment to strategic priorities through Policy Deployment. This leader influences across manufacturing sites, functional teams, and the broader AMC organization to deliver year-over-year performance improvement. As a key member of the AMC RBS Team, this role will impact results and culture by establishing standards, institutionalizing management systems and ensuring effective problem-solving skills (& tool capability) across the organization.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
**Continuous Improvement Leadership and Standard Work**

* Champion the Lean philosophy and its deployment across all functions and manufacturing sites.
* Support the organization in achieving SQDCG and financial objectives through effective application of the RBS tools and methodologies to achieve continuous improvement.
* Develop and drive the divisional CI Roadmap and ensure alignment to site-level plans.
* Lead, guide, and help create solutions for highly complex and multi-faceted problems requiring ingenuity, creativity, innovation, and strong analytical skills. Problems are unique and require a thorough understanding of operating unit policies and practices. Apply knowledge of different techniques and practices to achieve desired results
* Connect operational improvements (e.g., machine productivity, labor productivity, lead time/turnaround time, quality, backlog, capacity, OEE, etc.) to financial outcomes (Revenue/TVOS, Cost, Cash, Margin).
* Participate in the hiring, development and coaching of site continuous improvement leaders.
* Utilize a team-oriented structured problem-solving approach to analyze current conditions, diagnose problems, and identify improvement opportunities.

**Capability and Talent Development**

* Support Division and Site RBS leaders in maturing the Regal Rexnord Business System through the development of skills, capabilities, and engagement driving impact to the next level.
* Coach, mentor, and train Regal Rexnord associates on CI tools and Lean leadership.
* Develop RBS capability through formal training and “stop-and-teach” coaching at Gemba.
* Lead and coach multiple projects and Kaizen events simultaneously through both a hands-on and influential approach.
* Engage and influence teams at all levels to drive momentum toward the future state.
* Identify, coach, and develop talent; build a strong bench of RBS tool champions across the division to leverage RBS Continuous Improvement tools and methodologies to support their professional advancement and improve the business's operational performance.

**Policy Deployment**

* Lead the creation of annual X-Matrix and oversee the deployment plan via RBS charters, bowlers, and action plans.
* Manage charters, bowlers, action plans and monthly PD cadence.
* Support Division Annual Improvement Priorities through effective application of RBS tools and methodologies to support Policy Deployment initiatives.

**Qualifications**
**PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE/QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in a technical field; Advanced degree preferred (MS Engineering, MBA)
* 8-10 years relevant work experience across Continuous Improvement, Business Systems, or Operations (global and/or multi-site experience preferred)
* Familiarity with Policy Deployment, its facilitation and implementation.
* Technical background in continuous improvement methodology and framework
* Proven successful applications of multiple CI tools: 80/20, Lean Leadership, including Daily Management, KPI Leadership, Standard Work, Gemba Walks, Value Stream Mapping, 6S, Transactional Process Improvements, Kanban/replenishment systems, FMEA, Advanced Problem Solving, RCCMs
* Demonstrated ability to facilitate Kaizen-type events to produce measurable improvements (financial, service, quality, etc.)
* Skilled and experienced in decomposing a strategic vision into actionable strategies and tactics.
* Critical thinking skills to properly identify problem area & potential solutions
* Demonstrate the Regal Rexnord Values; Integrity, Responsibility, Diversity, Engagement & Inclusion, Customer Success, Innovation with Purpose, Continuous Improvement, Performance, Passion to Win, and Sense of Urgency
* Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently.
* Must be able to travel at least 50-75% of the time domestically and internationally as required

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Project and program management expertise (PMP, Prince II)
* Lean Six Sigma certification (e.g, Green Belt or Black Belt)
* Experience with High Mix / Low Volume and Low Mix / High Volume manufacturing

Physical Demand and Work Environment
 
 
**Physical Demands**
– while performing the duties in this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands; reach with hands and arms; and talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to stand, walk, and sit.
 
 
**Work Environment**
– the noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
 
 
Restrictions imposed by federal export control laws may limit this job opportunity to candidates who are a "U.S. Person,' which includes U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, U.S. permanent residents, individuals granted asylum in the United States, and refugees in the United States.
 
 
Expected salary: $160,000 - $190,000 annually. The salary range provided is intended to display the value of the company's base pay compensation for all statewide locations across the United States. Salary is dependent on a multitude of factors, including but not limited to the physical worksite location, candidate's skill set, level of experience, education, and internal peer compensation comparisons.
 
 
**Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, Vision and Prescription Drug Coverage
* Spending accounts (HSA, Health Care FSA and Dependent Care FSA)
* Paid Time Off and Holidays
* 401k Retirement Plan with Matching Employer Contributions
* Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance
* Paid Leaves
* Tuition Assistance

**About Regal Rexnord**
Regal Rexnord is a publicly held global industrial manufacturer with 30,000 associates around the world who help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.
 
 
The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture.
 
 
Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. records.title: PEPI: Director, Operations & Manufacturing (OPEN TO ALL U.S. LOCATIONS)
records.description:
**Description**
**Alvarez & Marsal Private Equity Performance Improvement**
**Director: Operations & Manufacturing**
**(OPEN TO ALL U.S. LOCATIONS)**
**About Alvarez & Marsal**
Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 13,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M.
 
 
**The Team**
A&M’s Private Equity Performance Improvement Services (PEPI) practice, with offices throughout the US, focuses on serving the middle market and large cap private equity firms who have engaged A&M to help improve operating results at their portfolio companies.
 
 
Our professionals are aligned with a PEPI service line to promote the development of deep functional skills & experiences and to maximize our ability to tailor solutions to solve our clients' business issues.
 
 
We bring a structured and disciplined approach to create and capture value. We provide private equity clients with a broad continuum of knowledge and tools for cost improvements, transformations, mergers, acquisitions, and carve-outs.
 
 
A&M’s Operations professionals assist our clients in analyzing
**manufacturing operations**
, supply chain and distribution channels, procurement, SG&A operations, and sales force effectiveness for potential value creation opportunities and help drive them during our client’s ownership. From our thorough fact-based analysis, we assess the state of operations, identify key risks to investment and quantify potential EBITDA improvement plans for the buyer and seller.
 
 
The PEPI Operations group is a growing business targeting high growth in the next two to four years. We offer excellent opportunities for career advancement and leadership skills. The leadership team is focused on providing development opportunities, training, and exposure to international business assignments.
 
 
**How You Will Contribute**
We are seeking individuals that can lead and deliver large, complex client engagements, working closely with PE leadership to identify, design, and implement creative business solutions for their portfolio companies. Directors frequently lead the following types of engagements:
 
 

* Gain a comprehensive understanding of a target’s manufacturing and distribution operations-- organization design, production capacity, efficiency, quality, planning, warehousing and team capability
* Evaluate the maintainability and operability of production facilities
* Review current and historical data to understand efficiency & capacity, including equipment conditions, maintenance logs, spare parts and detailed production numbers
* Provide shop floor insights by talking with employees and customers and reviewing all available data
* Identify potential cost improvement opportunities through lean improvements, outsourcing or consolidation of facilities
* Develop transformation plans to drive proposed changes and identify key risks and mitigation strategies
* Implement and oversee the quality of deliverables and effectively manage the team and day-to-day relationships to ensure exceptional performance.

**Qualifications**

* 10-15 plus years of combined professional industry and consulting experience, with a minimum of 4 years specializing in manufacturing and/or distribution functions
* Previous advisory experience from a top-tier strategy firm, leading specialist, niche advisory firm, or Big-4 consultancy REQUIRED
* Travel-- This role requires significant client-site presence, with travel up to 80% of the time — generally Monday through Thursday or Friday, including overnight stays. Candidates should be comfortable with a consulting travel lifestyle.
* Experience working for or with private equity sponsors and portfolio companies. Deep functional expertise in one of more of the following areas:
* Supply Chain Operations
* Manufacturing Operations, SI&OP
* Footprint optimization, plant consolidation and product line transfer
* Manufacturing strategy, CapEx planning, Manufacturing 4.0/IIoT
* Lean, Six Sigma, TOC and Value Engineering
* Demonstrated track record working with C-suite executives as well as private equity deal and operating partners
* Excellent fact-gathering and analytical skills, including business process mapping and quantitative analysis
* Specific experience designing and leading the execution of internally-focused and externally-focused change/communications strategy.
* Excellent fact-gathering and analytical skills, including business process mapping and quantitative analysis
* Previous strategy and change management experience.
* Bachelor's degree required; MBA a plus

**Your journey at A&M**
We recognize that our people are the driving force behind our success, which is why we prioritize an employee experience that fosters each person’s unique professional and personal development. Our robust performance development process promotes continuous learning, rewards your contributions, and fosters a culture of meritocracy. With top-notch training and on-the-job learning opportunities, you can acquire new skills and advance your career.
 
 
We prioritize your well-being, providing benefits and resources to support you on your personal journey. Our people consistently highlight the growth opportunities, our unique, entrepreneurial culture, and the fun we have together as their favorite aspects of working at A&M. The possibilities are endless for high-performing and passionate professionals.
 
 
The salary range is $150,000--$225,000 annually, dependent on several variables including but not limited to education, experience, skills, and geography. In addition, A&M offers a discretionary bonus program which is based on a number of factors, including individual and firm performance. Please ask your recruiter for details.
 
 
Alvarez & Marsal recruits on an ongoing basis. Candidates are considered as they apply, until the opportunity is filled. Candidates are encouraged to apply expeditiously to any role(s) that they are qualified for and that are of interest to them.
 
 
Full-time Positions and Part-time Positions Over 30 hours
 
 
Regular employees working 30 or more hours per week are also entitled to participate in Alvarez & Marsal Holdings’ fringe benefits consisting of healthcare plans, flexible spending and savings accounts, life, AD&D, and disability coverages at rates determined from time to time as well as a 401(k)-retirement plan. Provided the eligibility requirements are met, employees will also receive a discretionary contribution to their 401(k) from Alvarez & Marsal. Additionally, employees are eligible for paid time off including vacation, personal days, seventy-two (72) hours of sick time (prorated for part time employees), ten federal holidays, one floating holiday, and parental leave. The amount of vacation and personal days available varies based on tenure and role type. Click here for more information regarding A&M’s benefits programs.
 
 
A&M does not require or administer lie detector tests as a condition of employment or continued employment. It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.

records.title: Director, Industrial Engineering
records.description:
**Who We Are**
Applied Materials is a global leader in materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every new chip and advanced display in the world. We design, build and service cutting-edge equipment that helps our customers manufacture display and semiconductor chips – the brains of devices we use every day. As the foundation of the global electronics industry, Applied enables the exciting technologies that literally connect our world – like AI and IoT. If you want to push the boundaries of materials science and engineering to create next generation technology, join us to deliver material innovation that changes the world.
 
 
**What We Offer**
Salary:
 
 
$168,000.00 - $231,000.00
 
 
Location:
 
 
Santa Clara,CA
 
 
You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.
 
 
At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.
 
 
**What You'll Do**
Be a part of internal consulting team with high visibility to Applied Global Services executive leadership. Lead strategic projects to streamline business processes, improve supply chain and operations, reduce costs, and improve business performance through advanced analytics. Have responsibility for complete project life cycle starting with analysis of the as-is process, identification and quantification of the opportunities, development of improvement streams, securing buy-in from stakeholders, and driving implementation.
 
 
High impact role that requires relentless change management motivation rewarded with material impact to business unit performance.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Structure and break down complex business problems, develop hypothesis, drive analysis and deliver data-driven recommendations
* Lead thoughtful and rigorous analysis across large data sets and synthesize insights and opportunities
* Develop and present high-quality recommendation and deliverables for executive level consumption and contribute to associated strategy and execution discussions
* Work collaboratively across a cross-functional set of stakeholders to gather the right information, pressure test your hypothesis, co-create deliverables, accelerate execution and unlock value
* Optimize operations and business process to improve performance, reduce cycle time, and shrink costs

**Qualifications**

* Industrial Engineering or equivalent Bachelor degree. MBA preferred
* 10+ years relevant work experience
* Semiconductor experience preferred
* Management consulting experience preferred
* Broad understanding and experience including logistics, financial reporting, operations, and service business management.
* Strong analytical skills – able to extract real insight from multiple data sources
* Excellent oral and written communication, organizational, analytical, and interpersonal skills
* Able to work effectively in a matrix environment and influence others
* Detail oriented, able to connect the dots and communicate complex ideas effectively
* Knowledge of Lean / Six Sigma

**Additional Information**
**Time Type:**
Full time
 
 
**Employee Type:**
Assignee / Regular
 
 
**Travel:**
Yes, 10% of the Time
 
 
**Relocation Eligible:**
Yes
 
 
The salary offered to a selected candidate will be based on multiple factors including location, hire grade, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and with consideration of internal equity of our current team members. In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, candidates may be eligible for other forms of compensation such as participation in a bonus and a stock award program, as applicable.
 
 
For all sales roles, the posted salary range is the Target Total Cash (TTC) range for the role, which is the sum of base salary and target bonus amount at 100% goal achievement.
 
 
Applied Materials is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law.
 
 
In addition, Applied endeavors to make our careers site accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process, please contact us via e-mail at Accommodations\_Program@amat.com, or by calling our HR Direct Help Line at 877-612-7547, option 1, and following the prompts to speak to an HR Advisor. This contact is for accommodation requests only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications.
